docs.title: Divisibility of alpha values
docs.text:
ZInQ.AlphaPower.alphaZ_dvd_alphaZ_iff ZInQ.AlphaPower.alphaZ_sq_dvd_alphaZ_iff

Let \(b>2\) be a natural number and \(U_n=\alpha_b(n)\).

  1. For \(k>0\) and every \(m\in\mathbb N\): \(U_k\mid U_m\iff k\mid m\).
  2. (Equation (C.1)) For every \(k\in\mathbb N\) and every \(m>0\): $\(U_k^2\mid U_m\iff kU_k\mid m .\)$ For \(k=0\) both sides are false.

Divisibility is in \(\mathbb Z\); all values involved are natural by the growth lemma.

Proof sketch. (1) Reducing \(M^k\) modulo \(U_k\) gives the scalar matrix \(U_{k+1}I\) up to the entry \(-U_{k-1}\equiv U_{k+1}\) (from the recurrence \(U_{k+1}+U_{k-1}=bU_k\)), which is invertible modulo \(U_k\) by coprimality of adjacent terms. Equivalently, by the addition formula \(U_{k+n}=U_{k}U_{n+1}-U_{k-1}U_n\), so \(U_k\mid U_{k+n}\iff U_k\mid U_n\) (as \(\gcd(U_k,U_{k-1})=1\)). Removing periods of length \(k\) reduces to \(m<k\), where \(0\le U_m<U_k\) by strict growth, so \(U_k\mid U_m\) iff \(U_m=0\) iff \(m=0\). (2) For \(k=0\): \(U_0^2=0\) divides \(U_m\ge m>0\) never, and \(0\mid m\) never. For \(k>0\), both sides imply \(k\mid m\) (the left by (1) since \(U_k\mid U_m\)); write \(m=kq\) with \(q\ge1\). From \(M^k\equiv U_kM-U_{k-1}I\) entrywise (the recurrence gives \(M^k=U_kM-U_{k-1}I\) exactly), $\(M^{kq}=(U_kM-U_{k-1}I)^q\equiv(-U_{k-1})^qI+qU_k(-U_{k-1})^{q-1}M\pmod{U_k^2},\)$ whose lower-left entry gives \(U_m\equiv qU_k(-U_{k-1})^{q-1}\pmod{U_k^2}\). Since \(\gcd(U_k,U_{k-1})=1\), \(U_k^2\mid U_m\iff U_k\mid q\iff kU_k\mid kq=m\); this includes \(U_k=1\).

docs.title: Period and reflection modulo the companion
docs.text:
ZInQ.AlphaPower.alphaZ_period ZInQ.AlphaPower.alphaZ_reflection ZInQ.AlphaPower.alphaZ_folded_residue ZInQ.AlphaPower.two_mul_alphaZ_lt_companion'

Let \(b>2\) be a natural number, \(U_n=\alpha_b(n)\), \(m>0\), and put $\(v=U_{m+1}-U_{m-1}=\operatorname{tr}(M_b^m)=bU_m-2U_{m-1}.\)$

  1. (Folding) Every \(n\in\mathbb N\) can be written as \(n=2lm+j\), or as \(n=2lm-j\) with \(0<j<2lm\), for some \(l\in\mathbb N\) and \(0\le j\le m\).
  2. (Period and reflection) For all \(l,j\in\mathbb N\), $\(U_{j+2lm}\equiv(-1)^lU_j\pmod v,\qquad U_{2lm-j}\equiv-(-1)^lU_j\pmod v\ \ (0<j<2lm).\)$ Consequently, for \(n\) folded as in item 1, \(U_n\equiv\pm U_j\pmod v\).
  3. (Bounds) If \(b>3\) then \(2U_j<v\) for every \(0\le j\le m\); in particular \(v>2U_m\).

The value sign in item 2 need not equal the index sign. In the manuscript's notation, \(n=2lm+\varepsilon j\) with \(\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}\) and \(U_n\equiv(-1)^l\varepsilon U_j\).

Proof sketch. (1) Take \(l\) with \(2lm\le n<2(l+1)m\) and fold to the nearer of \(2lm\) and \(2(l+1)m\). (2) \(M^m\) has determinant \(1\) and trace \(v\), so by Cayley-Hamilton \(M^{2m}=vM^m-I\equiv-I\pmod v\), hence \(M^{2lm}\equiv(-1)^lI\). The lower-left entry of \(M^{j+2lm}=M^jM^{2lm}\) gives the period congruence. For the reflection, the lower-left entry of \(M^{2lm}M^{-j}\), where \(M^{-j}\) is the inverse matrix (entries in \(\mathbb Z\) since \(\det M=1\)), equals \(U_{2lm-j}\) and is congruent to \((-1)^l\cdot(-U_j)\). In terms of the recurrence alone: the identity \(U_{n+2m}+U_n=vU_{n+m}\) (the addition formula) gives the period, and \(U_{N-j}=U_N(-U_{j-1})+(-U_{N-1})(-U_j)\) with \(N=2lm\), \(U_N\equiv0\), \(U_{N-1}\equiv-(-1)^l\), gives the reflection. (3) For \(j\le m\), \(2U_j\le2U_m\), and \(v-2U_m=(b-2)U_m-2U_{m-1}\ge2(U_m-U_{m-1})>0\) when \(b\ge4\), using strict growth.

docs.title: Odd alpha values are unbounded
docs.text:
ZInQ.AlphaPower.alphaZ_large_odd

Let \(b>3\) and \(a\in\mathbb N\). There is \(k>0\) such that \(u=\alpha_b(k)\) is odd and \(u>2a\); moreover \(t=\alpha_b(k+1)\) satisfies \(u<t\) and \(u^2+t^2=1+but\).

Proof sketch. Of the adjacent terms \(\alpha_b(2a+1)\) and \(\alpha_b(2a+2)\) at least one is odd (adjacent terms are not both even), and both exceed \(2a\) since \(\alpha_b(n)\ge n\). Take \(k\) the corresponding index. The last two claims are strict growth and the quadratic identity.

docs.title: The alpha formula
docs.text:
ZInQ.AlphaPower.AlphaEqns

For natural numbers \(X,b,N\), the alpha formula \(\mathrm{Alpha}(X,b,N)\) is the statement that there are natural numbers \(r,s,t,u,v,w,x,y\) satisfying the fifteen conditions (C.2): $\(\begin{gathered} b>3,\quad u^2+t^2=1+but,\quad s^2+r^2=1+bsr,\quad r<s,\quad u^2\mid s,\quad v+2r=bs,\\ w\equiv b\pmod v,\quad w\equiv2\pmod u,\quad w>2,\quad x^2+y^2=1+wxy,\\ 2X<u,\quad 2X<v,\quad x\equiv X\pmod v,\quad 2N<u,\quad x\equiv N\pmod u . \end{gathered}\)$ Here \(p\equiv q\pmod M\) means \(p\bmod M=q\bmod M\) for natural numbers (so for \(M=0\) it means \(p=q\)), and \(p\mid q\) is divisibility in \(\mathbb N\).

The compiler emits this system as the alpha macro: each strict inequality, divisibility and congruence is replaced by an equation with fresh natural witnesses (see the equational gadgets), and the macro introduces its eight witnesses in the order \(r,s,t,u,v,w,x,y\). The conditions are exactly those of Exp_Matrices.alpha_equations in the AFP development, with \(a=X\) and \(c=N\); equation order and the orientation of each equality are immaterial.

This is a definition.

docs.title: Soundness of the alpha formula
docs.text:
ZInQ.AlphaPower.alphaEqns_sound

For all natural numbers \(X,b,N\): if \(\mathrm{Alpha}(X,b,N)\) holds then \(b>3\) and \(X=\alpha_b(N)\).

Proof sketch. Fix witnesses \(r,s,t,u,v,w,x,y\).

  1. Shapes. From \(u^2+t^2=1+but\) and \(b>2\), \(u=\alpha_b(k)\) for some \(k\) (unordered Pell classification); \(u>2X\ge0\) gives \(u\ge1\), hence \(k>0\). From \(s^2+r^2=1+bsr\) with \(r<s\), \((r,s)=(\alpha_b(m-1),\alpha_b(m))\) with \(m>0\) (ordered classification). From \(x^2+y^2=1+wxy\) and \(w>2\), \(x=\alpha_w(n)\) for some \(n\in\mathbb N\).
  2. \(u\mid m\). \(u^2\mid s\) is \(\alpha_b(k)^2\mid\alpha_b(m)\) with \(m>0\); by (C.1) \(k\,\alpha_b(k)\mid m\), so \(u\mid m\).
  3. Residues. \(v+2r=bs\) identifies \(v=\alpha_b(m+1)-\alpha_b(m-1)\) (the companion). Parameter congruence with \(w\equiv b\pmod v\) gives \(x\equiv\alpha_b(n)\pmod v\); with \(w\equiv2\pmod u\) and \(\alpha_2(n)=n\) it gives \(x\equiv n\pmod u\).
  4. Recover \(X\). Fold \(n\) as \(n=2lm\pm j\) with \(0\le j\le m\). By period and reflection, \(\alpha_b(n)\equiv\pm\alpha_b(j)\pmod v\), so \(X\equiv x\equiv\pm\alpha_b(j)\pmod v\). Both \(X\) and \(\alpha_b(j)\) are nonnegative and below \(v/2\) (\(2X<v\) by hypothesis, \(2\alpha_b(j)<v\) by the companion bound for \(b>3\), \(j\le m\)), so \(v\mid X-\alpha_b(j)\) or \(v\mid X+\alpha_b(j)\) forces \(X=\alpha_b(j)\) (in the second case both are \(0\)).
  5. Recover \(N\). \(j\le\alpha_b(j)=X\), so \(2j\le2X<u\); also \(2N<u\). Since \(u\mid m\), the folded form gives \(n\equiv\pm j\pmod u\), and \(N\equiv x\equiv n\pmod u\). Two residues below \(u/2\) that agree up to sign modulo \(u\) are equal: \(N=j\). Hence \(X=\alpha_b(N)\).

The natural-subtraction case \(n=2lm-j\) requires \(0<j<2lm\), which the folding lemma supplies.

docs.title: Completeness of the alpha formula
docs.text:
ZInQ.AlphaPower.alphaEqns_complete ZInQ.AlphaPower.alphaEqns_iff

For all natural numbers \(b,N\) with \(b>3\), the formula \(\mathrm{Alpha}(\alpha_b(N),b,N)\) holds; that is, the fifteen conditions have natural witnesses with \(X=\alpha_b(N)\). This includes \(N=X=0\).

Together with soundness: for natural \(X,b,N\), \(\mathrm{Alpha}(X,b,N)\iff(b>3\wedge X=\alpha_b(N))\).

Proof sketch. Put \(X=\alpha_b(N)\in\mathbb N\).

  1. Choose \(k>0\) with \(u=\alpha_b(k)\) odd and \(u>2X\) (odd alpha values are unbounded); put \(t=\alpha_b(k+1)\), so \(u^2+t^2=1+but\).
  2. Put \(m=ku>0\), \(s=\alpha_b(m)\), \(r=\alpha_b(m-1)\); then \(r<s\) and \(s^2+r^2=1+bsr\). By (C.1), \(u^2\mid s\) because \(ku\mid m\).
  3. Put \(v=bs-2r\); then \(v\in\mathbb N\), \(v+2r=bs\) and \(v>2s\) (companion bound, \(b>3\)).
  4. Bounds. \(2X<u\) by choice; \(s=\alpha_b(m)\ge\alpha_b(k)=u\) since \(m\ge k\), so \(2X<u\le s<v\); and \(2N\le2\alpha_b(N)=2X<u\).
  5. Coprimality. \(\gcd(u,v)=1\): a common prime divisor \(p\) is odd (\(u\) is odd), divides \(s\) (as \(u\mid s\)) and hence \(2r=bs-v\), hence \(r\); but \(r,s\) are adjacent alpha values, which are coprime.
  6. CRT. With \(u,v>0\) coprime, choose \(w>2\) with \(w\equiv2\pmod u\) and \(w\equiv b\pmod v\).
  7. Put \(x=\alpha_w(N)\), \(y=\alpha_w(N+1)\) (natural since \(w\ge2\)). Then \(x^2+y^2=1+wxy\), and by parameter congruence \(x\equiv\alpha_b(N)=X\pmod v\) and \(x\equiv\alpha_2(N)=N\pmod u\).

All fifteen conditions hold.

docs.title: The power formula
docs.text:
ZInQ.AlphaPower.PowEqns

For natural numbers \(P,Q,R\), the power formula \(\mathrm{Pow}(P,Q,R)\) is the disjunction of three branches:

  1. \(Q=0\), \(R=0\) and \(P=1\);
  2. \(Q=0\), \(0<R\) and \(P=0\);
  3. \(0<Q\) and there are natural numbers \(b,m,a_0,a_1,a_2\) with (C.3) $\(\mathrm{Alpha}(a_0,Q+4,R+1),\quad b=a_0+Q^2+2,\quad m+Q^2+1=bQ,\quad P<m,\)$ $\(\mathrm{Alpha}(a_1,b,R),\quad \mathrm{Alpha}(a_2,b,R+1),\quad P+ba_1\equiv Qa_1+a_2\pmod m .\)$

The compiler's power macro introduces \(b,m,a_0,a_1,a_2\) in this order (before the witnesses of the inner macros), writes the strict inequalities \(0<R\), \(0<Q\), \(P<m\) and the congruence with the equational gadgets, and writes the three alpha formulas as alpha macros; the three branches are joined by a disjunction, each branch being a conjunction. The third branch is Exponential_Relation.exp_repr of the AFP development.

This is a definition.

docs.title: The power formula expresses exponentiation
docs.text:
ZInQ.AlphaPower.powEqns_iff

For all natural numbers \(P,Q,R\): $\(\mathrm{Pow}(P,Q,R)\iff P=Q^R,\)$ with \(0^0=1\). This includes \(R=0\), \(Q=1\) and the base \(Q=0\).

Proof sketch. If \(Q=0\) the third branch is excluded and the first two say exactly \(P=0^R\). Let \(Q\ge1\); only the third branch can hold.

Forward. By alpha soundness, \(a_0=\alpha_{Q+4}(R+1)\); then \(b=a_0+Q^2+2\ge4\), so the two other alpha formulas give \(a_1=\alpha_b(R)\), \(a_2=\alpha_b(R+1)\). By growth, \(a_0\ge(Q+3)^R\), and therefore \(m=bQ-Q^2-1=(a_0+Q^2+2)Q-Q^2-1>Q^R\), so \(m>0\). Put \(U=\alpha_b\) and \(E_R=QU_R-bU_R+U_{R+1}\). Then \(E_0=1\) and, by the recurrence, \(E_{R+1}-Q^{R+1}=Q(E_R-Q^R)+(bQ-Q^2-1)U_R\), so \(m\mid E_R-Q^R\) for every \(R\) (as integers; this needs no sign or size hypothesis). The congruence \(P+ba_1\equiv Qa_1+a_2\pmod m\) says \(P\equiv E_R\equiv Q^R\pmod m\); since \(0\le P<m\) and \(0\le Q^R<m\), \(P=Q^R\).

Backward. Given \(P=Q^R\) with \(Q\ge1\), take \(a_0=\alpha_{Q+4}(R+1)\), \(b=a_0+Q^2+2\), \(m=bQ-Q^2-1\) (natural, and \(m>Q^R=P\)), \(a_1=\alpha_b(R)\), \(a_2=\alpha_b(R+1)\); alpha completeness supplies the three alpha formulas (\(Q+4>3\), \(b>3\)), and the congruence holds by the divisibility above (in natural numbers, \(P+ba_1\) and \(Qa_1+a_2\) have equal remainders modulo \(m\) because \(Qa_1+a_2-ba_1=E_R\) is congruent to \(P\)).

docs.title: Binomial coefficients as base-B digits
docs.text:
ZInQ.binomial_digit_iff_choose

For natural numbers \(C,N,K\) the following are equivalent:

  1. there are natural numbers \(\beta,\tau,\pi,q,r\) with $\(\beta=2^{N+1},\quad\tau=(\beta+1)^N,\quad\pi=\beta^K,\quad C<\beta,\quad r<\pi,\quad \tau=\pi(\beta q+C)+r;\)$
  2. \(C=\binom NK\) (with \(\binom NK=0\) for \(K>N\)).

In particular, with \(\beta=2^{N+1}\), the \(K\)-th base-\(\beta\) digit of \((1+\beta)^N\) is \(\binom NK\), including the cases \(N=0\), \(K=0\) and \(K>N\). In the compiler the three powers are power macros and the witnesses are introduced in the order \(\beta,\tau,\pi,q,r\) (binomial_base, binomial_total, binomial_place, binomial_quotient, binomial_remainder).

Proof sketch. Each \(\binom Nj\le2^N<\beta\), so the binomial theorem \((1+\beta)^N=\sum_{j\le N}\binom Nj\beta^j\) is the base-\(\beta\) expansion of \(\tau\), with digit \(\binom NK\) at place \(K\) (zero for \(K>N\)). For positive \(\beta\) and \(\pi\), the existence of \(q,r\) with \(C<\beta\), \(r<\pi\) and \(\tau=\pi(\beta q+C)+r\) is equivalent to \(C=\lfloor\tau/\pi\rfloor\bmod\beta\) (uniqueness of division with remainder, twice). Hence \(C\) is the digit at place \(K\).

docs.title: Lucas's criterion for bit inclusion and disjointness
docs.text:
ZInQ.lucas_choose_odd_iff_masked ZInQ.lucas_choose_add_odd_iff_disjoint

For natural numbers \(a,b\) write \(a\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}b\) for the bitwise conjunction of their binary expansions, and say \(a\) is masked by \(b\) when \(a\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}b=a\) (every set bit of \(a\) is set in \(b\)). Then:

  1. \(\binom ba\) is odd if and only if \(a\) is masked by \(b\);
  2. \(\binom{a+b}a\) is odd if and only if \(a\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}b=0\).

Proof sketch. (1) Lucas's theorem at the prime \(2\): \(\binom ba\equiv\binom{b\bmod2}{a\bmod2}\binom{\lfloor b/2\rfloor}{\lfloor a/2\rfloor}\pmod2\), and \(\binom{\beta}{\alpha}\) for bits \(\alpha,\beta\) is \(0\) exactly when \(\alpha=1,\beta=0\); induct on \(b\). Equivalently, \((1+t)^b=\prod_{i:\,\mathrm{bit}_i(b)=1}(1+t^{2^i})\) over \(\mathbb F_2\). (2) By (1) it suffices that \(a\) is masked by \(a+b\) iff \(a\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}b=0\). If the bits are disjoint the addition has no carries and \(a+b=a\mathbin{\mathrm{OR}}b\). Otherwise, at the least position where both \(a\) and \(b\) have a set bit there is no incoming carry (below it at most one summand has each bit set, so no carry is generated), so that bit of \(a+b\) is \(0\) while the bit of \(a\) is \(1\).

docs.title: The bitwise AND gadget
docs.text:
ZInQ.bitAnd_gadget_iff ZInQ.bitAnd_macro_iff

For natural numbers \(z,x,y\) the following are equivalent:

  1. there are natural numbers \(a,b\) with \(x=z+a\), \(y=z+b\) and \(z\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}a=z\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}b=a\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}b=0\);
  2. \(z=x\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}y\).

In the compiler, each of the three disjointness conditions is the orthogonality macro (\(\binom{p+q}p\) odd, through the binomial-digit gadget and an odd-witness equation), and the witnesses are introduced in the order \(a,b\) (and_left_only, and_right_only).

Proof sketch. (1)\(\Rightarrow\)(2): disjointness makes the additions carry-free, so \(x=z\mathbin{\mathrm{OR}}a\) and \(y=z\mathbin{\mathrm{OR}}b\), and with \(z,a,b\) pairwise disjoint, \((z\mathbin{\mathrm{OR}}a)\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}(z\mathbin{\mathrm{OR}}b)=z\). (2)\(\Rightarrow\)(1): take \(a=x-z\) and \(b=y-z\), the bit differences \(x\mathbin{\mathrm{AND\,NOT}}y\) and \(y\mathbin{\mathrm{AND\,NOT}}x\); they are disjoint from \(z\) and from each other.

docs.title: Natural constructions and the power interface
Natural constructions and the power interface
docs.text:
The compiler writes its conditions as formulas over integer polynomials with fresh natural witnesses: equality is a difference, conjunction a sum of squares, disjunction a product, and strict inequality, divisibility, congruence and oddness are single equations with fresh witnesses.

Over the naturals a compiled formula vanishes exactly where it holds, and the existential quantifiers over the witnesses of different conjuncts separate.

The power template is the compiled power macro: three parameters, \(79\) witnesses, \(474\) nodes. Its natural zeros are exactly the triples with \(P=Q^R\). With it, every macro means what it should.

A natural circuit denotes a polynomial, a call node denoting literal substitution into the power template on a private block; its natural relation quantifies over natural witnesses. A hierarchical construction yields a well-scoped circuit whose relation is the conjunction of its macro relations.

8 fully proved

docs.title: Natural constructions and their macros
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.NForm ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.NM ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.alpha ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.power ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.binomial ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.orthogonal ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.mask ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.bitAnd

Polynomials live in \(\mathbb Z[X_i:i\in\mathbb N]\) and formulas are those of the specification chapter: atoms \(a\doteq b\) and \(\langle f\rangle\), conjunctions and disjunctions, with the compilation \(\kappa\) (difference, sum of squares, product; empty conjunction \(0\), empty disjunction \(1\)). A formula holds naturally at \(x:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\) when it holds at the integer point \((x_i)_i\), atoms being read in \(\mathbb Z\).

Constructions. A natural construction with \(k\) inputs keeps a variable counter \(c\), initially \(k\) (the inputs are \(X_0,\dots,X_{k-1}\)), and a list of explicit variables (index and kind, the inputs first). It may

  1. take a fresh variable: record \(X_c\) as an explicit witness and increase \(c\) by one;
  2. in hierarchical mode over a fixed template \(\mathcal P\) with three parameters and \(79\) witnesses (in this chapter always the power template), call \(\mathcal P\) on polynomials \(P,Q,R\): take the block \(X_c,\dots,X_{c+78}\), increase \(c\) by \(79\), and return the atom \(\langle\mathcal P[P,Q,R;c]\rangle\) (block variables are not explicit variables).

The result of a construction is a formula \(\varphi\) and the final counter \(v\); its polynomial is \(\kappa(\varphi)\), with no further squaring, and its node list is the hash-consed node encoding of the specification chapter (an atom \(a\doteq b\) becomes \(a+(-1)\cdot b\), sums and products of lists are left-nested, the empty sum is the constant \(0\) and the empty product the constant \(1\), \(n\cdot x\) is the product node of the constant \(n\) and \(x\), \(x^2\) is the product node \(x\cdot x\), and structurally equal nodes and formulas are created once).

Gadgets and macros. Each of the following is a construction step sequence returning a formula; fresh variables are taken in the order listed, and the witnesses of inner gadgets are taken when those gadgets are created, in the order in which they occur in the formula.

  • \(\mathrm{lt}(a,b)\): fresh \(d\); the atom \(b\doteq a+1+d\).
  • \(\mathrm{divides}(a,b)\): fresh \(d\); the atom \(b\doteq a\cdot d\).
  • \(\mathrm{congruent}(a,M,b)\): fresh \(u,v\); the atom \(a+Mu\doteq b+Mv\).
  • \(\mathrm{odd}(x)\): fresh \(h\); the atom \(x\doteq2h+1\).
  • \(\mathrm{alpha}(X,b,N)\): fresh \(r,s,t,u,v,w,x,y\); the conjunction, in this order, of \(\mathrm{lt}(3,b)\), \(1+b\,u\,t\doteq u^2+t^2\), \(1+b\,s\,r\doteq s^2+r^2\), \(\mathrm{lt}(r,s)\), \(\mathrm{divides}(u^2,s)\), \(v+2r\doteq bs\), \(\mathrm{congruent}(b,v,w)\), \(\mathrm{congruent}(2,u,w)\), \(\mathrm{lt}(2,w)\), \(1+w\,x\,y\doteq x^2+y^2\), \(\mathrm{lt}(2X,u)\), \(\mathrm{lt}(2X,v)\), \(\mathrm{congruent}(x,v,X)\), \(\mathrm{lt}(2N,u)\), \(\mathrm{congruent}(x,u,N)\).
  • \(\mathrm{power}(P,Q,R)\) in flat mode: fresh \(b,m,a_0,a_1,a_2\); the disjunction of \(\bigwedge(Q\doteq0,\ R\doteq0,\ P\doteq1)\), \(\bigwedge(Q\doteq0,\ \mathrm{lt}(0,R),\ P\doteq0)\) and \(\bigwedge\bigl(\mathrm{lt}(0,Q),\ \mathrm{alpha}(a_0,Q+4,R+1),\ b\doteq a_0+Q^2+2,\ m+Q^2+1\doteq bQ,\ \mathrm{lt}(P,m),\ \mathrm{alpha}(a_1,b,R),\ \mathrm{alpha}(a_2,b,R+1),\ \mathrm{congruent}(P+ba_1,m,Qa_1+a_2)\bigr)\). In hierarchical mode, \(\mathrm{power}(P,Q,R)\) is the call of step 2.
  • \(\mathrm{binomial}(C,N,K)\): fresh \(\beta,\tau,\pi,q,r\); the conjunction of \(\mathrm{power}(\beta,2,N+1)\), \(\mathrm{power}(\tau,\beta+1,N)\), \(\mathrm{power}(\pi,\beta,K)\), \(\mathrm{lt}(C,\beta)\), \(\mathrm{lt}(r,\pi)\), \(\tau\doteq\pi(\beta q+C)+r\).
  • \(\mathrm{orthogonal}(a,b)\): fresh \(c\); \(\bigwedge(\mathrm{binomial}(c,a+b,a),\mathrm{odd}(c))\).
  • \(\mathrm{mask}(a,b)\): fresh \(c\); \(\bigwedge(\mathrm{binomial}(c,b,a),\mathrm{odd}(c))\).
  • \(\mathrm{bitAnd}(z,x,y)\): fresh \(a,b\); the conjunction of \(x\doteq z+a\), \(y\doteq z+b\), \(\mathrm{orthogonal}(z,a)\), \(\mathrm{orthogonal}(z,b)\), \(\mathrm{orthogonal}(a,b)\).

This is a definition, a transcription of the compiler's builder. The intended meanings are proved in the macro semantics; the arguments are always polynomials in variables allocated before the macro, so a macro's own variables occur only inside its formula.

docs.title: The equational gadgets over the naturals
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.lt_gadget_iff ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.dvd_gadget_iff ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.congr_gadget_iff ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.odd_gadget_iff

For all natural numbers \(a,b,M,x\):

  1. \((\exists d\in\mathbb N,\ b=a+1+d)\iff a<b\);
  2. \((\exists d\in\mathbb N,\ b=ad)\iff a\mid b\);
  3. \((\exists u,v\in\mathbb N,\ a+Mu=b+Mv)\iff a\equiv b\pmod M\), where for \(M=0\) the right side means \(a=b\);
  4. \((\exists h\in\mathbb N,\ x=2h+1)\iff x\) is odd.

There is no exception at zero modulus: for \(M=0\) the equation in item 3 says \(a=b\).

Proof sketch. Items 1, 2 and 4 are the definitions of \(<\), \(\mid\) and oddness in \(\mathbb N\). Item 3: if \(a\equiv b\pmod M\) with \(M>0\), say \(a\le b\), then \(M\mid b-a\); take \(u=(b-a)/M\), \(v=0\) (symmetrically if \(b<a\)). Conversely \(a+Mu=b+Mv\) gives \(a\bmod M=b\bmod M\). For \(M=0\) both sides say \(a=b\).

docs.title: Compilation and private witnesses over the naturals
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.compile_zv_eq_zero_iff ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.exists_agree_congr ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.callPower_spec
  1. For every formula \(\varphi\) and every \(x:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\), \(\kappa(\varphi)(x)=0\iff\varphi\) holds naturally at \(x\).
  2. Let a natural construction run from counter \(c_0\) to counter \(c_1\) and produce \(\varphi\), with all argument polynomials in variables below \(c_0\). For \(x:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\) and \(y:[c_0,c_1)\to\mathbb N\) write \(x[y]\) for the assignment equal to \(y\) on \([c_0,c_1)\) and to \(x\) elsewhere. Then the statement $\(\exists y:[c_0,c_1)\to\mathbb N,\ \ \varphi\text{ holds naturally at }x[y]\)$ depends only on \(x\) below \(c_0\). If \(\varphi=\bigwedge_i\varphi_i\) where \(\varphi_i\) is produced on the subinterval \([c_{i-1},c_i)\), it is equivalent to the conjunction of the corresponding statements for the \(\varphi_i\); if \(\varphi=\bigvee_i\varphi_i\), to their disjunction, the variables of inactive disjuncts being set to \(0\).
  3. The same holds when some atoms are power-template calls \(\langle\mathcal P[P,Q,R;w]\rangle\) with blocks inside \([c_0,c_1)\), pairwise disjoint and not occurring in any other atom or argument: the call atom may then be replaced by the statement that some values of its block make \(\mathcal P\) vanish, quantified inside its conjunct.

Proof sketch. (1) For integers, a sum of squares vanishes iff every term does and a product vanishes iff some factor does; induct on \(\varphi\) (this is the specification chapter's statement over \(\mathbb Q\) restricted to integer points). (2) Induct on the construction: atoms and fresh variables are immediate; for a conjunction the intervals of the conjuncts are disjoint, so witnesses for the conjuncts glue to one \(y\) and a common \(y\) restricts to each; for a disjunction a witness for the true disjunct is extended by \(0\) on the other intervals, which do not occur in the true disjunct. Nonemptiness of \(\mathbb N\) is what allows existential quantifiers to be pulled across the connectives. (3) is (2) with the block of each call treated as the interval of a one-atom construction.

docs.title: The power template
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.powerTemplate ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.powerTemplate_poly ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.powerTemplateCircuit_stats

The power template \(\mathcal P\) is the template obtained from the natural construction with \(3\) inputs \(P=X_0\), \(Q=X_1\), \(R=X_2\) consisting of the single flat macro \(\mathrm{power}(P,Q,R)\): it has parameter count \(3\), variable count \(82\) (so \(79\) witnesses \(X_3,\dots,X_{81}\), all explicit), and polynomial $\(\mathcal P(P,Q,R,w)=\kappa(\mathrm{power}(P,Q,R)),\)$ the product of the three branch polynomials (each a sum of squares); it is not squared again. Its witnesses are, in order: \(b,m,a_0,a_1,a_2\); the strict-difference witness of \(0<R\); that of \(0<Q\); the \(23\) witnesses of \(\mathrm{alpha}(a_0,Q+4,R+1)\) (its eight variables \(r,s,t,u,v,w,x,y\) followed by the fifteen gadget witnesses: one each for \(3<b\), \(r<s\), \(u^2\mid s\), two for each of the four congruences, one each for \(2<w\), \(2X<u\), \(2X<v\), \(2N<u\), in formula order); the witness of \(P<m\); the \(23\) witnesses of \(\mathrm{alpha}(a_1,b,R)\); the \(23\) of \(\mathrm{alpha}(a_2,b,R+1)\); the two of the final congruence. Its node list is the hash-consed node encoding of the construction; its node statistics (\(474\) nodes, constants \(0,1,4,2,3,-1\) in order of first occurrence, no calls) are a finite check of the universal-circuit section.

This is a definition. A power call \(\mathcal P[g_P,g_Q,g_R;w]\) substitutes the three parameter polynomials and moves the \(79\) witnesses to the block \(X_w,\dots,X_{w+78}\), as in the call semantics of the specification chapter; this is the power interface between the natural circuit and the power-value recipe.

docs.title: Semantics of the power template
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.powerTemplate_natRel ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.powerSpec_hierarchical_powerTemplate

For all natural numbers \(P,Q,R\): $\(\bigl(\exists w\in\mathbb N^{79},\ \mathcal P(P,Q,R,w)=0\bigr)\iff P=Q^R,\)$ with \(0^0=1\). Consequently, in any natural construction in hierarchical mode, a power call whose argument polynomials take natural values at every natural point and whose block is private (pairwise disjoint from the other blocks and occurring in no other atom or argument) may be replaced by the relation \(g_P=g_Q^{\,g_R}\) of its argument values.

Proof sketch. By the compilation statement, \(\mathcal P(P,Q,R,w)=0\) iff the flat power formula holds naturally at \((P,Q,R,w)\); by item 2 of that statement the existential over the \(79\) witnesses distributes over the three branches and over the conjuncts of each branch, the witnesses of the two inactive branches being set to \(0\). The branch conditions are those of the power formula once the gadgets and the three alpha macros are replaced by their relations (equational gadgets, alpha soundness and completeness). The power formula expresses exponentiation.

docs.title: Semantics of the natural macros
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.lt_spec ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.divides_spec ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.alpha_spec ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.powerSpec_hierarchical ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.binomial_spec ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.orthogonal_spec ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.mask_spec ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.bitAnd_spec

Let a gadget or macro of the natural constructions be run from counter \(c_0\) to \(c_1\) on argument polynomials in variables below \(c_0\) that take natural values at every natural point, producing \(\varphi\). For every \(x:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\), writing \(a,b,\dots\) for the values of the arguments at \(x\), $\(\exists y:[c_0,c_1)\to\mathbb N,\ \ \varphi\text{ holds naturally at }x[y]\)$ is equivalent to the following relation (in hierarchical mode, the template is the power template and its calls are read as in item 3 of the compilation statement):

Macro Relation \(\mathrm{lt}(a,b)\) \(a<b\) \(\mathrm{divides}(a,b)\) \(a\mid b\) \(\mathrm{congruent}(a,M,b)\) \(a\equiv b\pmod M\) (\(a=b\) if \(M=0\)) \(\mathrm{odd}(x)\) \(x\) odd \(\mathrm{alpha}(X,b,N)\) \(b>3\) and \(X=\alpha_b(N)\) \(\mathrm{power}(P,Q,R)\), flat or hierarchical \(P=Q^R\) \(\mathrm{binomial}(C,N,K)\) \(C=\binom NK\) \(\mathrm{orthogonal}(a,b)\) \(a\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}b=0\) \(\mathrm{mask}(a,b)\) \(a\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}b=a\) \(\mathrm{bitAnd}(z,x,y)\) \(z=x\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}y\)

The hypothesis on the arguments holds whenever the argument polynomials have nonnegative coefficients, as all arguments in this chapter do (\(Q+4\), \(R+1\), \(2X\), \(a+b\), \(K\cdot N_j\), \(R_j+D\) and so on).

Proof sketch. By the compilation statement each conjunction splits along the intervals of its conjuncts, so each macro reduces to its listed conditions with the inner macros replaced by their relations (induction in the order lt, divides, congruent, odd; alpha; power; binomial; orthogonal, mask; bitAnd). Then: the four equational gadgets; alpha is the alpha formula with its strict inequalities, divisibility and congruences replaced by the gadgets, so soundness and completeness of the alpha formula apply; power is the power formula, whose correctness gives \(P=Q^R\) (hierarchical mode: the power-template semantics); binomial is the binomial-digit statement; orthogonal and mask are Lucas's criterion with the odd gadget; bitAnd is the AND gadget with orthogonality.

docs.title: Natural semantics of a natural circuit
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.NatCircuit ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.NatCircuit.poly ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.NatCircuit.NatRel ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.NatCircuit.WellScoped

Let \(\mathcal C\) be a natural circuit in the format of the specification chapter: \(k\) inputs, a list of explicit variables (inputs first, with indices \(0,\dots,k-1\)), a node list of constants, variables, additions, multiplications and calls \(\mathrm{call}\,(a,b,c)\,w\) of the power template on three earlier nodes with block start \(w\), a root node, and a variable count \(V\) (the number of explicit variables plus \(79\) times the number of calls, when the blocks and explicit variables tile \([0,V)\)).

  1. The polynomial \([\![\mathcal C]\!]\in\mathbb Z[X_i:i\in\mathbb N]\) is the denotation of the root under the template semantics of the specification chapter, a call node denoting the power call \(\mathcal P\bigl[[\![a]\!],[\![b]\!],[\![c]\!];w\bigr]\) (literal substitution).
  2. The natural relation of \(\mathcal C\) is the predicate on \(\mathbb N^k\) $\(Z_{\mathcal C}(c_0,\dots,c_{k-1})\iff\exists z\in\mathbb N^{V-k},\ \ [\![\mathcal C]\!](c_0,\dots,c_{k-1},z)=0 ,\)$ the variables of index at least \(V\), if any occur, being set to \(0\).
  3. \(\mathcal C\) is well scoped if every block \([w,w+79)\) lies in \([k,V)\), the blocks are pairwise disjoint and disjoint from the explicit variables, the explicit variables and blocks together cover \([0,V)\), and every variable node refers to an explicit variable.

This is a definition. Item 2 quantifies over natural witnesses only; replacing \(\mathbb N\) by \(\mathbb Q\) here is not justified, and the translation to rational point codes is the subject of the next section.

docs.title: Circuits of hierarchical constructions
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.toCircuit_item1 ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.toCircuit_natRel_iff ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.toCircuit_natRel_iff_of_mspec ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.toCircuit_andM_natRel_iff ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.toCircuit_wellScoped ZInQ.Compiler.Natural.toCircuit_poly

Let a natural construction with \(k\) inputs in hierarchical mode end with formula \(\varphi\) and counter \(V\), and let \(\mathcal C\) be its natural circuit: its explicit variables are the inputs and fresh variables in allocation order, its node list is the node encoding of \(\varphi\) with root the encoding of \(\kappa(\varphi)\), and its call nodes are the power calls with their blocks. Assume every macro argument is a polynomial in variables allocated before the macro. Then:

  1. \(\mathcal C\) is well scoped, its variable count is \(V\), and \([\![\mathcal C]\!]=\kappa(\varphi)\);
  2. if moreover \(k\le V\), the variables of \(\kappa(\varphi)\) are below \(V\), and the call blocks of \(\varphi\) are private (they lie in \([k,\infty)\), are pairwise disjoint, and contain no variable of an atom or of a call argument of \(\varphi\)), then for every \(c\in\mathbb N^k\), \(Z_{\mathcal C}(c)\) holds if and only if there are natural values of the variables, equal to \(c\) on the inputs, for which \(\varphi^\natural\) holds, where \(\varphi^\natural\) is \(\varphi\) with every power call atom replaced by the statement that some natural values of the \(79\) witnesses make \(\mathcal P\) vanish at the values of its arguments; when these values are natural, this is the relation \(g_P=g_Q^{\,g_R}\) of its arguments;
  3. consequently, if the construction has a macro specification \(R\) over its inputs (built from the macro semantics by the composition rules: conjunction, disjunction, and an existential over each fresh variable), then \(Z_{\mathcal C}(c)\iff R(c)\); that is, \(Z_{\mathcal C}(c)\) is equivalent to the conjunction of the relations of the macros of the construction, quantified over the remaining fresh variables.

The flat construction gives the same relation: replacing each power call by the flat power macro changes the polynomial and the variable numbering but not the relation.

Proof sketch. (1) Induction over construction steps as in the specification chapter's construction theorem: every node handed out denotes the polynomial of the expression it was created for (hash-consing returns only structurally equal nodes), the counter only grows, blocks are taken from it consecutively, and a block index is passed only as a call's witness start, so no variable node refers to a block and the explicit variables and blocks tile \([0,V)\). (2) By the compilation statement (items 1 and 3), applied to the private blocks, together with the power-template semantics for natural argument values. (3) is (2) with the macro semantics. The flat/hierarchical remark follows because both readings of a power call have relation \(P=Q^R\).

docs.title: The packed-history compiler
docs.text:
A primitive program with \(m\) instructions over \(r\) registers is compiled by packing a run of length \(q\) into base-\(B\) integers, with \(K=2^c\), \(B=4K>m\), \(T=B^q\), \(F_q=1+B+\dots+B^q\) and \(D=(K-1)F_q\), every input being below \(K\).

Masks by \(D\) and \(F_q\) and the bound \(R_j<T\) make register digits smaller than \(K\) with a zero final digit, and state digits zero or one; since \(B>m\) the state sum selects exactly one state at each time.

The nonzero indicator is read off one bit per slot of \(R_j+D\), and a sub instruction splits its state history into nonzero and zero branch histories; the increment, decrement and incoming indicators then have zero-one digits.

The register and state equations have all coefficients below \(B\), so uniqueness of base-\(B\) digits turns them into the initial conditions and the exact transitions, the extra final slot vanishing.

Every solution decodes to an accepting run, and every accepting run fits once \(c\) is large. The compiled circuit therefore has a natural zero exactly at the accepted inputs.

The numbers of explicit variables and power calls are linear in \(m\), \(r\), the number of sub instructions and the number of inputs.

10 fully proved

docs.title: The packed-history construction
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Packed.construction ZInQ.Compiler.Packed.compiled

Let \(p=(p_0,\dots,p_{m-1})\) be a primitive program valid for \(r\) registers and let \(1\le k\le r\). The packed-history construction of \(p\) is the natural construction in hierarchical mode with \(k\) inputs \(a_0,\dots,a_{k-1}\) (\(=X_0,\dots,X_{k-1}\)) which takes the fresh variables $\(q,\ c,\ K,\ B,\ T,\ F,\ D,\qquad R_0,\dots,R_{r-1},\qquad N_0,\dots,N_{r-1},\qquad S_0,\dots,S_{m-1}\)$ in this order and returns the conjunction of the following formulas, in this order:

  1. \(\mathrm{lt}(0,c)\), \(\mathrm{power}(K,2,c)\), \(B\doteq4K\), \(\mathrm{lt}(m,B)\), \(\mathrm{power}(T,B,q)\), then \(\mathrm{lt}(a_i,K)\) for \(i<k\);
  2. \(BF+1\doteq F+BT\), \(D+F\doteq KF\), \(S_0+\dots+S_{m-1}\doteq F\), \(S_{m-1}\doteq T\);
  3. \(\mathrm{mask}(S_i,F)\) for \(i<m\);
  4. for each \(j<r\): \(\mathrm{mask}(R_j,D)\), \(\mathrm{lt}(R_j,T)\), \(\mathrm{bitAnd}(K\cdot N_j,\ R_j+D,\ K\cdot F)\);
  5. for each sub instruction \(p_i=\mathrm{dec}(j,x,y)\), in increasing \(i\): fresh \(V_i,W_i\), then \(\mathrm{bitAnd}(V_i,S_i,N_j)\) and \(S_i\doteq V_i+W_i\);
  6. for each \(j<r\): \(R_j+B\cdot C_j\doteq\iota_j+B\cdot R_j+B\cdot A_j\), where \(\iota_j=a_j\) for \(j<k\) and \(0\) otherwise, \(A_j=\sum_{i:\,p_i=\mathrm{inc}(j,\cdot)}S_i\) and \(C_j=\sum_{i:\,p_i=\mathrm{dec}(j,\cdot,\cdot)}V_i\);
  7. for each \(i<m\): \(S_i\doteq[i=0]+B\cdot I_i\), where \(I_i\) is the sum, in program order, of \(S_{i'}\) for \(p_{i'}=\mathrm{inc}(\cdot,i)\), of \(V_{i'}\) for \(p_{i'}=\mathrm{dec}(\cdot,i,\cdot)\) and of \(W_{i'}\) for \(p_{i'}=\mathrm{dec}(\cdot,\cdot,i)\) (for a sub instruction its nonzero target is listed before its zero target).

Empty sums are the constant \(0\). The compiled circuit \(\mathcal C_{p,k}\) is the natural circuit of this construction. Here \(R_j\) is the packed history of register \(j\), \(S_i\) that of state \(i\), \(N_j\) the packed nonzero indicator, \(V_i,W_i\) the nonzero and zero branch histories, and \(F=F_q=1+B+\dots+B^q\), \(D=(K-1)F_q\) by item 2.

This is a definition. No equation is repeated \(q\) times: \(q\) is one variable and the number of conjuncts depends only on \(p\).

docs.title: Digits of masked histories
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Packed.packed_masks

Let \(c>0\), \(K=2^c\), \(B=4K\), \(q\in\mathbb N\), \(T=B^q\), and let \(F,D\in\mathbb N\) satisfy \(BF+1=F+BT\) and \(D+F=KF\). Then:

  1. \(F=F_q=\sum_{t=0}^qB^t\) and \(D=(K-1)F_q=\sum_{t=0}^q(K-1)B^t\);
  2. a natural number \(R\) is masked by \(D\) and satisfies \(R<T\) if and only if \(R=\sum_{t=0}^q\rho_tB^t\) with \(\rho_t<K\) for all \(t\) and \(\rho_q=0\);
  3. a natural number \(S\) is masked by \(F_q\) if and only if \(S=\sum_{t=0}^q\sigma_tB^t\) with \(\sigma_t\in\{0,1\}\).

In words: register digits are below \(K\), the terminal register digit is zero, and state digits are zero or one. The digit sequences are unique.

Proof sketch. (1) \(B\ge8\), so \(BF+1=F+BT\) gives \((B-1)F=B^{q+1}-1\), hence \(F=\sum_{t\le q}B^t\); then \(D=KF-F\). (2), (3) \(B=2^{c+2}\), so the binary expansion of a number splits into base-\(B\) slots of \(c+2\) bits. \(D\) has, in each slot \(t\le q\), the bits \(0,\dots,c-1\) set (value \(K-1\)) and nothing above slot \(q\); \(F_q\) has bit \(0\) of each slot \(t\le q\). Masking by \(D\) (resp. \(F_q\)) therefore says exactly that every slot digit is below \(K\) (resp. at most \(1\)) and that the slots above \(q\) vanish. Finally \(R<B^q\) is equivalent to \(\rho_q=0\) given the other slots vanish.

docs.title: One active state per time slot
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Packed.one_active_state

Let \(B,q,T=B^q,F_q\) be as in the masked-digit statement, let \(1\le m<B\), and let \(S_0,\dots,S_{m-1}\) be masked by \(F_q\), with digits \(\sigma_i(t)\in\{0,1\}\) (\(t\le q\)). If $\(S_0+\dots+S_{m-1}=F_q\qquad\text{and}\qquad S_{m-1}=T,\)$ then for every \(t\le q\) there is exactly one \(i<m\) with \(\sigma_i(t)=1\), and \(\sigma_{m-1}(t)=1\) if and only if \(t=q\). Conversely, if exactly one state digit is \(1\) in each slot \(t\le q\) and the last state's digit is \(1\) exactly at \(t=q\), both equations hold.

Proof sketch. In slot \(t\) the digits sum to \(\sum_i\sigma_i(t)\le m<B\), so the sum of the \(S_i\) is computed without carries and its slot-\(t\) digit is \(\sum_i\sigma_i(t)\); comparing with the digit \(1\) of \(F_q\) gives exactly one active state. \(S_{m-1}=B^q\) says the last state's digits are \(0\) except at \(t=q\).

docs.title: The packed nonzero indicator
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Packed.nonzero_indicator

Let \(c>0\), \(K=2^c\), \(B=4K\), \(F_q\), \(D=(K-1)F_q\) be as in the masked-digit statement and \(R=\sum_{t=0}^q\rho_tB^t\) with all \(\rho_t<K\). Then $\((R+D)\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}(KF_q)=K\cdot\sum_{t=0}^q[\rho_t>0]\,B^t .\)$ Consequently, for \(N\in\mathbb N\), \(KN=(R+D)\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}(KF_q)\) holds if and only if \(N=\sum_{t\le q}[\rho_t>0]B^t\), the packed nonzero indicator of \(R\); no separate mask condition on \(N\) is needed.

Proof sketch. \(R+D=\sum_t(\rho_t+K-1)B^t\), and each slot digit satisfies \(\rho_t+K-1\le2K-2<2K<B\), so the sum has no carries. \(KF_q\) has exactly bit \(c\) of each slot \(t\le q\). The bit \(c\) (value \(K\)) of the slot digit \(\rho_t+K-1\in[K-1,2K-2]\) is set exactly when \(\rho_t+K-1\ge K\), that is when \(\rho_t>0\). Cancel the factor \(K=2^c\).

docs.title: Branch histories and indicator digits
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Packed.branch_split ZInQ.Compiler.Packed.indicator_digits

Let \(B\ge2\), \(q\in\mathbb N\), \(S=\sum_{t\le q}\sigma_tB^t\) and \(N=\sum_{t\le q} u_tB^t\) with \(\sigma_t, u_t\in\{0,1\}\), \(B\) a power of two.

  1. \(V=S\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}N\) and \(S=V+W\) hold (for natural \(V,W\)) if and only if \(V=\sum_t\sigma_t u_tB^t\) and \(W=\sum_t\sigma_t(1- u_t)B^t\).
  2. In the setting of the packed-history construction, suppose that in every slot \(t\le q\) exactly one state digit \(\sigma_i(t)\) is \(1\) and that the halt state has no outgoing instruction. Then the packed indicators \(A_j\), \(C_j\) and \(I_i\) of items 6 and 7 of the construction have all slot digits in \(\{0,1\}\); precisely, writing \(i_t\) for the active state at time \(t\), the slot-\(t\) digit of \(A_j\) is \([p_{i_t}=\mathrm{inc}(j,\cdot)]\), that of \(C_j\) is \([p_{i_t}=\mathrm{dec}(j,\cdot,\cdot)]\, u_j(t)\), and that of \(I_i\) is \(1\) exactly when the instruction at \(i_t\) takes, at time \(t\), a branch to \(i\) (the nonzero branch of a sub instruction if \( u_j(t)=1\), its zero branch otherwise).

Proof sketch. (1) Both \(S\) and \(N\) have zero-one digits in distinct bit positions, so \(S\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}N\) is computed slotwise; \(W=S-V\) slotwise. (2) A sum of packed numbers with zero-one digits is computed slotwise as long as the slot sums stay below \(B\); at time \(t\) only the instruction at \(i_t\) contributes, through \(S_{i_t}\), \(V_{i_t}\) or \(W_{i_t}\), and for a sub instruction exactly one of \(V_{i_t},W_{i_t}\) has digit \(1\) by (1); this holds even if two branches of the program have the same target, since only one branch is taken at a time.

docs.title: Decoding the transition equations
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Packed.packed_register_iff ZInQ.Compiler.Packed.packed_state_iff

Let \(K<B\) be natural numbers and \(q\in\mathbb N\).

  1. (Registers) Let \(\rho_t<K\), \(\alpha_t\le1\), \(\gamma_t\le1\) for \(t\le q\), let \(\iota<K\), and put \(R=\sum_{t\le q}\rho_tB^t\), \(A=\sum_{t\le q}\alpha_tB^t\), \(C=\sum_{t\le q}\gamma_tB^t\). Then $\(R+BC=\iota+BR+BA\)$ holds if and only if \(\rho_0=\iota\), \(\rho_{t+1}+\gamma_t=\rho_t+\alpha_t\) for all \(t<q\), and \(\gamma_q=\rho_q+\alpha_q\).
  2. (States) Suppose \(B\ge2\). Let \(\sigma_t\le1\) and \(\eta_t\le1\) for \(t\le q\), \(S=\sum_{t\le q}\sigma_tB^t\), \(I=\sum_{t\le q}\eta_tB^t\) and \(e\in\{0,1\}\). Then \(S=e+BI\) holds if and only if \(\sigma_0=e\), \(\sigma_{t+1}=\eta_t\) for \(t<q\), and \(\eta_q=0\).

Proof sketch. Compare base-\(B\) digits. In item 1 the slot-\(0\) digits are \(\rho_0\) and \(\iota\), the slot-\((t+1)\) digits are \(\rho_{t+1}+\gamma_t\le K\) and \(\rho_t+\alpha_t\le K\) for \(t<q\), and the slot-\((q+1)\) digits are \(\gamma_q\) and \(\rho_q+\alpha_q\le K\); every digit on either side is at most \(K<B\), so uniqueness of base-\(B\) expansions (with an unbounded top part) gives digitwise equality, and conversely. Item 2 is the same with digits at most \(1<B\).

docs.title: Soundness of the packed-history construction
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Packed.packed_sound ZInQ.Compiler.Packed.packed_sound_accepts

Let \(p\) be valid for \(r\) registers with \(m\) instructions, \(1\le k\le r\) and \(a\in\mathbb N^k\). If the formula of the packed-history construction of \(p\) holds for some natural values of its fresh variables, with every macro read as its relation (masks as bit inclusion, bitAnd as bitwise conjunction, power as exponentiation, lt as strict inequality), then \(p\) accepts \(a\), and its accepting run has exactly \(q\) steps.

Proof sketch. From \(c>0\), \(K=2^c\), \(B=4K\), \(T=B^q\) and the two equations for \(F,D\), the masked-digit statement decodes \(R_j=\sum_{t\le q}\rho_j(t)B^t\) with \(\rho_j(t)<K\), \(\rho_j(q)=0\), and \(S_i=\sum_{t\le q}\sigma_i(t)B^t\) with zero-one digits; \(m<B\) and the state equations give one active state \(i_t\) per slot with the halt state \(m-1\) active exactly at \(t=q\). The nonzero indicator gives \(N_j\) with digits \(\nu_j(t)=[\rho_j(t)>0]\), and the branch statement gives \(V_i,W_i\) and the indicator digits. Define the configuration at time \(t\le q\) as \((i_t,\rho(t))\). The state equations (decoded with \(e=[i=0]\)) give \(i_0=0\) and \(i_{t+1}=\) the branch target taken at time \(t\); the register equations (decoded with \(\iota_j=a_j<K\) or \(0\)) give \(\rho_j(0)=\iota_j\) and \(\rho_j(t+1)=\rho_j(t)+\alpha_j(t)-\gamma_j(t)\), which is exactly the effect of the instruction at \(i_t\) (a decrement happens only when \(\nu_j(t)=1\), that is when \(\rho_j(t)>0\)). Since the halt state is active only at \(t=q\), the configurations form the run of \(p\) from the initial file, it reaches the final state at time \(q\), and there \(\rho_j(q)=0\) for all \(j\). The extra slot \(q+1\) of the register equation, \(\gamma_j(q)=\rho_j(q)+\alpha_j(q)\), is \(0=0\) because halt has no outgoing instruction, and the extra slot of the state equation says \(\eta_i(q)=0\) for the same reason. If \(q=0\) the state \(0\) is the halt state (so \(m=1\)) and every input vanishes.

  • Halting correctness proof

docs.title: Completeness of the packed-history construction
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Packed.packed_complete

Let \(p\) be valid for \(r\) registers with \(m\) instructions, \(1\le k\le r\) and \(a\in\mathbb N^k\). If \(p\) accepts \(a\), then the formula of the packed-history construction of \(p\) holds for some natural values of its fresh variables, with every macro read as its relation.

Proof sketch. Let the accepting run have \(q\) steps, configurations \((i_t,\rho(t))\) for \(t\le q\), with \(i_q=m-1\) and \(\rho(q)=0\). Choose \(c\ge1\) with \(2^c\) larger than every input, every register value \(\rho_j(t)\), and with \(4\cdot2^c>m\); put \(K=2^c\), \(B=4K\), \(T=B^q\), \(F=\sum_{t\le q}B^t\), \(D=(K-1)F\), \(R_j=\sum_t\rho_j(t)B^t\), \(S_i=\sum_t[i_t=i]B^t\), \(N_j=\sum_t[\rho_j(t)>0]B^t\), and for each sub instruction \(i\) on register \(j\), \(V_i=\sum_t[i_t=i][\rho_j(t)>0]B^t\), \(W_i=S_i-V_i\). Every equation of items 1, 2 holds by construction; the masks, the bounds \(R_j<T\) and the bitAnd conditions hold by the masked-digit, nonzero-indicator and branch statements read backwards; the register and state equations hold by the transition statement read backwards, since consecutive configurations obey the one-step rule, the run starts at state \(0\) with the initial file, halt has no outgoing branch and \(\rho(q)=0\).

docs.title: The compiled circuit of a register machine
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Packed.compiled_natRel_iff

Let \(p\) be a primitive program valid for \(r\) registers and \(1\le k\le r\). For every \(a\in\mathbb N^k\), $\(Z_{\mathcal C_{p,k}}(a)\iff p\text{ accepts }a,\)$ where \(\mathcal C_{p,k}\) is the compiled circuit of the packed-history construction. In particular the compiled polynomial has a natural zero with inputs \(a\) exactly when \(p\) reaches its final halt from the initial file with all registers zero. This holds for every run length, every size of the register values and every number of inputs.

Proof sketch. All macro arguments of the construction are polynomials in previously allocated variables, so the hierarchical-construction statement applies: \(Z_{\mathcal C}(a)\) is equivalent to the existence of natural values of the fresh variables satisfying the conjunction with every macro replaced by its relation. Soundness and completeness of the packed-history construction give the two implications.

docs.title: Variable and gadget counts of the packed construction
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Packed.packed_counts

Let \(p\) be valid for \(r\) registers with \(m\) instructions, of which \(s\) are sub instructions, and \(1\le k\le r\). The packed-history construction of \(p\) creates

  • \(m+r\) mask macros, \(r+s\) bitAnd macros, \(3(r+s)\) orthogonal macros, \(m+4r+3s\) binomial macros, \(m+4r+3s\) odd gadgets and \(2+k+r+2(m+4r+3s)\) strict-inequality gadgets (\(2+k+r\) outside the binomials and two in each binomial);
  • \(2+3(m+4r+3s)=2+3m+12r+9s\) power calls, each with a private block of \(79\) variables;
  • \(2k+9+41r+10m+31s\) explicit variables, the \(k\) inputs included.

Hence the compiled circuit \(\mathcal C_{p,k}\) has variable count $\(V=(2k+9+41r+10m+31s)+79\,(2+3m+12r+9s).\)$ These counts are independent of the order of the instructions and of the jump targets. The numbers of addition and multiplication nodes depend on hash-consing and on the targets, and are not given in closed form here.

Proof sketch. Count the allocations of each step of the construction: seven fresh variables \(q,\dots,D\), \(2r\) for \(R_j,N_j\), \(m\) for \(S_i\), \(2s\) for \(V_i,W_i\); each lt, divides and odd gadget takes one variable and each congruent two (only lt and odd occur outside the power template); a binomial takes \(5\) fresh variables, three power calls and two lt gadgets; a mask or orthogonal macro takes one fresh variable, one binomial and one odd gadget; a bitAnd takes two fresh variables and three orthogonals. Summing: \(k+7+2r+m+2s+(2+k+r)+2(m+4r+3s)+5(m+4r+3s)+(m+r)+3(r+s)+(m+4r+3s)+2(r+s) =2k+9+41r+10m+31s\), and the power calls are the two of item 1 plus three per binomial.

docs.title: The exact precision computation
docs.text:
The five natural inputs of the precision computation are signed encodings, decoded in the fixed order \((n,\kappa,a,l,j)\).

The local parameter \(z=-x/y\) is defined at multiples of \(P_0\) that are affine with nonzero ordinate; at such an index \(k\) it gives the components \(u_k,v_k\), the size \(\epsilon_k=|u_k|+|v_k|\), and the trace ratio \(r(a,j)\).

The precision exponent uses the six-contact constant for the primes up to \(324\), written as an explicit natural-number expression; it is never evaluated.

The relation itself consists of the early tests, admissibility, and two strict tests. Given that \(P_0\) has infinite order, admissibility follows from the early tests; the model chapter proves this unconditionally (nonzero multiples of the generator).

17 fully proved

docs.title: The signed encoding of integers
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.enc ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.dec ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.decode5

The signed encoding \(\operatorname{enc}:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb N\) and its decoding \(\operatorname{dec}:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z\) are $\(\operatorname{enc}(n)=\begin{cases}2n,&n\ge0,\\-2n-1,&n<0,\end{cases}\qquad \operatorname{dec}(c)=\begin{cases}c/2,&c\text{ even},\\-(c+1)/2,&c\text{ odd}.\end{cases}\)$ A tuple \(c=(c_0,c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4)\in\mathbb N^5\) of precision inputs decodes, in this fixed order, to \((n,\kappa,a,l,j)=(\operatorname{dec}c_0,\dots,\operatorname{dec}c_4)\in\mathbb Z^5\).

This is a definition. The order \((n,\kappa,a,l,j)\) is the order in which the ordinary-value relation links its five signed codes to the precision inputs.

docs.title: The signed encoding is a bijection
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.dec_enc ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.enc_dec ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.encEquiv

\(\operatorname{dec}(\operatorname{enc}(n))=n\) for every \(n\in\mathbb Z\) and \(\operatorname{enc}(\operatorname{dec}(c))=c\) for every \(c\in\mathbb N\). Moreover \(\operatorname{enc}(n)\) is even exactly when \(n\ge0\), and \(|\operatorname{dec}(c)|=\lceil c/2\rceil\).

Proof sketch. Case analysis on the sign of \(n\) and the parity of \(c\): \(2n\) is even with half \(n\); \(-2n-1\) is odd for \(n<0\) and \(-((-2n-1)+1)/2=n\); conversely \(c=2h\) decodes to \(h\ge0\) and \(c=2h+1\) to \(-(h+1)<0\), which encodes to \(2h+1\).

docs.title: The local parameter z on multiples of the generator
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.zPt ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.zPt_ne_zero ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.Admissible ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.zIdx ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.epsIdx ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.rRatio ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.rRatio_eq_half_trace

Let \(E:y^2=x^3+Ax\) over \(K_0\) with \(A=-d^2\), and \(P_0\) the fixed point.

  1. For an affine point \(P=(x,y)\in E(K_0)\) with \(y e0\) put \(z(P)=-x/y\in K_0\). Such a point has \(x e0\) (if \(x=0\) then \(y^2=0\)), so \(z(P) e0\); and \(z(-P)=-z(P)\).
  2. An index \(k\in\mathbb Z\) is admissible if \([k]P_0\) is an affine point with nonzero ordinate. For admissible \(k\) write $\(z_k=z([k]P_0)=u_k+v_ks\quad(u_k,v_k\in\mathbb Q),\qquad \epsilon_k=|u_k|+|v_k|>0 .\)$
  3. For admissible \(a\) and \(j\) put $\(r(a,j)= frac12\operatorname{Tr}_{K_0/\mathbb Q} rac{z_j}{z_a}\in\mathbb Q,\)$ the rational component of \(z_j/z_a\).

This is a definition. The manuscript defines \(z\) on nonzero multiples of \(P_0\), where it is well defined because \(P_0\) has infinite order (no nonzero multiple is the identity or a point of order two); admissibility makes this explicit, so that the precision relation and its computation do not depend on the generator theorem.

docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.Q0 ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.A0 ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.sixF ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.bound ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.contacts

The following natural numbers are defined by their displayed expressions and are never evaluated: $\(\begin{aligned} F_0&=324!, & D&=F_0\,3^{256F_0^4}, & G_0&=116064000000, & E_0&=10(DG_0)^2,\\ Q_0&=D^{DE_0}, & B_{\rm cm}&=D^2\,3^{21000D^2}+1, & C_{\rm cm}&=2B_{\rm cm}+4096(1028+5D+84000D^2), \end{aligned}\)$ $\(A^{(0)}_{\rm ht}=2\cdot10^{13}\cdot\max\bigl(1,\ C_{\rm cm},\ Q_0^{17}\bigr).\)$ With \(F(u)=u(u+15)(u+20)(u+24)(u+30)(u+60)\) and \(\mathcal C=\{0,-15,-20,-24,-30,-60\}\), the precision bound of \((n,\kappa)\in\mathbb Z^2\) is the natural number $\(\mathcal B(n,\kappa)=A^{(0)}_{\rm ht}\,|\kappa F(n)|^{24}.\)$

This is a definition. \(A^{(0)}_{\rm ht}\) is the six-contact constant \(H_6(S_{\rm ht})\) for \(S_{\rm ht}=\{p\le324\}\); the identification is a separate statement. Its symbol \(F_0\) is distinct from the polynomial \(F\).

docs.title: The precision constant is the six-contact constant
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.A0_eq_heightH6 ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.max_heightD_heightPrimes ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.bound_eq_heightH6

Let \(S_{\rm ht}\) be the set of primes at most \(324\). Then \(\max(D,\max S_{\rm ht},10^{12})=D\), and the six-contact constant at this argument is the precision constant: $\(H_6(S_{\rm ht})=H_6(S_{\rm ht};D)=2\cdot10^{13}\max(1,C_{\rm cm},Q_D^{17})=A^{(0)}_{\rm ht},\)$ where \(Q_D=D^{DE_0}\) is computed as a real power. Consequently, for all \((n,\kappa)\in\mathbb Z^2\), \(\mathcal B(n,\kappa)=H_6(S_{\rm ht})\,|\kappa F(n)|^{24}\) is the bound \(B(n,\kappa)\) of the ordinary-value relation, and \(R=D\) is an admissible argument of the six-contact estimate for \(S_{\rm ht}\).

Proof sketch. \(\max S_{\rm ht}=317\), and \(D\ge F_0=324!>10^{12}\), so the maximum is \(D\) (no evaluation of \(D\) is needed: \(324!\ge10^{12}\) is a small finite check, for instance \(324!\ge20!>10^{12}\)). The real power \(D^{D E_0}\) with natural base and natural exponent equals the natural power, so \(Q_D=Q_0\), and the remaining expressions agree term by term.

docs.title: The precision relation
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.accepts ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.acceptsInt ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.accepts_iff

For \(c\in\mathbb N^5\) let \((n,\kappa,a,l,j)\in\mathbb Z^5\) be its signed decoding. The precision relation \(\operatorname{accepts}(c)\) holds if and only if all of the following hold:

  1. (early tests) \(n\notin\mathcal C=\{0,-15,-20,-24,-30,-60\}\), \(\kappa\ne0\), \(a\ge1\), \(l\ge1\) and \(j=na\);
  2. (admissibility) \(l\), \(a\) and \(j\) are admissible indices;
  3. (closeness) \(|r(a,j)-n|<\epsilon_l\);
  4. (precision) \(4\epsilon_l<4^{-\mathcal B(n,\kappa)}\), that is \(4\,\epsilon_l\cdot4^{\mathcal B(n,\kappa)}<1\), with \(\mathcal B(n,\kappa)=A^{(0)}_{\rm ht}|\kappa F(n)|^{24}\).

Both final tests are strict inequalities between rational numbers (equivalently, between real numbers). This is the predicate called \(\operatorname{accepts\_naturals}\) in equation (C.4).

This is a definition. Item 2 is implicit in the manuscript, which defines \(z\) only on nonzero multiples of \(P_0\); given the generator theorem it follows from item 1, so the relation is the manuscript's on every input where the latter is meaningful.

ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.admissible_of_ne_zero ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.accepts_iff_tests

Assume \(P_0\) has infinite order in \(E(K_0)\). Then every \(k\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}\) is admissible. Consequently, for \(c\in\mathbb N^5\) passing the early tests of the precision relation, the indices \(l,a,j\) are admissible, and \(\operatorname{accepts}(c)\) holds if and only if the closeness and precision tests hold.

Proof sketch. For \(k e0\), \([k]P_0 e O\) since \(P_0\) has infinite order. If its ordinate were \(0\) then \([k]P_0=-[k]P_0\), so \([2k]P_0=O\) with \(2k e0\), again impossible. For inputs passing the early tests, \(l,a\ge1\) and \(j=na e0\) because \(n e0\) (\(0\in\mathcal C\)) and \(a e0\).

docs.title: Exact evaluation
docs.text:
The second strict test compares \(\epsilon_l=U/V\) with \(4^{-\mathcal B}\); it becomes an integer comparison with the finite cap \(L=\lfloor(V-1)/(4U)\rfloor\). Saturating every operation at \(L+1\) computes the comparison exactly without evaluating \(\mathcal B\).

Field divisions are guarded by the norm, which vanishes only at zero. Points are handled in Jacobian coordinates over \(\mathbb Z[s]\), with explicit identities for doubling and addition and their exceptional branches, and a finite check that the fixed projective point is \(P_0\); scalar multiplication halves its counter.

The decision program assembles these steps, and it computes the relation on every input.

docs.title: The precision threshold as an integer comparison
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.four_eps_lt_iff_nat ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.four_eps_lt_iff ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.four_eps_mul_pow_lt_one_iff

Let \(U,V\) be positive natural numbers, \(\epsilon=U/V\), and \(B\in\mathbb N\). Then $\(4\epsilon<4^{-B}\iff4U\cdot4^B<V\iff4^B\le\left\lfloor\frac{V-1}{4U}\right\rfloor .\)$

Proof sketch. Multiply by the positive number \(V4^B\) for the first equivalence. For the second, for positive \(a\) and \(D\) and natural \(x\), \(ax<D\iff ax\le D-1\iff x\le\lfloor(D-1)/a\rfloor\), applied with \(a=4U\), \(x=4^B\), \(D=V\).

docs.title: Saturated arithmetic
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.saturatedArithmetic

For \(L\in\mathbb N\) let \(\sigma_L(x)=\min(x,L+1)\) on \(\mathbb N\). For all natural \(x,y,n\):

  1. \(\sigma_L(x)\le L\iff x\le L\), and more generally \(\sigma_L(x)\le k\iff x\le k\) for \(k\le L\); \(\sigma_L(\sigma_L(x))=\sigma_L(x)\); \(\sigma_L(0)=0\), \(\sigma_L(1)=1\);
  2. \(\sigma_L(\sigma_L(x)+\sigma_L(y))=\sigma_L(x+y)\), \(\sigma_L(\sigma_L(x)\cdot\sigma_L(y))=\sigma_L(xy)\) and \(\sigma_L(\max(\sigma_L(x),\sigma_L(y)))=\sigma_L(\max(x,y))\);
  3. \(\sigma_L(\sigma_L(x)^n)=\sigma_L(x^n)\);
  4. if \(L\ge1\), then \(\sigma_L(x^{\sigma_L(n)})=\sigma_L(x^n)\), hence \(\sigma_L(\sigma_L(x)^{\sigma_L(n)})=\sigma_L(x^n)\);
  5. \(\sigma_L((n+1)!)=\sigma_L(\sigma_L(n!)\cdot(n+1))\), so factorials are computed exactly by iterating saturated multiplication.

Item 4 is where bases zero and one and exponent zero are separate cases: for \(x\ge2\) an exponent above \(L\) already gives \(x^n>L\).

Proof sketch. Items 1-3 and 5 by cases on whether the arguments exceed \(L\): if \(x\ge L+1\) and \(y\ge1\) then \(xy\ge L+1\), and \(\sigma_L(x)\cdot y\ge L+1\); if \(y=0\) both sides are \(0\); item 3 by induction on \(n\) from item 2. Item 4: if \(n\le L+1\) nothing changes; otherwise \(\sigma_L(n)=L+1\) and, for \(x=0\), \(0^n=0^{L+1}=0\) (both exponents positive), for \(x=1\) both powers are \(1\), and for \(x\ge2\) both \(x^n\) and \(x^{L+1}\) exceed \(L\) because \(x^e>e\) for \(e\ge0\).

docs.title: Capped multiplication and binary exponentiation
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.cappedArithmetic

For \(L\in\mathbb N\) define capped multiplication by \(\mathrm{cmul}_L(a,b)=0\) if \(a=0\) or \(b=0\), \(L+1\) if \(a>\lfloor L/b\rfloor\), and \(ab\) otherwise; and capped binary exponentiation \(\mathrm{cpow}_L(x,e)\) by: \(1\) if \(e=0\); \(x\) if \(x\le1\); otherwise run the loop with state \((\beta,e,\pi)\) starting from \((x,e,1)\): if \(e=0\) return \(\pi\); if \(\beta>L\) return \(L+1\); put \(\pi'=\mathrm{cmul}_L(\pi,\beta)\) if \(e\) is odd and \(\pi'=\pi\) otherwise; if \(e\) is odd and \(\pi'=L+1\) return \(L+1\); if \(\lfloor e/2\rfloor=0\) return \(\pi'\); else continue with \((\mathrm{cmul}_L(\beta,\beta),\lfloor e/2\rfloor,\pi')\). Then for all natural \(L,a,b,x,e\): $\(\mathrm{cmul}_L(a,b)=\sigma_L(ab),\qquad\mathrm{cpow}_L(x,e)=\sigma_L(x^e),\)$ and \(\mathrm{cpow}_L(x,e)\le L\iff x^e\le L\). The loop terminates because \(e\) halves.

Proof sketch. For \(b>0\), \(a>\lfloor L/b\rfloor\iff ab>L\). For the loop, prove by strong induction on \(e\) the invariant \(\mathrm{loop}(\beta,e,\pi)=\sigma_L(\pi\beta^e)\) for \(\beta\ge1\), \(1\le\pi\le L+1\), using \(\beta^e=\beta^{e\bmod2}(\beta^2)^{\lfloor e/2\rfloor}\) and the saturation identities; the early returns are justified because \(\beta>L\) or \(\pi'=L+1\) force \(\sigma_L(\pi\beta^e)=L+1\). The initial cases are \(x^0=1\), \(0^e=0\), \(1^e=1\) for \(e>0\).

docs.title: The capped precision test
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.NExpr.capped_eq ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.cappedBound_eq ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.precision_test_iff

Expressions. Natural-number expressions are built from natural literals with \(+\), \(\cdot\), \(\max\), powers \(e_1^{e_2}\) and factorials \(e!\); \([\![e]\!]\in\mathbb N\) is the value. For \(L\in\mathbb N\) the capped value \(\langle e\rangle_L\) is defined by recursion on \(e\): \(\langle c\rangle_L=\sigma_L(c)\) for a literal \(c\); \(\langle e_1+e_2\rangle_L=\sigma_L(\langle e_1\rangle_L+\langle e_2\rangle_L)\); \(\langle e_1\cdot e_2\rangle_L=\mathrm{cmul}_L(\langle e_1\rangle_L,\langle e_2\rangle_L)\); \(\langle\max(e_1,e_2)\rangle_L=\sigma_L(\max(\langle e_1\rangle_L,\langle e_2\rangle_L))\); \(\langle e_1^{e_2}\rangle_L=\mathrm{cpow}_L(\langle e_1\rangle_L,\langle e_2\rangle_L)\); and \(\langle e!\rangle_L=f_L(\langle e\rangle_L)\), where \(f_L(0)=1\) and \(f_L(n+1)=\mathrm{cmul}_L(f_L(n),\sigma_L(n+1))\) (a loop of \(n\) capped multiplications).

The precision expressions. Let \(e_A\) be the expression of the precision height constant written with the literals displayed there: \(e_{F_0}=324!\), \(e_D=e_{F_0}\cdot3^{256\cdot e_{F_0}^4}\), \(e_{G_0}=116064000000\), \(e_{E_0}=10\cdot(e_D\cdot e_{G_0})^2\), \(e_{Q_0}=e_D^{\,e_D\cdot e_{E_0}}\), \(e_{B}=e_D^2\cdot3^{21000\cdot e_D^2}+1\), \(e_{C}=2\cdot e_B+4096\cdot(1028+5\cdot e_D+84000\cdot e_D^2)\) and \(e_A=2\cdot10^{13}\cdot\max(1,\max(e_C,e_{Q_0}^{17}))\) (here \(10^{13}\) is the literal \(10000000000000\)). So \([\![e_A]\!]=A^{(0)}_{\rm ht}\).

Let \(L\ge1\) and \(M\in\mathbb N\). Put $\(\beta=\mathrm{cmul}_L\bigl(\langle e_A\rangle_L,\ \mathrm{cpow}_L(\sigma_L(M),24)\bigr)\)$ and run the division-by-four loop: \(x_0=L\), \(x_{i+1}=\lfloor x_i/4\rfloor\), stopping after \(\beta\) steps. Then:

  1. \(\langle e\rangle_L=\sigma_L([\![e]\!])\) for every expression \(e\); in particular \(\langle e_A\rangle_L=\sigma_L(A^{(0)}_{\rm ht})\);
  2. \(\beta=\sigma_L(A^{(0)}_{\rm ht}M^{24})\);
  3. \(x_\beta=\lfloor L/4^\beta\rfloor\), and \(x_\beta\ge1\iff4^{A^{(0)}_{\rm ht}M^{24}}\le L\).

Moreover \(\beta\le L+1\), so the loop takes at most \(L+1\) steps, and every capped value \(\langle e\rangle_L\) is at most \(L+1\): nothing astronomically large is computed.

Proof sketch. (1) Induction on \(e\). Literals by definition. For \(+\), \(\max\): the saturation identities \(\sigma_L(\sigma_L(x)+\sigma_L(y))=\sigma_L(x+y)\) and the same for \(\max\). For \(\cdot\): \(\mathrm{cmul}_L(a,b)=\sigma_L(ab)\), then \(\sigma_L(\sigma_L(x)\sigma_L(y))=\sigma_L(xy)\). For powers: \(\mathrm{cpow}_L(a,b)=\sigma_L(a^b)\) and \(\sigma_L(\sigma_L(x)^{\sigma_L(n)})=\sigma_L(x^n)\), which needs \(L\ge1\). For factorials: by induction on \(n\), \(f_L(n)=\sigma_L(n!)\) (item 5 of the saturation statement), and \(f_L(\sigma_L(n))=\sigma_L(n!)\) because for \(n\ge L+1\) both \(n!\) and \((L+1)!\) are at least \(L+1\). (2) By (1), the capped power and the capped product, \(\beta=\sigma_L(\sigma_L(A^{(0)}_{\rm ht})\cdot\sigma_L(M^{24}))=\sigma_L(A^{(0)}_{\rm ht}M^{24})\). (3) \(\lfloor\lfloor x/4\rfloor/4^i\rfloor=\lfloor x/4^{i+1}\rfloor\) gives \(x_i=\lfloor L/4^i\rfloor\), and \(\lfloor L/4^\beta\rfloor\ge1\iff4^\beta\le L\). Put \(B=A^{(0)}_{\rm ht}M^{24}\). If \(B\le L\) then \(\beta=B\). Otherwise \(\beta=L+1\), and both \(4^{L+1}\le L\) and \(4^B\le L\) are false, since \(4^x>x\) for every \(x\) and \(B>L\).

docs.title: Elements of norm zero
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.rat_eq_zero_of_sq_sub_two_sq ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.intNorm_ne_zero

For \(u,v\in\mathbb Q\), if \(u^2-2v^2=0\) then \(u=v=0\). Equivalently, an element \(z\) of \(K_0\) with \(\operatorname N(z)=0\) is zero, and for \(Y\in\mathbb Z[s]\) with \(Y e0\) the integer \(\operatorname N(Y)=Y ar Y\) is nonzero. Hence every division by an element of \(K_0\) in the precision computation can be guarded by the exact test \(\operatorname N e0\) on integer components.

Proof sketch. If \(v e0\) then \((u/v)^2=2\), contradicting the irrationality of \(\sqrt2\). Equivalently, after clearing denominators a primitive integer solution of \(a^2=2b^2\) has \(a\) even, then \(b\) even, a contradiction. So \(v=0\) and then \(u=0\).

docs.title: Jacobian formulas on the weighted model
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.JTriple.curveE_jdbl ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.JTriple.curveE_jadd ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.JTriple.jdbl_affine ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.JTriple.jadd_affine ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.JTriple.jH_eq_zero_iff ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.JTriple.jΛ_eq_zero_iff ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.JTriple.rep_jdblB ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.JTriple.rep_jaddB

Let \(R\) be a commutative ring and \(A\in R\); write \(\mathcal E(X,Y,Z)=Y^2-X^3-AXZ^4\). Define the Jacobian doubling and addition $\(\mathrm{dbl}(X,Y,Z)=(M^2-2S,\ M(S-X_3)-8Y^4,\ 2YZ),\quad M=3X^2+AZ^4,\ S=4XY^2,\ X_3=M^2-2S,\)$ and, for \(P_1=(X_1,Y_1,Z_1)\), \(P_2=(X_2,Y_2,Z_2)\), with \(U_1=X_1Z_2^2\), \(U_2=X_2Z_1^2\), \(S_1=Y_1Z_2^3\), \(S_2=Y_2Z_1^3\), \(H=U_2-U_1\), \(\Lambda=S_2-S_1\), $\(\mathrm{add}(P_1,P_2)= igl(\Lambda^2-H^3-2U_1H^2,\ \Lambda(U_1H^2-X_3)-S_1H^3,\ HZ_1Z_2 igr),\)$ \(X_3\) being the first coordinate. Then the following polynomial identities hold:

  1. \(\mathcal E(\mathrm{dbl}(X,Y,Z))\) lies in the ideal generated by \(\mathcal E(X,Y,Z)\);
  2. \(\mathcal E(\mathrm{add}(P_1,P_2))\) lies in the ideal generated by \(\mathcal E(P_1)\) and \(\mathcal E(P_2)\);
  3. for doubling over a field of characteristic \( e2\) with \(YZ e0\), with \(x=X/Z^2\), \(y=Y/Z^3\) and \(\lambda=(3x^2+A)/(2y)=M/Z_3\) where \(Z_3=2YZ\): \(X_3/Z_3^2=\lambda^2-2x\), by the identity \(X_3=M^2-2xZ_3^2\) (as \(xZ_3^2=4XY^2=S\));
  4. \(Y_3/Z_3^3=\lambda(x-X_3/Z_3^2)-y\) for doubling, by the identity \(Y_3=M(XZ_3^2/Z^2-X_3)-8Y^4\) with \(Z_3^2/Z^2=4Y^2\);
  5. for addition over a field with \(Z_1Z_2H e0\), with \(x_i=X_i/Z_i^2\), \(y_i=Y_i/Z_i^3\) and \(\lambda=(y_2-y_1)/(x_2-x_1)=\Lambda/Z_3\): \(X_3/Z_3^2=\lambda^2-x_1-x_2\), by the identity \(X_3=\Lambda^2-H^2(U_1+U_2)\) and \((x_1+x_2)Z_3^2=(U_1+U_2)H^2\);
  6. \(Y_3/Z_3^3=\lambda(x_1-X_3/Z_3^2)-y_1\) for addition, by \(x_1Z_3^2=U_1H^2\) and \(y_1Z_3^3=S_1H^3\);
  7. (equal abscissas) over a field with \(Z_1Z_2 e0\): \(H=0\iff x_1=x_2\), and then \(\Lambda=0\iff y_1=y_2\); for points of the curve over a field of characteristic \( e2\), the sum is the doubling if \(\Lambda=0\) and the identity \(O\) otherwise (opposite points);
  8. (zero ordinate) over a field of characteristic \( e2\), if \(Y=0\) and \(Z e0\) the point has order two and its double is \(O\); negation is \((X,Y,Z)\mapsto(X,-Y,Z)\).

Together these say that the Jacobian formulas, with the branches 7 and 8 and \(Z=0\) for \(O\), compute the chord-and-tangent law of \(E\) on representatives. They are polynomial identities, independent of the generator theorem. That the fixed projective point is the affine \(P_0\) is the separate finite check on the fixed Jacobian point.

The manuscript reports nine polynomial identities for the nonexceptional projective formulas and the preservation of \(Y^2=X^3+AXZ^4\) without listing them; the list above is the set this chapter uses.

Proof sketch. Items 1-6 are identities in polynomial rings over \(\mathbb Z\), checked by ring normalization (items 1 and 2 with explicit cofactors, found by polynomial division by \(\mathcal E\)). Item 7: \(U_1=U_2\) iff \(x_1=x_2\) after dividing by \(Z_1^2Z_2^2\), and likewise for \(S_i\); on the curve, equal abscissas give \(y_2=\pm y_1\). Item 8 is \(-(x,0)=(x,0)\).

In \(\mathbb Z[s]\), \(s^2=2\), with \(A=-11243+7950s\), the triple $\((X_0,Y_0,Z_0)=(3282-2320s,\ -247440+174966s,\ 4)\)$ satisfies \(Y_0^2=X_0^3+AX_0Z_0^4\), and in \(K_0\) $\(\frac{X_0}{Z_0^2}=\frac{3282-2320s}{16}=\frac{1641-1160s}{8}=x(P_0),\qquad \frac{Y_0}{Z_0^3}=\frac{-247440+174966s}{64}=\frac{-123720+87483s}{32}=y(P_0).\)$ So the fixed projective point of the precision computation is the affine point \(P_0\).

This is a finite computation on six explicit integers: both sides of the curve equation equal \(122452755912-86587174080s\), and the two quotients are the displayed coordinates of \(P_0\) (\(3282=2\cdot1641\), \(2320=2\cdot1160\), \(247440=2\cdot123720\), \(174966=2\cdot87483\), \(Z_0^2=16\), \(Z_0^3=64\)). It does not use the generator theorem.

docs.title: Scalar multiplication by halving
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.rep_jmul ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.jmul_eq_some ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.admissible_iff_jmul

A Jacobian representative of a point of \(E(K_0)\) is a triple \((X,Y,Z)\in\mathbb Z[s]^3\) representing \(O\) when \(Z=0\) and the affine point \((X/Z^2,Y/Z^3)\) when \(Z e0\) (which then lies on \(E\) whenever \(\mathcal E(X,Y,Z)=0\)). Let \(\oplus\) be the branching addition: if one argument has \(Z=0\) return the other; otherwise compute \(H,\Lambda\); if \(H e0\) return \(\mathrm{add}\); if \(H=0\) and \(\Lambda=0\) return \(\mathrm{dbl}\) (or \(O\) if \(Y=0\)); if \(H=0\) and \(\Lambda e0\) return \(O\). Let \(\mathrm{dbl}^\ast\) be doubling with \(O\mapsto O\) and zero ordinate \(\mapsto O\).

For \(k\in\mathbb N\) define \(\mathrm{mul}(k)\) by the loop with state \((\Pi,\Theta,e)\) starting at \((O,P^{ m J}_0,k)\), where \(P^{ m J}_0=(3282-2320s,-247440+174966s,4)\) and \(O=(1,1,0)\): while \(e>0\), if \(e\) is odd replace \(\Pi\) by \(\Pi\oplus\Theta\); replace \(\Theta\) by \(\mathrm{dbl}^\ast(\Theta)\) and \(e\) by \(\lfloor e/2 floor\); return \(\Pi\). For a negative integer \(k\) let \(\mathrm{mul}(k)\) be the negation \((X,-Y,Z)\) of \(\mathrm{mul}(-k)\).

Then for every \(k\in\mathbb Z\) the loop terminates and \(\mathrm{mul}(k)\) is a Jacobian representative of \([k]P_0\) satisfying \(\mathcal E=0\); in particular \([k]P_0=O\) if and only if the third coordinate is \(0\), and otherwise its ordinate is zero if and only if the second coordinate is \(0\).

Proof sketch. Termination: \(e\) halves. Invariant: \(\Pi\) and \(\Theta\) represent points \(\pi, heta\) on \(E\) with \(\pi+[e] heta=[k]P_0\); it holds initially because \(O=(1,1,0)\) represents \(O\) and \(P^{ m J}_0\) represents \(P_0\) (the fixed Jacobian point) and is preserved because \(\oplus\) and \(\mathrm{dbl}^\ast\) represent the group law (Jacobian formulas, items 1-8): if \(e\) is odd, \(\pi+[e] heta=(\pi+ heta)+[e-1] heta\), and \([2\lfloor e/2 floor] heta=[\lfloor e/2 floor](2 heta)\). At \(e=0\), \(\pi=[k]P_0\). Negation represents \(-P\). The last claim: for \(Z e0\), \(y=Y/Z^3\).

docs.title: The exact decision program
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.decide5

The decision program is the total function \(\mathrm{decide}:\mathbb N^5 o\{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}\) computed by the following steps on \(c\in\mathbb N^5\); every quantity is an integer, an element of \(\mathbb Z[s]\) (a pair of integers) or a natural number, and every test is exact.

  1. Decode \((n,\kappa,a,l,j)\). Return false unless \(n otin\mathcal C\), \(\kappa e0\), \(a\ge1\), \(l\ge1\) and \(j=na\).
  2. For \(k\in\{l,a,j\}\) compute the Jacobian representative \((X_k,Y_k,Z_k)=\mathrm{mul}(k)\). Return false if some \(Z_k=0\) or some \(Y_k=0\).
  3. For \(k\in\{l,a,j\}\) put \( u_k=-X_kZ_k ar Y_k\in\mathbb Z[s]\) and \(N_k=Y_k ar Y_k\in\mathbb Z\), so that \(z_k= u_k/N_k\), with \(N_k e0\). Write \( u_l=p+p's\) and put \(U=|p|+|p'|\), \(V=|N_l|\), so that \(\epsilon_l=U/V\) with \(U,V>0\).
  4. Put \(\delta=N_j\operatorname N( u_a)\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}\) and let \( heta\) be the rational component of \( u_j ar u_aN_a\in\mathbb Z[s]\), so that \(r(a,j)= heta/\delta\). Return false unless \(| heta-n\delta|\cdot V<U\cdot|\delta|\).
  5. Put \(L=\lfloor(V-1)/(4U) floor\). Return false if \(L=0\). Otherwise, with \(M=|\kappa F(n)|\), compute \( eta=\mathrm{cmul}_L(\langle e_A angle_L,\mathrm{cpow}_L(\sigma_L(M),24))\) and run the division-by-four loop from \(L\) for \( eta\) steps; return true if and only if the final value is at least \(1\).

This is a definition. It follows the description of the reference program S21: exact quadratic-field arithmetic on integer pairs, capped integer operations, a halving scalar loop, a precision loop dividing by four and a bounded factorial iteration. The source S21 itself is not available in this repository, so this program is specified here rather than transcribed.

docs.title: Correctness of the decision program
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.decide5_iff ZInQ.Compiler.Precision.decideInt_iff

For every \(c\in\mathbb N^5\), \(\mathrm{decide}(c)=\mathrm{true}\iff\operatorname{accepts}(c)\). The program terminates on every input, including every early rejection.

Proof sketch. Step 1 is item 1 of the relation (signed decoding). Step 2: by the scalar-multiplication statement, \(Z_k=0\) iff \([k]P_0=O\) and, for \(Z_k e0\), \(Y_k=0\) iff the ordinate vanishes; so step 2 passes iff \(l,a,j\) are admissible. Step 3: \(z_k=-x/y=-X_kZ_k/Y_k= u_k/N_k\) with \(N_k=\operatorname N(Y_k) e0\) by the norm-zero statement; \(\epsilon_l=(|p|+|p'|)/|N_l|\), and \(U>0\) because \(z_l e0\). Step 4: \(z_j/z_a= u_j ar u_aN_a/(N_j\operatorname N( u_a))\), with \( u_a e0\) so \(\operatorname N( u_a) e0\); then \(| heta/\delta-n|<U/V\) is the displayed integer inequality after multiplying by \(|\delta|V>0\). Step 5: by the threshold statement, \(4\epsilon_l<4^{-\mathcal B}\) iff \(4^{\mathcal B}\le L\); if \(L=0\) this is false since \(4^{\mathcal B}\ge1\); if \(L\ge1\) the capped precision test computes exactly this comparison with \(\mathcal B=A^{(0)}_{ m ht}M^{24}\). Termination: the scalar loop halves, the factorial and capped-power loops are bounded, and the precision loop runs at most \(L+1\) steps.

docs.title: Programs, lowering and the wrapper
docs.text:
Register machines have increment, decrement-or-branch and halt instructions. A primitive program halts only at its last instruction; it accepts when it halts with every register zero.

The precision program is written in an ideal register language with natural arithmetic and structured control, whose semantics is a statement about terminating executions, not about a budgeted simulator. Lowering replaces each operation by a primitive block with fresh auxiliary registers; acceptance enters cleanup and rejection a permanent self-loop.

The precision program is built from verified routines for normalized signed integers, quadratic-field pairs, Jacobian points and capped arithmetic. It follows the decision program step by step.

The wrapper receives the five inputs as one Cantor code, inverts four pairs into registers zero to four with scratch above the precision machine's registers, and runs the relocated precision machine.

15 fully proved

docs.title: Register machines
docs.text:
ZInQ.Compiler.RM.Instr ZInQ.Compiler.RM.Machine ZInQ.Compiler.RM.Config ZInQ.Compiler.RM.step ZInQ.Compiler.RM.Halts ZInQ.Compiler.RM.Program ZInQ.Compiler.RM.Program.Valid ZInQ.Compiler.RM.Program.Accepts

Instructions. An instruction is \(\mathrm{inc}(j,x)\) (increment register \(j\), go to state \(x\)), \(\mathrm{dec}(j,x,y)\) (if register \(j\) is positive, decrement it and go to \(x\); otherwise go to \(y\)) or \(\mathrm{halt}\). Registers are indexed by \(\mathbb N\) and hold natural numbers; a register file is a map \(\rho:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\).

Machines and virtual halting. A machine is a map \(\mu:\mathbb N\to\) instructions. A configuration is a pair \((i,\rho)\) of a state and a register file; the step relation executes \(\mu(i)\) and is undefined at a halt instruction. The run of \(\mu\) from \((0,\rho_0)\) halts if it reaches, after finitely many steps, a state \(i\) with \(\mu(i)=\mathrm{halt}\).

Primitive programs. A primitive program is a list \(p=(p_0,\dots,p_{m-1})\), \(m\ge1\), of instructions. It is valid for \(r\) registers if \(p_{m-1}=\mathrm{halt}\), no other instruction is a halt, every register index is below \(r\) and every target is below \(m\). It induces the machine with \(\mu(i)=p_i\) for \(i<m\) and \(\mu(i)=\mathrm{halt}\) for \(i\ge m\). For \(k\le r\) and inputs \(a\in\mathbb N^k\) the initial file has \(\rho_0(i)=a_i\) for \(i<k\) and \(0\) otherwise. A valid \(p\)

  • halts on \(a\) if its run from \((0,\rho_0)\) reaches the final state \(m-1\);
  • accepts \(a\) if its run reaches the final state \(m-1\) with every register zero.

The number of add instructions (increments), sub instructions (decrements) and registers \(r\) are the shape of \(p\). Since a valid program halts only at its final state, a run reaches it at most once and then stops.

This is a definition. Acceptance is the convention of the packed compiler; halting is the convention of the universal numbering; a cleanup stage that clears every register before the final halt converts the second into the first.
