docs.title: The finite specification of the polynomial
The finite specification of the polynomial
docs.text:
The target polynomial \(P_*\) is defined by construction. It is a finite composition of existential polynomial gadgets: a template is a polynomial in parameter and witness variables, a call substitutes parameter polynomials and moves the callee's witnesses into a fresh private block of the caller, a sum of squares expresses conjunction over \(\mathbb Q\), and a product expresses disjunction. A few astronomically large integers and finite polynomials enter through three constructors whose values are never expanded. This chapter defines the expression language and its semantics, proves the semantic lemmas that make the gadgets behave as intended, defines every template, recipe, constant and constructor of the manuscript's specification exactly, and defines \(P_*\) with its witness accounting. Whether each template expresses its intended relation is proved in the chapters that use it; the inventory at the end says where.

11 fully proved

docs.title: The expression language
docs.text:
Scalar nodes, templates, calls with witness blocks and recipes denote integer polynomials.

Over \(\mathbb Q\) a sum of squares vanishes exactly when every term does, and a product when some factor does. Inverses are equations \(uv=1\), and pairs of rationals represent the arithmetic of \(K_0=\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)\) faithfully.

Formulas, the template constructions that compile them, the scope of private witness blocks, rational constants, positivity, absolute value and point references are developed in their own section.

  • Formulas, gadgets and witness scope

docs.title: Semantics of templates and recipes
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.Template.denote ZInQ.Syntax.Recipe.denote ZInQ.Syntax.ExPoly.Rel

Polynomials live in \(\mathbb Z[X_i : i\in\mathbb N]\) and every variable ranges over \(\mathbb Q\). A rational assignment is a map \(x:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Q\), and \(f(x)\) is the value of \(f\) at it.

Scalar nodes. A node list \(n_0,\dots,n_{k-1}\) is a finite list in which every node refers only to earlier nodes. A node is one of:

  • \(\mathrm{const}\ c\) with \(c\in\mathbb Z\);
  • \(\mathrm{var}\ i\) with \(i\in\mathbb N\) a local variable;
  • \(\mathrm{add}\ j\ j'\) or \(\mathrm{mul}\ j\ j'\) with \(j,j'\) earlier nodes;
  • \(\mathrm{call}\ \tau\ (a_0,\dots,a_{p-1})\ w\): a call of an earlier template \(\tau\) with \(p\) parameters, parameter nodes \(a_i\) and witness start \(w\in\mathbb N\);
  • \(\mathrm{fixed}\ e\) with \(e\) a fixed integer expression;
  • \(\mathrm{psi}\ e\ (a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3)\ c\) with \(e\) a fixed integer expression and \(c\in\{0,1\}\);
  • \(\mathrm{guard}\ e\ (a_1,\dots,a_{15})\) with \(e\) a fixed integer expression and fifteen coordinate nodes in point-major order.

Templates. A template \(\tau=(p,v,n_0,\dots,n_{k-1},\mathrm{root})\) has parameter count \(p\le v\) and variable count \(v\); its local variables \(0,\dots,p-1\) are parameters and \(p,\dots,v-1\) are its \(m=v-p\) witnesses. Node values are polynomials: \([\![\mathrm{const}\ c]\!]=c\), \([\![\mathrm{var}\ i]\!]=X_i\), \([\![\mathrm{add}\ j\ j']\!]=[\![n_j]\!]+[\![n_{j'}]\!]\), \([\![\mathrm{mul}\ j\ j']\!]=[\![n_j]\!][\![n_{j'}]\!]\), \([\![\mathrm{fixed}\ e]\!]\) is the constant \(\mathrm{val}(e)\), \([\![\mathrm{psi}\ e\ a\ c]\!]=\Psi_{\mathrm{val}(e),c}([\![n_{a_0}]\!],\dots,[\![n_{a_3}]\!])\), \([\![\mathrm{guard}\ e\ a]\!]=G_{\mathrm{val}(e)}([\![n_{a_1}]\!],\dots,[\![n_{a_{15}}]\!])\) and \([\![\mathrm{call}\ \tau'\ a\ w]\!]=\tau'[[\![n_{a_0}]\!],\dots,[\![n_{a_{p'-1}}]\!];w]\). The polynomial of \(\tau\) is \([\![\tau]\!]=[\![n_{\mathrm{root}}]\!]\).

Calls. For a template or recipe \(\tau\) with \(p\) parameters, polynomials \(g_0,\dots,g_{p-1}\) and \(w\in\mathbb N\), the call \(\tau[g_0,\dots,g_{p-1};w]\) is the image of \([\![\tau]\!]\) under the ring homomorphism with \(X_i\mapsto g_i\) for \(i<p\) and \(X_i\mapsto X_{w+i-p}\) for \(i\ge p\). Thus witness \(p+j\) of the callee becomes the caller's variable \(X_{w+j}\).

Relations. For \(a\in\mathbb Q^p\), \(\mathrm{Rel}_\tau(a)\) holds when there are \(y_0,\dots,y_{m-1}\in\mathbb Q\) with \([\![\tau]\!]\,(a_0,\dots,a_{p-1},y_0,\dots,y_{m-1})=0\) (variables of index at least \(v\) set to \(0\)).

Recipes. A recipe \(\rho\) has parameter count \(p\), variable count \(v\) and a list of constraint polynomials \(c_1,\dots,c_k\); its polynomial is \([\![\rho]\!]=\sum_i c_i^2\) for a sum-of-squares recipe or a model-evaluation recipe and \([\![\rho]\!]=\prod_i c_i\) for a product recipe (empty sum \(0\), empty product \(1\)). Calls and relations of recipes are as for templates.

  • A composition recipe lists calls \((\kappa_i,(j_{i,0},\dots,j_{i,p_i-1}),w_i)\), where \(\kappa_i\) is a template or an earlier recipe with \(p_i\) parameters; its constraints are \(c_i=\kappa_i[X_{j_{i,0}},\dots,X_{j_{i,p_i-1}};w_i]\). It also records ranges of fresh variables, which add no constraint.
  • A model-evaluation recipe records generator indices \(g_0,g_1,g_2\), source variable rows \((r,s)\) with a point reference \(r\) and a natural start \(s\) or none, constant definitions \((\sigma,r,s)\) with a scalar template \(\sigma\), operations \((0,a,b,o,s)\), \((1,a,b,o,s)\) and \((2,a,b,c,o,s)\), and a root equality \((r,r')\), together with operation templates \(\nu\) (natural), \(\alpha\) (raw addition), \(\mu\) (multiplication) and possibly a power recipe \(\pi\). Writing \(\mathrm{ref}(r)\) for the five polynomials of a point reference and juxtaposing references for the concatenated coordinate lists, its constraints are, in this order: the three generator constraints \(8X_{g_0}-1641\), \(4X_{g_1}+15465\), \(32X_{g_2}-87483\); \(\nu[\mathrm{ref}(r);s]\) for each row with a natural start \(s\); \(\sigma[\mathrm{ref}(-2)\,\mathrm{ref}(r);s]\) for each constant definition; \(\alpha[\mathrm{ref}(a)\,\mathrm{ref}(b)\,\mathrm{ref}(o);s]\), \(\mu[\mathrm{ref}(a)\,\mathrm{ref}(b)\,\mathrm{ref}(o);s]\) and \(\pi[\mathrm{ref}(a)\,\mathrm{ref}(b)\,\mathrm{ref}(c)\,\mathrm{ref}(o);s]\) for the operations of kinds \(0\), \(1\) and \(2\); and the five differences \(\mathrm{ref}(r)_i-\mathrm{ref}(r')_i\).

The order of summands does not change the polynomial; the order listed follows the specification's description of model recipes. Source node numbers, source-node point lists, names, metadata and provenance strings carry no constraints.

This is a definition. The denotation of a node list is computed by one pass in stored order, keeping the polynomial of every node; a call refers to an earlier template, so the library is denoted in its stored order. The values \(\mathrm{val}(e)\), \(\Psi_{n,c}\) and \(G_T\) are used only as symbols in all later reasoning; in particular \(\mathrm{val}(e)\) is never evaluated for the astronomical constants.

docs.title: Sums of squares and products over the rationals
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.Formula.ev_compile_eq_zero_iff ZInQ.Syntax.ev_sum_sq_eq_zero_iff ZInQ.Syntax.ev_prod_eq_zero_iff

For every formula \(\varphi\) and every \(x:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Q\), $\(\kappa(\varphi)(x)=0\iff\varphi\text{ holds at }x .\)$ In particular, for polynomials \(f_1,\dots,f_k\), \(\sum_i f_i(x)^2=0\iff f_1(x)=\dots=f_k(x)=0\) and \(\prod_i f_i(x)=0\iff f_i(x)=0\) for some \(i\).

Proof sketch. Induction on \(\varphi\). For an atom, \(\kappa(a\doteq b)(x)=a(x)-b(x)\). For a conjunction, each square is a nonnegative rational, so a finite sum of squares vanishes exactly when every square vanishes, and \(t^2=0\iff t=0\); the empty sum is \(0\) and the empty conjunction is true. For a disjunction, \(\mathbb Q\) has no zero divisors, so a finite product vanishes exactly when a factor does; the empty product is \(1\ne0\) and the empty disjunction is false.

docs.title: Inverse witnesses
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.exists_mul_eq_one_iff ZInQ.Syntax.exists_mul_pairNorm_eq_one_iff

Inverses are expressed by equations \(uv=1\), never by partial division.

  1. For \(a\in\mathbb Q\): \(a e0\iff\exists w\in\mathbb Q,\ aw=1\), and then \(w=1/a\).
  2. For \(a_0,a_1\in\mathbb Q\) and \(s=\sqrt2\): \(a_0+a_1s e0\iff a_0^2-2a_1^2 e0\iff \exists w\in\mathbb Q,\ (a_0^2-2a_1^2)\,w=1\).

Consequently the gadget \(\mathrm{NZ}(a)\) is satisfiable by a choice of its fresh variable exactly when \(a e0\), and \(\mathrm{NZ}(a_0^2-2a_1^2)\) exactly when the pair \((a_0,a_1)\) is not \((0,0)\).

Proof sketch. Part 1 is the field structure of \(\mathbb Q\). For part 2, if \(a_0^2=2a_1^2\) with \(a_1 e0\) then \((a_0/a_1)^2=2\), contradicting the irrationality of \(\sqrt2\); so \(a_0^2-2a_1^2=0\) forces \(a_1=0\) and then \(a_0=0\). Conversely \((0,0)\) has norm \(0\). Then apply part 1 to the norm. Since \(1,s\) are linearly independent over \(\mathbb Q\), \(a_0+a_1s=0\) exactly when \(a_0=a_1=0\).

docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.Pair.val ZInQ.Syntax.holds_feq ZInQ.Syntax.holds_curve

For a rational pair \(u=(u_0,u_1)\) write \([u]=u_0+u_1s\in K_0\). For rational pairs \(u,u'\) and an integer \(k\):

  1. \([u+u']=[u]+[u']\), \([-u]=-[u]\), \([ku]=k[u]\), \([u\cdot u']=[u][u']\), \([ ar u]=\sigma[u]\) where \(\sigma\) is the conjugation \(s\mapsto-s\), and \(N(u)=[u]\,\sigma[u]\in\mathbb Q\);
  2. \(u\doteq u'\) holds exactly when \([u]=[u']\);
  3. \(\mathrm{NZ}_K(u)\) is satisfiable by its fresh variable exactly when \([u] e0\);
  4. \(\mathrm{Div}(n,d)\) holds for some value of its fresh variables with value \(q\) exactly when \([d] e0\) and \([q]=[n]/[d]\);
  5. for a rational point code \(p\) and pairs \(\zeta\), \(v\): \(Z(p,\zeta)\) holds for some value of its fresh variable exactly when either \(p=O\) and \([\zeta]=0\), or \(p_0=0\), \([y(p)] e0\) and \([\zeta]=-[x(p)]/[y(p)]\); and \(I\!X(p,v)\) holds exactly when either \(p=O\) and \([v]=0\), or \(p_0=0\) and \([x(p)][v]=1\).

Proof sketch. Part 1 is \(s^2=2\) and the definition of \(\sigma\). Part 2 is the linear independence of \(1,s\) over \(\mathbb Q\). Part 3 is the inverse-witness statement for pairs. Part 4 combines 2 and 3 with \([d][q]=[n]\). Part 5 unfolds the two disjunctions with the compilation theorem; the branches are exclusive because \(p_0=1\) in the first and \(p_0=0\) in the second.

docs.title: Fixed constants and division polynomials
docs.text:
The fixed integer constants, the prime catalogue, the least formal multiple and the false-triple product form one section.

  • Fixed constants and the guard product

The constructor psi_component inserts one coordinate of a normalized division polynomial. The normalized recurrences agree with the classical division polynomials; the classical multiplication-by-\(n\) formulas, stated as a proposition, give the fixed-scalar ordinate equation \(2y([n]P)\psi_n(P)^4=\psi_{2n}(P)\), and with it the meaning of the fixed-scalar templates on \(2E(K_0)\).

docs.title: Normalized division polynomials and their components
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.normDiv ZInQ.Syntax.divPsi ZInQ.Syntax.psiComponent

Let \(R\) be a commutative ring and \(A\in R\). The normalized division polynomials \(f_n\in R[x]\), \(n\ge0\), of \(y^2=x^3+Ax\) are defined by $\(f_0=0,\quad f_1=f_2=1,\quad f_3=3x^4+6Ax^2-A^2,\quad f_4=2(x^6+5Ax^4-5A^2x^2-A^3),\)$ and, for larger indices, $\(f_{2m}=f_m\bigl(f_{m+2}f_{m-1}^2-f_{m-2}f_{m+1}^2\bigr)\qquad(m\ge3),\)$ $\(f_{2m+1}=\begin{cases}D_0L-R_m,& m\text{ even},\\ L-D_0R_m,& m\text{ odd},\end{cases}\qquad(m\ge2),\)$ where \(L=f_{m+2}f_m^3\), \(R_m=f_{m-1}f_{m+1}^3\) and \(D_0=16(x^3+Ax)^2\). The recursion terminates because every index on the right is smaller than the index on the left for \(n\ge5\). The division polynomials \(\psi_n\in R[x,y]\), \(n\in\mathbb Z\), are $\(\psi_n=f_n\ (n\ge0\text{ odd}),\qquad\psi_n=2y\,f_n\ (n\ge0\text{ even}),\qquad\psi_{-n}=-\psi_n .\)$

Components. Take \(R=\mathbb Z[x_0,x_1,y_0,y_1][s]/(s^2-2)\), whose elements are pairs over \(\mathbb Z[x_0,x_1,y_0,y_1]\) with the pair product \((a,b)(c,d)=(ac+2bd,ad+bc)\), and \(A=-11243+7950s\). For \(n\in\mathbb Z\) and \(c\in\{0,1\}\), the component polynomial \(\Psi_{n,c}\in\mathbb Z[x_0,x_1,y_0,y_1]\) is the coefficient of \(s^c\) in \(\psi_n(x_0+x_1s,\ y_0+y_1s)\). The constructor \(\mathrm{psi}\ e\ (a_0,\dots,a_3)\ c\) denotes \(\Psi_{\mathrm{val}(e),c}\) evaluated at the polynomials of its four argument nodes.

The index of every occurring component is a fixed integer expression (\(n\), \(n+1\), \(n-1\) or \(2n\) for a fixed index \(n\) of a scalar template); the polynomials \(\Psi_{n,c}\) for the astronomical index \(c_*\) are never expanded, and every statement about them is proved from the recurrences.

docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.normDiv_eq_preΨ' ZInQ.Syntax.divPsi_eq_Ψ ZInQ.Syntax.mk_divPsi ZInQ.Syntax.psiEval_eq_evalEval_ψ

Let \(R\) be a commutative ring, \(A\in R\), and let \(W_A\) be the Weierstrass curve \(y^2=x^3+Ax\) (\(a_1=a_2=a_3=a_6=0\), \(a_4=A\)), so that \(b_2=b_6=0\), \(b_4=2A\), \(b_8=-A^2\). Let \(\mathrm{pre}\Psi_n\in R[x]\) and \(\Psi_n\in R[x,y]\) (\(n\in\mathbb Z\)) be the classical normalized division polynomials of \(W_A\): \(\mathrm{pre}\Psi_n\) is the normalized elliptic divisibility sequence with initial values \(0,1,1,\Psi_3,\mathrm{pre}\Psi_4\) and parameter \((\Psi_2^{\rm Sq})^2\), where \(\Psi_2^{\rm Sq}=4x^3+b_2x^2+2b_4x+b_6\), \(\Psi_3=3x^4+b_2x^3+3b_4x^2+3b_6x+b_8\), and \(\mathrm{pre}\Psi_4=2x^6+b_2x^5+5b_4x^4+10b_6x^3+10b_8x^2+(b_2b_8-b_4b_6)x+(b_4b_8-b_6^2)\); and \(\Psi_n=\mathrm{pre}\Psi_n\cdot2y\) for even \(n\), \(\Psi_n=\mathrm{pre}\Psi_n\) for odd \(n\). Then $\(f_n=\mathrm{pre}\Psi_n\ \ (n\ge0),\qquad \psi_n=\Psi_n\ \ (n\in\mathbb Z).\)$ Moreover \(\Psi_n\) agrees with the classical bivariate division polynomial modulo the curve equation, so the two take the same values at every point of \(W_A\).

Proof sketch. For \(W_A\): \(\Psi_2^{\rm Sq}=4(x^3+Ax)\), so \((\Psi_2^{\rm Sq})^2=D_0\); \(\Psi_3=3x^4+6Ax^2-A^2=f_3\); and \(\mathrm{pre}\Psi_4=2x^6+10Ax^4-10A^2x^2-2A^3=f_4\). The normalized sequence satisfies \(\mathrm{pre}\Psi_{2m}=\mathrm{pre}\Psi_{m-1}^2\mathrm{pre}\Psi_m\mathrm{pre}\Psi_{m+2} -\mathrm{pre}\Psi_{m-2}\mathrm{pre}\Psi_m\mathrm{pre}\Psi_{m+1}^2\) and \(\mathrm{pre}\Psi_{2m+1}=\mathrm{pre}\Psi_{m+2}\mathrm{pre}\Psi_m^3\cdot\epsilon_m-\mathrm{pre}\Psi_{m-1}\mathrm{pre}\Psi_{m+1}^3\cdot\epsilon_m'\) with \((\epsilon_m,\epsilon'_m)=(D_0,1)\) for even \(m\) and \((1,D_0)\) for odd \(m\), which are the recurrences of \(f_n\). Strong induction on \(n\) gives \(f_n=\mathrm{pre}\Psi_n\); the formulas for \(\psi_n\) and \(\Psi_n\), including \(\psi_{-n}=-\psi_n\) and the oddness of the sequence, then agree. The final assertion is the classical congruence between the two bivariate families in the coordinate ring.

docs.title: The multiplication-by-n formulas
docs.text:
ZInQ.DivisionPolynomialMultiplication

This article states, as a proposition, the classical formulas for multiplication by \(n\) on \(E:y^2=x^3-d^2x\) over \(K_0\) (so \(A=-d^2=-11243+7950s\)). The proposition asserts: for every affine point \(P=(x,y)\in E(K_0)\) and every integer \(n\ne0\),

  1. \([n]P=O\) if and only if \(\psi_n(x,y)=0\);
  2. if \([n]P\ne O\), then $\(x([n]P)=x-\frac{\psi_{n+1}(x,y)\,\psi_{n-1}(x,y)}{\psi_n(x,y)^2},\qquad y([n]P)=\frac{\psi_{2n}(x,y)}{2\,\psi_n(x,y)^4}.\)$

Equivalently \(x([n]P)=\phi_n/\psi_n^2\) and \(y([n]P)=\omega_n/\psi_n^3\) with \(\phi_n=x\psi_n^2-\psi_{n+1}\psi_{n-1}\), \(\omega_n=(\psi_{n+2}\psi_{n-1}^2-\psi_{n-2}\psi_{n+1}^2)/(4y)\) and \(\psi_{2n}=2\psi_n\omega_n\); the second formula is the fixed-scalar ordinate equation \(2y([n]P)\psi_n(P)^4=\psi_{2n}(P)\).

This is classical (Sutherland §§5.5-5.6, Lemmas 5.20 and 5.24 and Theorem 5.21; Silverman, Exercise 3.7; Washington, Theorem 9.33) for every elliptic curve in short Weierstrass form over a field of characteristic \(0\). It enters the proof only through the fixed-scalar templates. This article fixes the statement as a proposition; the elliptic-model chapter proves it as a background theorem, and the fixed-scalar semantics uses that theorem. Its formal proof is a substantial project independent of this manuscript.

docs.title: Semantics of the fixed-scalar templates
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.scalarTemplate_rel_iff_pointCode ZInQ.Syntax.scalarTemplate_rel_iff_iota

Let \(e\) be a fixed integer expression with \(n=\mathrm{val}(e)\ge1\), let \(p\) be the code of a point \(P\in2E(K_0)\) and \(r\in\mathbb Q^5\). Then $\(\mathrm{Rel}_{S_e}(p,r)\iff r ext{ is the code of }[n]P .\)$ In particular, on codes of \(2E(K_0)=\mathbb ZP_0\), \(\mathrm{Rel}_{S_e}(\iota(a),r)\iff r=\iota(na)\).

Proof sketch. By the compilation theorem the polynomial vanishes exactly when one of the two branches holds. If \(P=O\) then \(p_0=1\), the second branch fails, and the first holds exactly when \(r=O=[n]O\). If \(P e O\) the first branch fails since \(p_0=0\). As \(2E(K_0)=\mathbb ZP_0\) with \(P_0\) of infinite order, \([n]P e O\), so by the multiplication formulas \(\psi_n(P) e0\) and \([n]P=(x-\psi_{n+1}\psi_{n-1}/\psi_n^2,\ \psi_{2n}/(2\psi_n^4))\), where the components of \(\psi_k(P)\) are \(\Psi_{k,0},\Psi_{k,1}\) evaluated at the coordinates of \(p\). By the pair arithmetic, the inverse witness exists exactly because \(\psi_n(P) e0\), and the two pair equations, after division by \(\psi_n^2 e0\) and \(2\psi_n^4 e0\), say that \(x(r)\) and \(y(r)\) are the coordinates of \([n]P\), while \(r_0=0\) says \(r\) is affine. Clearing these denominators is reversible.

docs.title: The template library
docs.text:
The two basic elliptic templates express membership in \(2E(K_0)\) and raw addition of canonical codes.

The remaining templates (local parameter, inverse abscissa, logarithm, pole, the multiplication certificate, the guard, multiplication, natural codes and the value templates) and the ordered library are in their own section.

docs.title: The membership template
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.memberTemplate ZInQ.Syntax.memberTemplate_rel_iff

The template \(\mathtt{member}\) has \(5\) parameters and \(7\) witnesses (\(12\) variables). Its variables are: the point \(p=(X_0,\dots,X_4)\); the pairs \(X=(X_5,X_6)\), \(Y=(X_7,X_8)\) and \(H=(X_9,X_{10})\); and the inverse witness \(u=X_{11}\) of \(\mathrm{NZ}_K(Y)\). With \(x_P=H^2-2X\) and \(y_P=H\cdot(X-x_P)-Y\), its formula is $\(\varphi_{\rm member}=\bigvee\Bigl(\mathrm{isO}(p),\ \bigwedge\bigl(\mathrm{fin}(p),\ \mathrm{curve}(X,Y),\ N(Y)\,u\doteq1,\ (2Y)\cdot H\doteq3X^2+A,\ x(p)\doteq x_P,\ y(p)\doteq y_P\bigr)\Bigr),\)$ and, having no rational constants, its polynomial is \([\![\mathtt{member}]\!]=\kappa(\varphi_{\rm member})^2\).

The second branch says: \((X,Y)\in E(K_0)\) with \(Y\ne0\), \(H\) is the tangent slope at \((X,Y)\), and \(p\) is the code of the affine point \(2(X,Y)\). That \(\mathrm{Rel}_{\mathtt{member}}(p)\) holds exactly for the codes of points of \(2E(K_0)\) is the membership statement of the model chapter.

docs.title: The raw addition template
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.rawAddTemplate ZInQ.Syntax.rawAddTemplate_rel_iff

The template \(\mathtt{raw\_add}\) has \(15\) parameters and \(6\) witnesses (\(21\) variables). Its variables are the points \(p=(X_0,\dots,X_4)\), \(q=(X_5,\dots,X_9)\), \(r=(X_{10},\dots,X_{14})\), the slope pairs \(m_g=(X_{15},X_{16})\) and \(m_d=(X_{17},X_{18})\), and the inverse witnesses \(u_g=X_{19}\), \(u_d=X_{20}\). Write \(x=x(p)\), \(y=y(p)\), \(x'=x(q)\), \(y'=y(q)\), \(\mathrm{both}=\bigwedge(\mathrm{fin}(p),\mathrm{fin}(q))\) and, for a slope pair \(m\), $\(\mathrm{out}(m)=\bigwedge\bigl(\mathrm{fin}(r),\ x(r)\doteq m^2-x-x',\ y(r)\doteq m\cdot(x-x_r)-y\bigr),\qquad x_r=m^2-x-x'.\)$ The formula is the disjunction of five branches, in this order: $\(\varphi_{\rm add}=\bigvee(\beta_1,\beta_2,\beta_3,\beta_4,\beta_5),\)$ $\(\beta_1=\bigwedge(\mathrm{isO}(p),\ \mathrm{eq}(q,r)),\qquad \beta_2=\bigwedge(\mathrm{fin}(p),\ \mathrm{isO}(q),\ \mathrm{eq}(p,r)),\)$ $\(\beta_3=\bigwedge(\mathrm{both},\ x\doteq x',\ y\doteq-y',\ \mathrm{isO}(r)),\)$ $\(\beta_4=\bigwedge\bigl(\mathrm{both},\ N(x'-x)\,u_g\doteq1,\ (x'-x)\cdot m_g\doteq y'-y,\ \mathrm{out}(m_g)\bigr),\)$ $\(\beta_5=\bigwedge\bigl(\mathrm{both},\ x\doteq x',\ y\doteq y',\ N(y)\,u_d\doteq1,\ (2y)\cdot m_d\doteq3x^2+A,\ \mathrm{out}(m_d)\bigr).\)$ Its polynomial is \([\![\mathtt{raw\_add}]\!]=\kappa(\varphi_{\rm add})^2\).

The branches cover both identities, opposite points, distinct abscissas and doubling with nonzero ordinate. The contract \(\mathrm{Add}_{\rm raw}(\iota(a),\iota(b),r)\iff r=\iota(a+b)\) is proved in the model chapter.

docs.title: The specified polynomial
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.PstarNatOf ZInQ.Syntax.PstarOf ZInQ.Syntax.Pstar ZInQ.Syntax.specPstar

The specified polynomial is $\(P_*\in\mathbb Z[X_0,X_1,\dots,X_{292890231904}],\)$ the polynomial \([\![\mathtt{integers}]\!]\) of the root recipe of the construction, with every variable of index above \(292890231904\) replaced by \(0\) (by the witness accounting, no such variable occurs, so nothing is replaced). Unfolding the root, $\(P_*=\mathtt{value}[X_1,X_2,X_3,X_4,X_5,X_0;6]^2 ,\)$ where \(\mathtt{value}\) is the composition \(\mathtt{member}\) and \(\mathtt{value.exceptions}\times\mathtt{main}\), \(\mathtt{main}\) combines \(\mathtt{close}\) and \(\mathtt{value.test}\), and \(\mathtt{close}\) combines five signed encodings, the precision recipe and the coordinate window. Variable \(X_0\) is the external rational input; the code \((X_1,\dots,X_5)\) and all further variables are its rational witnesses.

\(P_*\) is defined in this blueprint by construction: every template, recipe, fixed constant and constructor is the term described in this chapter, and the natural precision circuit is the output of the compiler chapter. The manuscript's saved specification is compared with this construction by an external script and is not used in the proof. Its constants are kept symbolic: the polynomial is never expanded, and the constants \(c_*\), \(\ell\), \(T\), \(D\) and the program literal \(c_3\) occur only through their defining expressions.

docs.title: Cross-check against the saved specification
docs.text:
The manuscript ships its specification as a saved expression with the same 23 templates and seven recipes. It is not an input to the proof; an external comparison checks that the construction of this chapter reproduces it:

  1. the fixed-constant expressions are compared as expression trees, and the two decimal literals with the primorial values;
  2. each template is compared by parameter count, variable count and witness blocks exactly, and by its polynomial through a randomized identity test: both node lists are evaluated modulo a large prime at random points, with each constructor node replaced by a random function of its index expression and argument values, shared by both sides;
  3. the recipes are compared record by record: generator indices, source variable rows, constant definitions, operations, root equality, composition calls and fresh ranges.

The comparison uses a small sample of points per template and never expands a constructor.

docs.title: Fixed constants and the guard product
Fixed constants and the guard product
docs.text:
A fixed integer expression is built from literals, references, arithmetic, powers, maxima, factorials, the prime catalogue and the least formal multiple. Its value is a constant, never a quantified witness, and the astronomical values are never computed.

The specification binds eighteen named constants, from the primorial \(P_s\) through the guard cutoff \(T\); only the two primorial literals are checked numerically.

The constructor finite_guard_product inserts the product, over the false triples \((a,b,c)\in[-T,T]^3\) with \(ab\ne c\), of the denominator-cleared squared distances to \((\iota(a),\iota(b),\iota(c))\).

6 fully proved

docs.title: The prime catalogue
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.cataloguePrime ZInQ.Syntax.catalogueProduct ZInQ.Syntax.catalogueMax

Let \(W\ge1\), \(k\ge0\) and \(B\ge0\) be integers. For each residue \(r\) with \(1\le r<W\) and \(\gcd(r,W)=1\), let \(p_{r,1}<p_{r,2}<\dots<p_{r,k}\) be the first \(k\) primes \(p\) with \(p>B\) and \(p\equiv r\pmod W\). Define $\(\mathrm{catalogue\_product}(W,k,B)=\prod_{r}\prod_{j=1}^kp_{r,j},\qquad \mathrm{catalogue\_max}(W,k,B)=\max_{r,j}p_{r,j},\)$ with the maximum of an empty family equal to \(0\). The fixed catalogue of the manuscript is \(W=4\prod_{p\le324}p\), \(k=22\), \(B=324\): the first twenty-two primes above \(324\) in every unit residue class modulo \(W\). Its product is \(H_{\rm cat}\) and its maximum \(H_{\max}\).

The primes \(p_{r,j}\) exist by Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions. The definition takes \(p_{r,j}\) to be the \(j\)-th element, in increasing order, of the set of primes \(p>B\) with \(p\equiv r\pmod W\); Dirichlet's theorem shows this set is infinite, so the elements listed are the intended primes. Neither \(H_{\rm cat}\) nor \(H_{\max}\) is evaluated; the catalogue bound hypothesis controls \(H_{\max}\).

This is a definition.

docs.title: The least formal multiple
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.normalizedRep ZInQ.Syntax.xi ZInQ.Syntax.FormalCondition ZInQ.Syntax.leastFormalMultiple

Every \(u\in K_0\) has a unique normalized representation \(u=(a+bs)/c\) with \(a,b,c\in\mathbb Z\), \(c>0\) and \(\gcd(a,b,c)=1\) (for \(u=0\) this is \((0,0,1)\)). For a point \(Q\) of \(E(K_0)\) put \(\xi(Q)=1/x(Q)\) if \(Q\ne O\) and \(x(Q)\ne0\), and \(\xi(Q)=0\) otherwise.

For an integer \(N\ge1\), the least formal multiple \(\mathrm{LFM}(N)\) is the least \(m\ge1\) such that the normalized representation \((a,b,c)\) of \(\xi([m]P_0)\) satisfies $\(N^4\mid a,\qquad N^4\mid b,\qquad \gcd(c,N)=1 .\)$ If no such \(m\) exists, \(\mathrm{LFM}(N)=0\); this convention only makes the definition total, and the existence of a successful index for the fixed \(N_s\) is proved with the cutoff in Section 12. The fixed constant \(M_0=\mathrm{LFM}(N_s)\) is never evaluated.

Since \(P_0\) has infinite order, \([m]P_0\) is never \(O\) or a point of order two for \(m\ge1\), so the conventions for \(\xi\) at those points are never used for \(P_0\); they match the specification's rule that the identity has inverse abscissa zero.

docs.title: Fixed integer expressions
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.FixedExpr ZInQ.Syntax.FixedExpr.val

A fixed integer expression is built from

  • integer literals;
  • references to earlier named fixed constants;
  • \(\mathrm{add}(e_1,e_2)\), \(\mathrm{mul}(e_1,e_2)\), \(\mathrm{pow}(e_1,e_2)\);
  • \(\max(e_1,\dots,e_k)\) with \(k\ge1\);
  • \(\mathrm{factorial}(e)\);
  • \(\mathrm{catalogue\_product}(e_W,e_k,e_B)\) and \(\mathrm{catalogue\_max}(e_W,e_k,e_B)\);
  • \(\mathrm{least\_formal\_multiple}(e_N)\).

Its value \(\mathrm{val}(e)\in\mathbb Z\) is defined recursively: literals are themselves, a reference is the value of the named constant, \(\mathrm{add}\) and \(\mathrm{mul}\) are \(+\) and \(\times\), \(\mathrm{pow}(e_1,e_2)=\mathrm{val}(e_1)^{\mathrm{val}(e_2)}\) (the specification uses only nonnegative exponents; to make the definition total a negative exponent is replaced by \(0\), so the power is then \(1\)), \(\max\) is the maximum, \(\mathrm{factorial}(e)=\mathrm{val}(e)!\) (with \(n!=1\) for \(n\le0\)), the catalogue operators are the catalogue product and maximum of the prime catalogue with modulus \(\mathrm{val}(e_W)\), count \(\mathrm{val}(e_k)\) and floor \(\mathrm{val}(e_B)\), and \(\mathrm{least\_formal\_multiple}(e_N)\) is the least formal multiple of \(\mathrm{val}(e_N)\). Negative arguments of the last three operators do not occur; they are read through the natural-number truncation.

These expressions produce constants, not quantified witnesses, and none of the astronomical ones is ever evaluated: every later statement about them is proved symbolically from these defining equations.

docs.title: The finite false-triple product
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.guardPoly ZInQ.Syntax.guardPoly_eval_eq_zero_iff

For an integer \(T\ge0\), a triple \((a,b,c)\in\mathbb Z^3\) is a false triple in the box if \(|a|,|b|,|c|\le T\) and \(ab\ne c\). For such a triple write the fifteen coordinates of \((\iota(a),\iota(b),\iota(c))\), in point-major order, as reduced fractions \(A_j/B_j\) with \(B_j>0\) (\(j=1,\dots,15\)), and put \(D_{abc}=\prod_{j=1}^{15}B_j\). The guard polynomial is $\(G_T(X_1,\dots,X_{15})=\prod_{\substack{(a,b,c)\in[-T,T]^3\\ ab\ne c}}\ \sum_{j=1}^{15}\Bigl(D_{abc}X_j-\frac{D_{abc}}{B_j}A_j\Bigr)^2\ \in\mathbb Z[X_1,\dots,X_{15}],\)$ the product over the finite set of false triples (empty product \(1\)). Each factor has integer coefficients because \(B_j\mid D_{abc}\). The constructor \(\mathrm{guard}\ e\ (a_1,\dots,a_{15})\) denotes \(G_{\mathrm{val}(e)}\) at the polynomials of its argument nodes; the specification uses only \(e=T\).

The polynomial is never expanded: its arithmetic zero set is described by the guard semantics, and its size by the size chapter.

The specification describes the coordinates of \(\iota(n)\), \(n>0\), through division polynomials at \(P_0\), namely \(x_n=x(P_0)-\psi_{n+1}(P_0)\psi_{n-1}(P_0)/\psi_n(P_0)^2\) and \(y_n=\psi_{2n}(P_0)/(2\psi_n(P_0)^4)\), with \(\iota(-n)\) obtained by negating the ordinate. These are the coordinates of \([n]P_0\) by the multiplication-by-\(n\) formulas, because \(P_0\) has infinite order; the definition here uses \(\iota\) directly.

docs.title: Formulas, gadgets and witness scope
docs.text:
Templates are generated from formulas: equality is a difference, conjunction a sum of squares, disjunction a product, and rational constants are fresh variables tied by global equations. The node encoding of a constructed template denotes the compiled formula, and every construction keeps its private blocks apart.

A call evaluates its callee at the parameter values and its private block. Disjoint private blocks can be moved to the front, and the block of an inactive branch may take any values.

Rational constants are fresh variables with global equations, which stay active outside every internal disjunction. Strict positivity and absolute value are expressed with four squares.

Elements of \(K_0\) are pairs of rationals and points of \(E\) are five-coordinate codes; the shared pair and point formulas are fixed once.

Model-evaluation recipes refer to points by references; the references \(-1,-2,-3\) are the codes of \(O\), \(P_0\) and \(-P_0\) once the generator constraints hold.

11 fully proved

docs.title: Formulas and their polynomial compilation
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.Formula ZInQ.Syntax.Formula.compile ZInQ.Syntax.Formula.Holds ZInQ.Syntax.Build ZInQ.Syntax.Build.fresh ZInQ.Syntax.Build.call ZInQ.Syntax.Build.rational ZInQ.Syntax.globalEq ZInQ.Syntax.Build.template ZInQ.Syntax.Build.fullFormula ZInQ.Syntax.Build.template_eq ZInQ.Syntax.Build.nz ZInQ.Syntax.Build.pos

Formulas. A formula over \(\mathbb Z[X_i:i\in\mathbb N]\) is built from atoms \(a\doteq b\) (\(a,b\) polynomials), \(\langle f\rangle\) (\(f\) a polynomial) and call atoms \(\langle\tau[g;w]\rangle\) (\(\tau\) an existential polynomial with \(p\) parameters and \(m\) witnesses, \(g\) a \(p\)-tuple of polynomials, \(w\in\mathbb N\) the witness start) by the connectives \(\bigwedge(\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_k)\) and \(\bigvee(\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_k)\), \(k\ge0\). A formula holds at \(x:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Q\) when its atoms are read as \(a(x)=b(x)\), \(f(x)=0\) and \(\tau[g;w](x)=0\) and the connectives as conjunction and disjunction (the empty conjunction is true, the empty disjunction false). Its compilation \(\kappa\) is $\(\kappa(a\doteq b)=a-b,\quad \kappa(\langle f\rangle)=f,\quad \kappa(\langle\tau[g;w]\rangle)=\tau[g;w],\quad \kappa\Bigl(\bigwedge_i\varphi_i\Bigr)=\sum_i\kappa(\varphi_i)^2,\quad \kappa\Bigl(\bigvee_i\varphi_i\Bigr)=\prod_i\kappa(\varphi_i),\)$ with empty sum \(0\) and empty product \(1\). A conjunction nested inside a conjunction is squared twice; no flattening takes place. The call atom \(\langle\tau[g;w]\rangle\) owns the block \([w,w+m)\).

Template constructions. A construction of a template with \(p\) parameters keeps a counter \(c\), initially \(p\), and a list of global equations, initially empty; the parameters are \(X_0,\dots,X_{p-1}\). It may:

  1. take a fresh variable \(X_c\) and increase \(c\) by one;
  2. call an existential polynomial \(\tau\) with \(m\) witnesses on parameter polynomials \(g\): this takes the block \(X_c,\dots,X_{c+m-1}\), increases \(c\) by \(m\) and yields the call atom \(\langle\tau[g;c]\rangle\) (a block of length zero takes no variable);
  3. request a rational constant \(u/q\) (the pair \((u,q)\) normalized only by the sign of \(q\)): an integer constant (\(q=1\)) is the polynomial \(u\); otherwise the first request takes a fresh variable \(X_c\) and records the global equation \(q\,X_c\doteq u\), and later requests of the same normalized pair return the same variable.

If the construction ends with formula \(\varphi\), recorded global equations \(E_1,\dots,E_r\) (in order of creation) and counter \(v\), the template has \(p\) parameters, \(v-p\) witnesses and polynomial $\(\kappa\bigl(\textstyle\bigwedge(E_1,\dots,E_r,\varphi)\bigr)=\sum_{i=1}^r\kappa(E_i)^2+\kappa(\varphi)^2 .\)$ In particular a template without rational constants has polynomial \(\kappa(\varphi)^2\).

Gadgets. \(\mathrm{NZ}(a)\) takes a fresh \(w\) and is the atom \(a\cdot w\doteq1\). \(\mathrm{POS}(a)\) takes fresh \(z_1,z_2,z_3,z_4\) and is the atom \(a\,(z_1^2+z_2^2+z_3^2+z_4^2)\doteq1\).

This is a definition. Every later template article describes its construction by listing its variables in allocation order and its formula; the order of the constructor's steps is the order in which the allocations occur.

docs.title: Template construction from formulas
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.Build.Allocates ZInQ.Syntax.Build.Allocates.bind ZInQ.Syntax.Build.template_construction

Call a construction allocating if, run from any counter and list of global equations, it never decreases the counter and only appends global equations \(q\,X_c\doteq u\) whose variables \(c\) are newly allocated (at least the initial and below the final counter), in increasing order. Every fresh variable, call, rational constant and gadget is allocating, and so is every construction composed of them.

Let an allocating construction with \(p\) parameters end with formula \(\varphi\), global equations \(E_1,\dots,E_r\) and counter \(v\), and let \(\tau\) be its template. Then \(\tau\) has parameter count \(p\) and variable count \(v\), $\([\![\tau]\!]=\kappa\bigl(\textstyle\bigwedge(E_1,\dots,E_r,\varphi)\bigr),\)$ the variables \(c_1<\dots<c_r\) of \(E_1,\dots,E_r\) lie in \([p,v)\), and if every variable of \(\kappa(\varphi)\) has index below \(v\), so has every variable of \([\![\tau]\!]\).

Proof sketch. The polynomial and the counts are the definition of the template. Allocation is closed under sequencing: the counter of the second step starts where the first ended, so the equations appended by the first step lie below every equation appended by the second. A fresh variable or call only advances the counter; a rational constant either returns a constant or a recorded variable, or records the equation for the variable \(X_c\) it allocates. Run from \((p,[\,])\) this gives the ranges of the constant variables, and the polynomial of \(E_i\) has the single variable \(c_i<v\).

docs.title: Witness scope of constructed templates and recipes
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.Formula.InScope ZInQ.Syntax.ExPoly.WitnessScope ZInQ.Syntax.ExPoly.WitnessScope.rel_iff ZInQ.Syntax.ExPoly.WitnessScope.wf ZInQ.Syntax.Build.Facts.witnessScope ZInQ.Syntax.templateLibrary_witnessScope ZInQ.Syntax.CompositionRecipe.witnessScope_of ZInQ.Syntax.closeRecipe_callBlocks_disjoint ZInQ.Syntax.mainRecipe_callBlocks_disjoint ZInQ.Syntax.valueUnionRecipe_callBlocks_disjoint ZInQ.Syntax.valueRecipe_callBlocks_disjoint ZInQ.Syntax.integersRecipe_callBlocks_disjoint ZInQ.Syntax.translate_witnessScope ZInQ.Syntax.specLib_witnessScope ZInQ.Syntax.specLib_precisionCircuit_witnessScope

Call an existential polynomial \(\tau\) with \(p\) parameters and \(v\) variables in scope if \([\![\tau]\!]=\kappa(\varphi)\) for a formula \(\varphi\) such that

  1. every call atom of \(\varphi\) with callee witness count \(m\) and witness start \(w\) satisfies \(p\le w\) and \(w+m\le v\), and its callee has all its variables below its variable count;
  2. the blocks \([w,w+m)\) of the call atoms are pairwise disjoint;
  3. no variable of a block occurs in a parameter polynomial of any call atom or in any atom \(a\doteq b\) or \(\langle f\rangle\) of \(\varphi\);
  4. every variable occurring in \(\kappa(\varphi)\) has index below \(v\).

Then \(\mathrm{Rel}_\tau(a)\) holds exactly when \(\varphi^\ast\) holds at some assignment extending \(a\), and every variable of \([\![\tau]\!]\) has index below \(v\).

Every template of the library is in scope (with \(\varphi=\bigwedge(E_1,\dots,E_r,\varphi_0)\) for its construction). A composition recipe is in scope when its call arguments lie below a bound \(B\ge p\), its calls start at or above \(B\), and its call blocks are pairwise disjoint; the five composition recipes of the specification satisfy this with \(B=51\) (close), \(11\) (main), \(6\) (value_union, value, integers): their blocks are allocated one after another above the parameters and fresh ranges. The model-evaluation translation of a well-formed natural circuit is in scope. Hence every recipe of the specification is in scope.

Proof sketch. For a template, the list of call blocks of its construction is computed from the counter and checked to be separated and above \(p\); the parameter polynomials and atoms are checked to use only variables below \(v\) outside the blocks; constant variables are allocated by the counter. A construction may use a call atom twice, so this check is made per template. For a composition recipe the arguments are parameters or fresh-range variables below \(B\) and the blocks lie at or above \(B\). For the translation every reference, generator variable and block is allocated by its counter. The relational form is the private-witness lemma.

docs.title: Evaluation of a template call
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.ev_callPoly ZInQ.Syntax.ExPoly.exists_blockUpdate_call_iff

Let \(\tau\) be a template or recipe with \(p\) parameters, \(v\) variables and \(m=v-p\) witnesses, all of whose variables have index below \(v\). Let \(g_0,\dots,g_{p-1}\) be polynomials, \(w\in\mathbb N\) and \(x:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Q\). Then $\(\tau[g;w]\,(x)=[\![\tau]\!]\,(g_0(x),\dots,g_{p-1}(x),x_w,x_{w+1},\dots,x_{w+m-1}).\)$ Consequently, if none of the variables \(X_w,\dots,X_{w+m-1}\) occurs in any \(g_i\), then for every assignment \(x\) of the remaining variables $\(\bigl(\exists\,y_0,\dots,y_{m-1}\in\mathbb Q:\ \tau[g;w]\,(x[X_{w+j}\mapsto y_j])=0\bigr) \iff\mathrm{Rel}_\tau(g_0(x),\dots,g_{p-1}(x)).\)$

Proof sketch. Evaluation commutes with the substitution homomorphism: the value of \(\tau[g;w]\) at \(x\) is the value of \([\![\tau]\!]\) at the assignment \(i\mapsto g_i(x)\) for \(i<p\) and \(i\mapsto x_{w+i-p}\) for \(i\ge p\), and only \(i<v\) matters. If the block variables do not occur in the \(g_i\), changing \(x\) on the block leaves every \(g_i(x)\) unchanged, and the block values range over all of \(\mathbb Q^m\); this is the existential statement.

docs.title: Private witness blocks
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.Formula.exists_blocks_iff

Let \(\varphi\) be a formula whose atoms of the form \(\langle\cdot\rangle\) are calls \(\langle\tau_i[g_i;w_i]\rangle\), \(i=1,\dots,k\), where \(\tau_i\) has \(p_i\) parameters, \(v_i\) variables, \(m_i=v_i-p_i\) witnesses and all its variables below \(v_i\). Put \(B_i=\{w_i,\dots,w_i+m_i-1\}\) and assume:

  • the blocks \(B_1,\dots,B_k\) are pairwise disjoint;
  • no variable of any \(B_i\) occurs in any parameter polynomial \(g_j\) or in any atom \(a\doteq b\) of \(\varphi\).

Let \(\varphi^\ast(x)\) be the statement obtained from \(\varphi\) by replacing each call atom by \(\mathrm{Rel}_{\tau_i}(g_i(x))\) and each atom \(a\doteq b\) by \(a(x)=b(x)\). Then for every \(x:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Q\), $\(\bigl(\exists\,y:\textstyle\bigcup_iB_i\to\mathbb Q,\ \ \kappa(\varphi)(x[y])=0\bigr)\iff\varphi^\ast(x),\)$ where \(x[y]\) agrees with \(y\) on \(\bigcup_iB_i\) and with \(x\) elsewhere; both sides depend only on \(x\) outside the blocks. In particular a conjunction of calls with disjoint blocks has a rational zero exactly when every callee relation holds, a product of calls has one exactly when some callee relation holds, and the block of an inactive factor may be given arbitrary values (for instance all zero). Variables occurring in no atom and no block may likewise take arbitrary values.

Proof sketch. By the compilation theorem the left side says that \(\varphi\) holds at \(x[y]\) for some \(y\). Induct on \(\varphi\), proving the statement for every \(x\). For an atom \(a\doteq b\) the value does not depend on \(y\). For a call atom this is the evaluation of a call. For a conjunction \(\bigwedge\varphi_j\) the blocks used by different conjuncts are disjoint, so witnesses \(y_j\) for the conjuncts glue to one \(y\) that restricts to each \(y_j\) on its own blocks; conversely a common \(y\) restricts to witnesses for each conjunct. For a disjunction, a witness for the true disjunct extends by arbitrary values (the rational domain is nonempty) to the blocks of the other disjuncts. Fixed equations inside an active callee are part of that callee's relation and are not discarded.

docs.title: Rational constants by global equations
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.ev_globals_eq_zero_iff ZInQ.Syntax.generator_values

Let a template be constructed with formula \(\varphi\) and rational constants \(u_1/q_1,\dots,u_r/q_r\) (\(q_i\ge2\)) held in variables \(X_{c_1},\dots,X_{c_r}\), so that its polynomial is \(\kappa(\bigwedge(q_1X_{c_1}\doteq u_1,\dots,q_rX_{c_r}\doteq u_r,\varphi))\). Then for every \(x:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Q\) this polynomial vanishes at \(x\) exactly when \(x_{c_i}=u_i/q_i\) for every \(i\) and \(\varphi\) holds at \(x\). The equations are conjuncts of the whole template, outside every disjunction of \(\varphi\), so they constrain every branch.

For the cached coordinates of the generator, the three equations $\(8g_0=1641,\qquad 4g_1=-15465,\qquad 32g_2=87483\)$ hold exactly when \((g_0,g_1,g_2)=(1641/8,\,-15465/4,\,87483/32)\), and then \((0,g_0,-145,g_1,g_2)\) has \(x\)-coordinate \(1641/8-145s=(1641-1160s)/8\) and \(y\)-coordinate \(-15465/4+(87483/32)s=(-123720+87483s)/32\), the coordinates of \(P_0\).

Proof sketch. By the compilation theorem the polynomial vanishes exactly when every conjunct holds; \(q_ix_{c_i}=u_i\) with \(q_i\ne0\) means \(x_{c_i}=u_i/q_i\). The generator values are the arithmetic \(1641/8-145s=(1641-1160s)/8\) and \(-15465/4=-123720/32\).

docs.title: Strict positivity by four squares
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.pos_iff_four_squares ZInQ.Syntax.exists_blockUpdate_posFormula_iff

For every \(s\in\mathbb Q\), $\(s>0\iff\exists\,z_1,z_2,z_3,z_4\in\mathbb Q,\quad s\,(z_1^2+z_2^2+z_3^2+z_4^2)=1 .\)$ Hence the gadget \(\mathrm{POS}(a)\) is satisfiable by a choice of its four fresh variables exactly when \(a>0\).

Proof sketch. If \(s>0\) write \(1/s=a/b\) with integers \(a,b>0\). By Lagrange's four-square theorem \(ab=n_1^2+n_2^2+n_3^2+n_4^2\) with \(n_i\in\mathbb Z\); put \(z_i=n_i/b\), so that \(\sum z_i^2=ab/b^2=1/s\). Conversely a sum of squares is nonnegative, so \(s\sum z_i^2=1\) forces \(\sum z_i^2>0\) and then \(s=1/\sum z_i^2>0\).

docs.title: Absolute value by four squares
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.eq_abs_iff_four_squares ZInQ.Syntax.absTemplate_rel_iff

For all \(a,x\in\mathbb Q\), $\(a=|x|\iff\exists\,z_1,z_2,z_3,z_4\in\mathbb Q,\quad a=z_1^2+z_2^2+z_3^2+z_4^2\ \text{ and }\ a^2=x^2 .\)$ Consequently, for the absolute-value template, \(\mathrm{Rel}_{\mathtt{value.abs}}(x,a)\iff a=|x|\) for all \(x,a\in\mathbb Q\).

Proof sketch. If \(a\) is a sum of squares then \(a\ge0\), and \(a^2=x^2\) gives \(a=\pm x\), hence \(a=|x|\). Conversely write \(|x|=u/v\) with \(u\ge0\), \(v>0\) integers; by Lagrange's theorem \(uv=\sum_i n_i^2\), so \(|x|=\sum_i(n_i/v)^2\), and \(|x|^2=x^2\). The manuscript states the equivalence without proof; the converse direction is the step supplied here. For the template, its polynomial is \(\kappa(\varphi)^2\) for the conjunction \(\varphi\) of the two equations, which by the compilation theorem vanishes at \((x,a,z_1,\dots,z_4)\) exactly when both equations hold; the four witnesses are the \(z_i\).

docs.title: Quadratic-field pairs and point-code formulas
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.Pair ZInQ.Syntax.Build.fdiv ZInQ.Syntax.Build.zGadget

These are the formula-level abbreviations shared by the templates. Throughout, \(K_0=\mathbb Q(s)\) with \(s^2=2\).

Pairs. A pair is \(u=(u_0,u_1)\) of polynomials, standing for \(u_0+u_1s\). Define \(u+u'=(u_0+u_0',u_1+u_1')\), \(-u=(-u_0,-u_1)\), \(u-u'=u+(-u')\), \(k\,u=(ku_0,ku_1)\) for an integer or polynomial \(k\), $\(u\cdot u'=(u_0u_0'+2u_1u_1',\ u_0u_1'+u_1u_0'),\)$ \(u^2=u\cdot u\), \(u^{n}\) by repeated squaring, the conjugate \(\bar u=(u_0,-u_1)\) and the norm \(N(u)=u_0^2-2u_1^2\). Integer pairs are written \((a,b)\); \(1=(1,0)\). The curve coefficient is \(A=(-11243,7950)\), that is \(A=-d^2\) for \(d=75-53s\), and \(\delta=(11243,-7950)=d^2\).

Pair formulas. \(u\doteq u'\) is \(\bigwedge(u_0\doteq u_0',u_1\doteq u_1')\). \(\mathrm{NZ}_K(u)\) is \(\mathrm{NZ}(N(u))\) (one fresh variable). \(\mathrm{Div}(n,d)\) takes a fresh pair \(q\), then forms \(\bigwedge(\mathrm{NZ}_K(d),\ d\cdot q\doteq n)\); its value is \(q\).

Point codes. A point code is \(p=(p_0,\dots,p_4)\), with \(x(p)=(p_1,p_2)\) and \(y(p)=(p_3,p_4)\); a fresh point takes five fresh variables. Define \(O=(1,0,0,0,0)\), \(\mathrm{neg}(p)=(p_0,p_1,p_2,-p_3,-p_4)\), \(\mathrm{eq}(p,p')=\bigwedge_{i=0}^4(p_i\doteq p_i')\), \(\mathrm{isO}(p)=\mathrm{eq}(p,O)\), \(\mathrm{fin}(p)\) the atom \(p_0\doteq0\), and the curve atom pair \(\mathrm{curve}(X,Y)\): \(Y^2\doteq X^2\cdot X+A\cdot X\). The generator point of a template is \(G=(0,c_1,-145,c_2,c_3)\) with \(c_1,c_2,c_3\) the rational constants \(1641/8\), \(-15465/4\), \(87483/32\), requested in this order.

Local parameter and inverse abscissa. For a point \(p\) and a pair \(\zeta\), $\(Z(p,\zeta)=\bigvee\Bigl(\bigwedge(\mathrm{isO}(p),\ \zeta\doteq(0,0)),\ \ \bigwedge(\mathrm{fin}(p),\ \mathrm{NZ}_K(y(p)),\ y(p)\cdot\zeta\doteq-x(p))\Bigr)\)$ (one fresh variable) expresses \(\zeta=z(p)=-x/y\), with \(z(O)=0\). For a pair \(v\), $\(I\!X(p,v)=\bigvee\Bigl(\bigwedge(\mathrm{isO}(p),\ v\doteq(0,0)),\ \ \bigwedge(\mathrm{fin}(p),\ x(p)\cdot v\doteq(1,0))\Bigr)\)$ expresses \(v=1/x\), with value \(0\) at the identity.

This is a definition. In each template these abbreviations allocate their fresh variables at the moment they are formed, in the order written.

docs.title: Values of the point references
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.pointRef_eval_generator ZInQ.Syntax.generatorConstraints_eq_zero_iff

Let \(x:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Q\) satisfy the three generator constraints of a model-evaluation recipe, \(8x_{g_0}=1641\), \(4x_{g_1}=-15465\) and \(32x_{g_2}=87483\). Then $\(\mathrm{ref}(-1)(x)=\iota(0),\qquad\mathrm{ref}(-2)(x)=\iota(1),\qquad\mathrm{ref}(-3)(x)=\iota(-1),\)$ that is, the codes of \(O\), \(P_0\) and \(-P_0\). Explicitly \(\iota(1)=(0,\ 1641/8,\ -145,\ -15465/4,\ 87483/32)\) and \(\iota(-1)=(0,\ 1641/8,\ -145,\ 15465/4,\ -87483/32)\).

Proof sketch. The constraints give \(x_{g_0}=1641/8\), \(x_{g_1}=-15465/4\), \(x_{g_2}=87483/32\). docs.title: Recipes and witness accounting
docs.text:
A natural circuit is translated into a model-evaluation recipe: every variable and node gets a point code, natural variables get the natural template, constants get fixed-scalar templates, and additions, multiplications and power calls get the corresponding templates.

Five composition recipes assemble the value relation and the root.

The witness counts follow from the template counts, the shape of the natural circuit (proved in the compiler chapter: shape of the natural precision circuit) and explicit arithmetic; the root has one input and \(292{,}890{,}231{,}904\) witnesses.

In the variable format of the target statement, the rational zero projection of \(P_*\) is the set of \(q\) for which the value relation has a code.

8 fully proved

docs.title: Translation of a natural circuit into a model-evaluation recipe
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.translate ZInQ.Syntax.translate_variableCount

Natural circuits. A natural circuit has \(k\) inputs, a list of explicit variables \((i_0,\kappa_0),(i_1,\kappa_1),\dots\) (variable index and kind, the inputs first with indices \(0,\dots,k-1\)), a node list whose nodes are \(\mathrm{const}\ c\), \(\mathrm{var}\ i\), \(\mathrm{add}\ j\ j'\), \(\mathrm{mul}\ j\ j'\) or \(\mathrm{call}\ (a,b,c)\ w\) (a call of the power template on three earlier nodes with a private block of \(79\) variables at \(w\)), and a root node. The power template is itself a natural circuit with \(3\) inputs, \(79\) witnesses, no calls, and explicit variables \(0,\dots,81\).

Translation. Fix the operation templates \(\nu=\mathtt{natural}\), \(\alpha=\mathtt{raw\_add}\), \(\mu=\mathtt{multiply}\) with witness counts \(140604\), \(6\), \(35134\). The translation of a natural circuit with \(k\) inputs, in mode \(\mathrm{value}\) or \(\mathrm{zero}\), with or without natural constraints on the inputs, and with an optional power recipe \(\pi\), is the model-evaluation recipe with \(p=5(k+[\mathrm{value}])\) parameters built by one allocation counter starting at \(p\):

  1. the generator indices \(g_0,g_1,g_2\) take the next three variables;
  2. for each explicit variable in list order: an input \(i\) gets the point reference \(5i\) (inside the parameters), any other variable gets a fresh point (five variables); then, unless it is an input and inputs are unconstrained, a natural block of \(140604\) variables is taken; the row records the reference and the natural start (or none);
  3. each node \(j\) in order gets a point reference \(\mathrm{pt}(j)\): \(\mathrm{var}\ i\) the reference of \(i\); \(\mathrm{const}\ 0\), \(1\), \(-1\) the references \(-1\), \(-2\), \(-3\); any other constant \(c\) (the translation is defined only when every such constant is an integer \(c\ge2\), which holds for both circuits translated here), at its first occurrence in this circuit, a fresh point followed by a block of \(1\), recording the constant definition \((S_{\mathrm{integer\_constant}_h},\text{point},\text{start})\) where \(\mathrm{integer\_constant}_h=c\) (a new index \(h\) is created when \(c\) has not occurred in any earlier translation), and later occurrences reuse that point; \(\mathrm{add}\ j_1\ j_2\) and \(\mathrm{mul}\ j_1\ j_2\) nodes a fresh point followed by a block of \(6\) or \(35134\), recording the operation \((0\text{ or }1,\ \mathrm{pt}(j_1),\ \mathrm{pt}(j_2),\ \text{point},\ \text{start})\); a \(\mathrm{call}\ (a,b,c)\ w\) a fresh point followed by a block of the witness count of \(\pi\), recording \((2,\mathrm{pt}(a),\mathrm{pt}(b),\mathrm{pt}(c),\text{point},\text{start})\); the source block at \(w\) is not used;
  4. the root equality is \((\mathrm{pt}(\mathrm{root}),5k)\) in value mode and \((\mathrm{pt}(\mathrm{root}),-1)\) in zero mode;
  5. the variable count is the final counter.

The polynomial of the result is given by the semantics of model-evaluation recipes: the three generator constraints, the natural calls, the constant definitions (each a fixed-scalar template on \((\mathrm{ref}(-2),\text{point})\)), the operation calls and the five root differences, squared and summed.

Equivalently, the translation takes the table of nontrivial constants as an argument, listed in order of first occurrence across the translations: \((4,2,3)\) for power_value and \((4,2,3,c_3,1399)\) for precision, a constant \(c\) using the fixed-scalar template of its position in the table.

This is a definition. The arithmetic meaning (every node point is the code of the node's signed integer value) is the compiler chapter's rational translation statement.

docs.text:

The recipe \(\mathtt{power\_value}\) is the translation of the power template of the natural precision polynomial (\(3\) inputs, \(79\) witnesses) in value mode, without natural constraints on the inputs and without a power recipe. It has \(20\) parameters (three signed input codes at \(X_0,\dots,X_{14}\) and the output code at \(X_{15},\dots,X_{19}\)), generator indices \(20,21,22\), and every one of the \(79\) witnesses of the power template receives a fresh point and a natural block. Its constants are \(4,2,3\), which become \(\mathrm{integer\_constant}_0,\mathrm{integer\_constant}_1,\mathrm{integer\_constant}_2\). Its root equality equates the point of the root node with the output code; the value of the power-template polynomial is not required to vanish here.

This is a definition. With the natural circuit statistics it has \(17{,}786{,}698\) witnesses and \(17{,}786{,}718\) variables.

docs.title: The precision recipe
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.precisionRecipe ZInQ.Syntax.precisionRecipe_variableCount_le

The recipe \(\mathtt{precision}\) is the translation of the five-input natural precision polynomial in zero mode, with natural constraints on the inputs and with power recipe \(\mathtt{power\_value}\), performed after the translation of the power template (so the constants \(4,2,3\) keep their indices \(0,1,2\)). It has \(25\) parameters (the five input codes \(X_{5i},\dots,X_{5i+4}\), \(i=0,\dots,4\), in the input order \((n,\kappa,a,l,j)\)), generator indices \(25,26,27\), a natural block for every explicit variable including the inputs, and its root equality equates the point of the root node with \(\mathrm{ref}(-1)\), the code of \(O\). Its nontrivial constants, in order of first occurrence, are \(c_3\), \(2\), \(4\), \(1399\); \(c_3\) and \(1399\) become \(\mathrm{integer\_constant}_3\) and \(\mathrm{integer\_constant}_4\).

This is a definition. If the natural circuit has \(5\) inputs, listed first among at most \(54056\) explicit variables, at most \(125327\) addition, \(98382\) multiplication and \(15845\) call nodes, and nontrivial constants among \(c_3,2,4,1399\) (the shape given by the natural circuit statistics), then \(\mathtt{precision}\) has at most \(292{,}889{,}492{,}836\) witnesses and at most \(292{,}889{,}492{,}861\) variables.

docs.title: The outer composition recipes
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.closeRecipe ZInQ.Syntax.mainRecipe ZInQ.Syntax.valueUnionRecipe ZInQ.Syntax.valueRecipe ZInQ.Syntax.integersRecipe

Five composition recipes assemble the ordinary-value relation; each is built with one allocation counter starting at its parameter count, fresh ranges first, then the calls in order. Write \(\mathbf X_a=(X_a,\dots,X_{a+4})\).

  1. \(\mathtt{close}\) (sum of squares), parameters \(N=\mathbf X_0\), \(K=\mathbf X_5\), \(t=X_{10}\). Fresh points \(A=\mathbf X_{11}\), \(L=\mathbf X_{16}\), \(J=\mathbf X_{21}\) and \(E_0,\dots,E_4=\mathbf X_{26},\mathbf X_{31},\dots,\mathbf X_{46}\). Calls: \(\mathtt{value.signed\_encode}[\Sigma_i,E_i]\) for \((\Sigma_0,\dots,\Sigma_4)=(N,K,A,L,J)\) (starts \(51+140654i\)); \(\mathtt{precision}[E_0,\dots,E_4]\) (start \(703321\)); \(\mathtt{value.close\_coordinates}[A,L,J,t]\) (start \(292890196157\)). \(11\) parameters, \(292890196199\) witnesses.
  2. \(\mathtt{main}\) (sum of squares), parameters \(N=\mathbf X_0\), \(t=X_5\). Fresh point \(K=\mathbf X_6\). Calls: \(\mathtt{close}[N,K,t]\) (start \(11\)) and \(\mathtt{value.test}[N,K,t]\) (start \(292890196210\)). \(6\) parameters, \(292890231486\) witnesses.
  3. \(\mathtt{value\_union}\) (product), parameters \(N=\mathbf X_0\), \(t=X_5\). Calls: \(\mathtt{value.exceptions}[N,t]\) (start \(6\)) and \(\mathtt{main}[N,t]\) (start \(412\)). \(6\) parameters, \(292890231892\) witnesses.
  4. \(\mathtt{value}\) (sum of squares), parameters \(N=\mathbf X_0\), \(t=X_5\). Calls: \(\mathtt{member}[N]\) (start \(6\)) and \(\mathtt{value\_union}[N,t]\) (start \(13\)). \(6\) parameters, \(292890231899\) witnesses.
  5. \(\mathtt{integers}\) (sum of squares), parameter \(t=X_0\). Fresh point \(N=\mathbf X_1\). Call: \(\mathtt{value}[N,t]\) (start \(6\)). \(1\) parameter, \(292890231904\) witnesses.

Thus, with call polynomials as in the semantics of recipes, $\([\![\mathtt{integers}]\!]=\mathtt{value}[X_1,\dots,X_5,X_0;6]^2,\qquad [\![\mathtt{value}]\!]=\mathtt{member}[\mathbf X_0;6]^2+\mathtt{value\_union}[\mathbf X_0,X_5;13]^2,\)$ $\([\![\mathtt{value\_union}]\!]=\mathtt{value.exceptions}[\mathbf X_0,X_5;6]\cdot\mathtt{main}[\mathbf X_0,X_5;412],\)$ and similarly for \(\mathtt{main}\) and \(\mathtt{close}\). The same coordinates of \(K\) occur in \(\mathtt{close}\) and \(\mathtt{value.test}\); the exceptional branch and the main branch have disjoint private blocks.

The starts and witness counts from the precision call on are those for a precision recipe with \(292{,}889{,}492{,}836\) witnesses, the bound of the precision recipe; in general each of them shifts with the witness count of the recipe called (for instance \(\mathtt{close}\) has \(703310+w+53\) witnesses when precision has \(w\)), so the displayed values are upper bounds.

The seven recipes have the following parameter counts, and at most the following witness and variable counts:

Recipe Parameters Witnesses Variables power_value 20 17,786,698 17,786,718 precision 25 292,889,492,836 292,889,492,861 close 11 292,890,196,199 292,890,196,210 main 6 292,890,231,486 292,890,231,492 value_union 6 292,890,231,892 292,890,231,898 value 6 292,890,231,899 292,890,231,905 integers 1 292,890,231,904 292,890,231,905

The row of power_value is exact, and so are the differences between consecutive rows from precision on; in particular integers has exactly \(739{,}069\) variables more than precision has witnesses.

Every variable occurring in the polynomial of a template or recipe has index below its variable count. In particular every variable of \([\![\mathtt{integers}]\!]\) is among \(X_0,\dots,X_{292890231904}\), so \(P_*\), which is \([\![\mathtt{integers}]\!]\) read in these variables, has input \(X_0\) and its witness variables among \(X_1,\dots,X_{292890231904}\), the variables allowed by the target statement, which need not all occur.

The manuscript states the table as exact counts, and the private blocks of every template and recipe as pairwise disjoint and disjoint from the variables used outside them. The exact counts follow in the same way from the exact node statistics. The variable format of the target needs neither; the relational statements of the compiler and assembly chapters prove the separation of blocks they use.

Proof sketch. For the composition recipes the witness count is the sum of the fresh ranges and the callee witness counts, read off the recipe definitions. For a model-evaluation translation it is \(3\) (generator) plus, for each explicit witness variable, \(5+140604\); for each constrained input, \(140604\); for each distinct nontrivial constant, \(5+1\); for each addition, multiplication and call node, \(5+6\), \(5+35134\) and \(5+17786698\). Inserting the template counts and the bounds of the circuit shape gives the table, through the witness-count arithmetic. The variable bounds are the witness-scope theorem applied to every template and recipe, by induction along the library and recipe order.

docs.title: The rational zero projection of the specified polynomial
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.PstarOf_spec ZInQ.Syntax.PstarOf_zero_projection ZInQ.Syntax.specPstar_spec ZInQ.Syntax.specPstar_zero_projection

For every \(q\in\mathbb Q\) the following are equivalent:

  1. there is \(w=(w_1,\dots,w_{292890231904})\in\mathbb Q^{292890231904}\) with \(P_*(q,w_1,\dots,w_{292890231904})=0\);
  2. \(\mathrm{Rel}_{\mathtt{integers}}(q)\);
  3. there is \(x:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Q\) with \(x_0=q\) and \([\![\mathtt{integers}]\!]\,(x)=0\);
  4. there are \(N\in\mathbb Q^5\) and rational values of the witnesses of \(\mathtt{value}\) making \([\![\mathtt{value}]\!]\) vanish at \((N,q)\), that is, \(\mathrm{Rel}_{\mathtt{value}}(N,q)\) for some \(N\in\mathbb Q^5\).

Moreover \(P_*\) is \([\![\mathtt{integers}]\!]\) read in the variables indexed by \(\{0,\dots,292890231904\}\): \(\mathrm{rename}(\iota)\,P_*=[\![\mathtt{integers}]\!]\) for the inclusion \(\iota\) of the indices into \(\mathbb N\). Hence \(P_*\) has total degree at most that of \([\![\mathtt{integers}]\!]\) and the same coefficients, \(\mathrm{coeff}_d(P_*)=\mathrm{coeff}_{\iota_*d}([\![\mathtt{integers}]\!])\) for every exponent vector \(d\), and \(P_*(v)=[\![\mathtt{integers}]\!](\bar v)\) for every \(v\in\mathbb Q^{292890231905}\), where \(\bar v\) extends \(v\) by zeros.

So the rational zero projection of \(P_*\) to its first variable is \(\{q:\exists N,\ \mathrm{Rel}_{\mathtt{value}}(N,q)\}\), which the assembly chapter identifies with \(\mathbb Z\).

Proof sketch. By the witness accounting, \([\![\mathtt{integers}]\!]\) involves only \(X_0,\dots,X_{292890231904}\), so its value at \(x\) depends only on \(x_0,\dots,x_{292890231904}\) and equals \(P_*(x_0,\dots,x_{292890231904})\); this gives \(1\iff2\iff3\) (unused variables take arbitrary values, for instance \(0\)). For \(3\iff4\): \([\![\mathtt{integers}]\!]\) is the square of one call of \(\mathtt{value}\) with parameters \(X_1,\dots,X_5,X_0\) and block \([6,292890231905)\), which is disjoint from \(X_0,\dots,X_5\); apply the evaluation of a call and the compilation theorem.

docs.title: The other templates
docs.text:
Besides membership and raw addition, the core elliptic templates express the local parameter \(z=-x/y\), the inverse abscissa and the truncated formal logarithm, whose seven coefficients are \(16575(-1)^j\binom{2j}{j}/(4j+1)\).

The multiplication certificate is assembled from the pole polynomial, twelve local tests, the normalized slope certificate and the height certificate. The pole template's relation is the pole predicate \(\Phi\) of pole completeness.

Fixed scalar multiples are expressed with division polynomials, and the guard excludes exactly the false triples of codes in the finite box.

The multiplication template conjoins four scalar shifts, the height certificate and the guard. The natural template expresses a code of a natural number as a sum of four squares; given the multiplication statement, its relation holds exactly on the codes of natural numbers.

Its semantics, the natural-code predicate, is proved in the translation chapter: the natural-code predicate.

The value templates encode signed indices, absolute values, the coordinate window, the six raw tests with the pole predicate, and the six exceptional values.

The library lists the 23 templates in order, including five fixed-scalar templates for the constants of the natural precision polynomial.

20 fully proved

docs.title: The pole template
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.poleTemplate ZInQ.Syntax.poleTemplate_poly

The template \(\mathtt{pole}\) has \(1\) parameter and \(11\) witnesses (\(12\) variables): \(B=X_0\), the bits \(b_i=X_{1+i}\) (\(i=0,\dots,5\)), and \(e=X_7\), \(z=X_8\), \(r_1=X_9\), \(r_2=X_{10}\), \(w=X_{11}\). With $\(m=(1-2b_0)(1+b_1)(1+2b_2)(1+4b_3)(1+6b_4)(1+12b_5),\quad A=mB,\quad H=A(A-B^2),\)$ $\(T_1=A(A-e)(A+e),\qquad T_2=A(Az^2-eH)(Az^2+eH),\)$ $\(S=\sum_{i=0}^5(b_i^2-b_i)^2+(eHzw-1)^2+(r_1^2-T_1)^2+(r_2^2-T_2)^2,\)$ its formula is the atom \(B\,S\doteq0\) and its polynomial is $\([\![\mathtt{pole}]\!]=(B\,S)^2=Q_{\rm pole}^2 ,\)$ where \(Q_{\rm pole}=BS\) is the pole polynomial of the pole completeness statement, with the witnesses in the same order. Its relation is therefore \(\Phi(B)\), as stated in the pole-template semantics. These are the Route K factors \(A+e\) and \(Az^2+eH\); the manuscript's template has \(A+3e\) and \(Az^2+3eH\).

docs.title: Semantics of the pole template
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.poleTemplate_rel_iff

For every \(B\in\mathbb Q\), $\(\mathrm{Rel}_{\mathtt{pole}}(B)\iff\Phi(B),\)$ where \(\Phi(B)\) is the statement that the pole polynomial \(Q_{\rm pole}\) of pole completeness has a rational zero with input \(B\): there are \(b_0,\dots,b_5,e,z,r_1,r_2,w\in\mathbb Q\) with \(Q_{\rm pole}(B;b,e,z,r_1,r_2,w)=0\).

Proof sketch. The template polynomial is \((B\,S)^2\), where \(B\,S\) is \(Q_{\rm pole}\) written with \(B=X_0\), \(b_i=X_{1+i}\), \(e=X_7\), \(z=X_8\), \(r_1=X_9\), \(r_2=X_{10}\), \(w=X_{11}\); the compilation \(B\,S-0\) of the atom \(B\,S\doteq0\) is the same polynomial. Evaluating at \((B,y_0,\dots,y_{10})\) gives \(Q_{\rm pole}(B;y)^2\), which vanishes exactly when \(Q_{\rm pole}(B;y)=0\). The eleven witnesses of the template are exactly the eleven witnesses of \(\Phi\), in the same order.

docs.title: The test-group template
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.testGroupTemplate ZInQ.Syntax.testGroupBuild_formula

The template \(\mathtt{test\_group}\) has \(44\) parameters and \(162\) witnesses (\(206\) variables). Parameters: points \(C_0,\dots,C_3\) (\(C_i=(X_{5i},\dots,X_{5i+4})\)) and output pairs \(D_0,\dots,D_{11}\) (\(D_j=(X_{20+2j},X_{21+2j})\)). Witnesses in allocation order:

  • points \(F_i=(X_{44+5i},\dots,X_{48+5i})\) and \(V_i=(X_{64+5i},\dots,X_{68+5i})\), \(i=0,\dots,3\);
  • for \(i=0,\dots,3\): a \(\mathtt{member}\) block of \(7\) and a \(\mathtt{raw\_add}\) block of \(6\) (starts \(84,91,97,104,110,117,123,130\));
  • for \(i=0,\dots,7\), with base \(b=136+7i\): pairs \(\zeta_i=(X_b,X_{b+1})\), \(\lambda_i=(X_{b+2},X_{b+3})\), \(\rho_i=(X_{b+4},X_{b+5})\), then a \(\mathtt{raw\_z}\) block \(\{X_{b+6}\}\) and empty \(\mathtt{log25}\) and \(\mathtt{raw\_inverse\_x}\) blocks at \(b+7\);
  • inverse witnesses \(u_1=X_{192}\), \(u_2=X_{193}\);
  • ratio pairs \(q_{0,1},q_{0,2},q_{0,3},q_{1,1},q_{1,2},q_{1,3}\) at \(X_{194},\dots,X_{205}\).

Let \(\Pi_i=F_i\) and \(\Pi_{4+i}=V_i\) (\(i=0,\dots,3\)), and let the twelve tests be $\(\tau=\bigl(\rho_0,\rho_1,\rho_2,\rho_3,\ \bar\rho_4,\bar\rho_5,\bar\rho_6,\bar\rho_7,\ q_{0,1}-\bar q_{1,1},\ q_{0,2}-\bar q_{1,2},\ q_{0,3}-\bar q_{1,3},\ q_{0,1}\cdot q_{0,2}-q_{0,3}\bigr).\)$ The formula is the conjunction of the following items, in this order:

  1. for \(i=0,\dots,3\): \(\langle\mathtt{member}[F_i]\rangle\) and \(\langle\mathtt{raw\_add}[F_i,\mathrm{neg}(C_i),V_i]\rangle\);
  2. \(\mathrm{fin}(F_0)\) and \(\mathrm{fin}(V_0)\);
  3. for \(i=0,\dots,7\): \(\langle\mathtt{raw\_z}[\Pi_i,\zeta_i]\rangle\), \(\langle\mathtt{log25}[\zeta_i,\lambda_i]\rangle\), \(\langle\mathtt{raw\_inverse\_x}[\Pi_i,\rho_i]\rangle\);
  4. \(N(\lambda_0)\,u_1\doteq1\) and \(N(\lambda_4)\,u_2\doteq1\);
  5. for \(\sigma=0,1\) and \(i=1,2,3\): \(\lambda_{4\sigma}\cdot q_{\sigma,i}\doteq\lambda_{4\sigma+i}\);
  6. for \(j=0,\dots,11\): \(D_j\doteq\tau_j\).

Each call uses its block listed above. The polynomial is \(\kappa\) of this conjunction, squared.

With \(V_i=F_i-C_i\), the tests are four inverse abscissas at \(F_0,\dots,F_3\), the conjugates of the inverse abscissas at \(V_0,\dots,V_3\), three differences of \(L\)-ratios and the product test; their use is the multiplication chapter's.

This is a definition (template index \(6\)).

docs.title: The slope template
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.slopeTemplate ZInQ.Syntax.slopeBuild_formula

The template \(\mathtt{slope}\) has \(22\) parameters and \(1298\) witnesses (\(1320\) variables). Parameters: \(t=X_0\), \(\ell=X_1\) and points \(C_0,\dots,C_3\) (\(C_i=(X_{2+5i},\dots,X_{6+5i})\)). Witnesses in allocation order: \(\eta=X_{22}\), \(q=X_{23}\), \(R_0=X_{24}\); inverse witnesses \(u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4=X_{25},\dots,X_{28}\); for each group \(g=0,\dots,5\) with base \( eta=29+213g\): pairs \(D_{g,j}=(X_{ eta+2j},X_{ eta+2j+1})\) (\(j=0,\dots,11\)), a \(\mathtt{test\_group}\) block \([ eta+24, eta+186)\), pairs \(C'_{g,j}=(X_{ eta+186+2j},X_{ eta+187+2j})\), the pair \(\omega_g=(X_{ eta+210},X_{ eta+211})\) and its inverse witness \(v_g=X_{ eta+212}\); then \(B=X_{1307}\), \(u_ heta=X_{1308}\) and a \(\mathtt{pole}\) block \([1309,1320)\).

Abbreviations: \(F(t)=t(t+15)(t+20)(t+24)(t+30)(t+60)\) (left to right, the first factor written \(t+0\)); \(a=1-R_0q^2\); \(R=\ell^2a^2R_0\); \(\mathrm{den}_j=R_0(t-1)^2\) for \(j<8\) and \(\mathrm{den}_j=R_0^{25}(t-1)^{26}\) for \(j\ge8\); \(W_g=\prod_{j=0}^{11} igl(1+R\,C_{g,j}'^{\,2} igr)\) in pair arithmetic (with \(R\,u=(Ru_0,Ru_1)\) and \(1=(1,0)\)); \( heta=2\sum_{g=0}^5(\omega_g)_0\).

The formula is the conjunction of, in this order:

  1. \(\eta^2\doteq1\), \((t-1)\,u_1\doteq1\), \(F(t)\,u_2\doteq1\), \(\ell\,u_3\doteq1\), \(R_0(t-1)^8\doteq\eta F(t)\), \(a\,u_4\doteq1\);
  2. for \(g=0,\dots,5\): \(\langle\mathtt{test\_group}[C_0,\dots,C_3,D_{g,0},\dots,D_{g,11}] angle\); the pair equations \(\mathrm{den}_j\,C'_{g,j}\doteq D_{g,j}\) for \(j=0,\dots,11\); and \( igwedge igl(N(W_g)\,v_g\doteq1,\ W_g\cdot\omega_g\doteq(1,0) igr)\);
  3. \( heta\,u_ heta\doteq1\), \(B heta^2\doteq R\), \(\langle\mathtt{pole}[B] angle\).

The polynomial is \(\kappa\) of this conjunction, squared.

This is the normalized six-contact slope certificate: for a slope \(t otin\{0,-15,-20,-24,-30,-60,1\}\) it imposes \(R_0=\eta F(t)/(t-1)^8\), \(a e0\), the normalized tests \(C'_{gj}=D_{gj}/(R_0^{k_j}(t-1)^{k_j+1})\) with \(k_j\in\{1,25\}\), \(W_g e0\), \( heta=\mathrm{Tr}\sum_gW_g^{-1} e0\) and \(\Phi(R/ heta^2)\).

docs.title: The height certificate template
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.heightTemplate ZInQ.Syntax.heightBuild_formula

The template \(\mathtt{height\_certificate}\) has \(36\) parameters and \(35106\) witnesses (\(35142\) variables). Parameters: points \(P_0,P_1,P_2\) (\(P_i=(X_{5i},\dots,X_{5i+4})\)), \(\ell=X_{15}\) and points \(C_0,\dots,C_3\) (\(C_i=(X_{16+5i},\dots,X_{20+5i})\)). Witnesses in allocation order:

  • for \(i=0,1,2\) with base \(b=36+11i\): a \(\mathtt{member}\) block \([b,b+7)\), then \(a_{i0}=X_{b+7}\), \(a_{i1}=X_{b+8}\), \(b_i=X_{b+9}\) and the inverse witness \(u_i=X_{b+10}\);
  • for \(k=0,\dots,8\) with base \(c=69+3897k\): slopes \(s_{k,0},s_{k,1},s_{k,2}=X_c,X_{c+1},X_{c+2}\) and three \(\mathtt{slope}\) blocks \([c+3+1298l,\ c+1301+1298l)\), \(l=0,1,2\).

The nine quantities are \(Q=(a_{00},a_{01},b_0,a_{10},a_{11},b_1,a_{20},a_{21},b_2)\). The formula is the conjunction of, in this order:

  1. for \(i=0,1,2\): \(\langle\mathtt{member}[P_i]\rangle\), \(b_iu_i\doteq1\), \(b_i\,(P_i)_1\doteq a_{i0}\), \(b_i\,(P_i)_2\doteq a_{i1}\);
  2. for \(k=0,\dots,8\): \(s_{k,0}+s_{k,1}+s_{k,2}\doteq Q_k\), and \(\langle\mathtt{slope}[s_{k,l},\ell,C_0,\dots,C_3]\rangle\) for \(l=0,1,2\).

The polynomial is \(\kappa\) of this conjunction, squared. It writes the three abscissas as \(a_{i0}/b_i+(a_{i1}/b_i)s\) with \(b_i\ne0\), expresses each of the nine rational quantities as a sum of three slopes, and imposes the slope certificate on all \(27\) slopes; it is the unguarded certificate, and false triples in the finite box are excluded separately.

This is a definition (template index \(8\)).

docs.title: The fixed-scalar templates
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.scalarTemplate ZInQ.Syntax.scalarTemplate_rel_iff

For a fixed integer expression \(e\) with value \(n=\mathrm{val}(e)\), the template \(S_e\) has \(10\) parameters and \(1\) witness (\(11\) variables): points \(p=(X_0,\dots,X_4)\) and \(r=(X_5,\dots,X_9)\) and the inverse witness \(u=X_{10}\). For an index expression \(e'\) write \(\psi_{e'}=(\Psi_{\mathrm{val}(e'),0},\Psi_{\mathrm{val}(e'),1})(p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4)\), the pair of \(\mathrm{psi}\) nodes at \(x(p),y(p)\). With \(g=\psi_e\), \(g_+=\psi_{e+1}\), \(g_-=\psi_{e+(-1)}\), \(g_2=\psi_{2\cdot e}\) (index expressions \(\mathrm{add}(e,1)\), \(\mathrm{add}(e,-1)\), \(\mathrm{mul}(2,e)\)), the formula is $\(\bigvee\Bigl(\bigwedge(\mathrm{isO}(p),\mathrm{isO}(r)),\ \ \bigwedge\bigl(\mathrm{fin}(p),\ \mathrm{fin}(r),\ N(g)\,u\doteq1,\ g^2\cdot x(r)\doteq x(p)\cdot g^2-g_+\cdot g_-,\ \bigl(2(g^2)^2\bigr)\cdot y(r)\doteq g_2\bigr)\Bigr)\)$ in pair arithmetic, and the polynomial of \(S_e\) is \(\kappa\) of this formula, squared.

The library contains six instances: \(\mathtt{multiply.scalar}=S_{c_*}\) (template index \(9\)) and \(\mathtt{scalar.integer\_constant}_k=S_{\mathrm{integer\_constant}_k}\) for \(k=0,\dots,4\) (template indices \(18,\dots,22\)). The polynomials \(\Psi_{n,c}\) for \(n=c_*\) are never expanded.

The second branch is the denominator-cleared form of \(x(r)=x-\psi_{n+1}\psi_{n-1}/\psi_n^2\) and \(y(r)=\psi_{2n}/(2\psi_n^4)\) with \(\psi_n\ne0\).

ZInQ.Syntax.guardTemplate ZInQ.Syntax.guardTemplate_rel_iff

The template \(\mathtt{multiply.guard}\) has \(15\) parameters and \(1\) witness (\(16\) variables): points \(P_0,P_1,P_2\) (\(P_i=(X_{5i},\dots,X_{5i+4})\)) and the inverse witness \(u=X_{15}\). docs.title: Semantics of the guard template
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.guardTemplate_rel_codes3_iff ZInQ.Syntax.guardTemplate_rel_iff_not_falseTriple_guardPoly

For all \(P_0,P_1,P_2\in\mathbb Q^5\), $\(\mathrm{Rel}_{\mathtt{multiply.guard}}(P_0,P_1,P_2)\iff eg\,\exists\,(a,b,c)\in\mathbb Z^3:\ |a|,|b|,|c|\le T,\ ab e c,\ (P_0,P_1,P_2)=(\iota(a),\iota(b),\iota(c)).\)$ That is, the zero set of \(G_T\) over \(\mathbb Q\) is exactly the finite set of false triples of codes in the box, and the guard holds exactly off that set. Nothing here bounds or evaluates \(T\).

Proof sketch. By the inverse-witness statement the relation holds exactly when \(G_T(P_0,P_1,P_2) e0\), that is, when no factor vanishes. A factor \(\sum_j(D_{abc}X_j-(D_{abc}/B_j)A_j)^2\) vanishes at rational \(X\) exactly when \(D_{abc}X_j=(D_{abc}/B_j)A_j\) for all \(j\), i.e. \(X_j=A_j/B_j\) since \(D_{abc}>0\), i.e. \((X_1,\dots,X_{15})=(\iota(a),\iota(b),\iota(c))\).

docs.title: The multiplication template
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.multiplyTemplate ZInQ.Syntax.multiplyBuild_formula

The template \(\mathtt{multiply}\) has \(15\) parameters and \(35134\) witnesses (\(35149\) variables). Parameters: points \(P_0,P_1,P_2\) (\(P_i=(X_{5i},\dots,X_{5i+4})\)). Witnesses in allocation order: the rational constants \(c_1=X_{15}\) (\(1641/8\)), \(c_2=X_{16}\) (\(-15465/4\)), \(c_3=X_{17}\) (\(87483/32\)), giving the generator point \(G=(0,c_1,-145,c_2,c_3)\); for \(i=0,\dots,3\) a shift point \(S_i=(X_{18+6i},\dots,X_{22+6i})\) followed by an \(S_{c_*}\) block \(\{X_{23+6i}\}\); a \(\mathtt{height\_certificate}\) block \([42,35148)\); and a \(\mathtt{multiply.guard}\) block \(\{X_{35148}\}\).

With \((\Pi_0,\Pi_1,\Pi_2,\Pi_3)=(G,P_0,P_1,P_2)\) and \(\ell\) the node \(\mathrm{fixed}\ \ell\), the formula is the conjunction $\(\varphi_{\rm mul}=\bigwedge\Bigl(\langle S_{c_*}[\Pi_0,S_0]\rangle,\dots,\langle S_{c_*}[\Pi_3,S_3]\rangle,\ \langle\mathtt{height\_certificate}[P_0,P_1,P_2,\ell,S_0,S_1,S_2,S_3]\rangle,\ \langle\mathtt{multiply.guard}[P_0,P_1,P_2]\rangle\Bigr),\)$ and the polynomial, including the global generator equations, is $\([\![\mathtt{multiply}]\!]=(8X_{15}-1641)^2+(4X_{16}+15465)^2+(32X_{17}-87483)^2+\kappa(\varphi_{\rm mul})^2 .\)$

So the four scalar shifts are \(c_*G\), \(c_*P_0\), \(c_*P_1\), \(c_*P_2\), the membership of the three roots is imposed inside the height certificate, and the guard excludes the false triples in the box. That \(\mathrm{Rel}_{\mathtt{multiply}}\) holds exactly on code triples with indices \(a,b,ab\) is the multiplication statement M.

docs.title: The natural-code template
docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.naturalTemplate ZInQ.Syntax.naturalBuild_formula

The template \(\mathtt{natural}\) has \(5\) parameters and \(140604\) witnesses (\(140609\) variables). Parameter: the point \(A=(X_0,\dots,X_4)\). Witnesses in allocation order: points \(\sigma_i=(X_{5+5i},\dots,X_{9+5i})\) and \(\Sigma_i=(X_{25+5i},\dots,X_{29+5i})\) for \(i=0,\dots,3\); four \(\mathtt{multiply}\) blocks \([45+35134i,\ 35179+35134i)\); the point \(\pi_1=(X_{140581},\dots,X_{140585})\) and a \(\mathtt{raw\_add}\) block \([140586,140592)\); the point \(\pi_2=(X_{140592},\dots,X_{140596})\) and a \(\mathtt{raw\_add}\) block \([140597,140603)\); and a \(\mathtt{raw\_add}\) block \([140603,140609)\). The formula is $\(\bigwedge\Bigl(\langle\mathtt{multiply}[\sigma_i,\sigma_i,\Sigma_i]\rangle_{i=0,\dots,3},\ \langle\mathtt{raw\_add}[\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1,\pi_1]\rangle,\ \langle\mathtt{raw\_add}[\pi_1,\Sigma_2,\pi_2]\rangle,\ \langle\mathtt{raw\_add}[\pi_2,\Sigma_3,A]\rangle\Bigr),\)$ and the polynomial is \(\kappa\) of it, squared.

It says that \(A\) is the sum of four squares of indices; that, given the multiplication statement M, its relation holds exactly on \(\iota(\mathbb N)\) is the natural-code semantics.

docs.text:
ZInQ.Syntax.signedEncodeTemplate ZInQ.Syntax.signedEncode_facts

The template \(\mathtt{value.signed\_encode}\) has \(10\) parameters and \(140654\) witnesses (\(140664\) variables). Parameters: points \(N=(X_0,\dots,X_4)\) and \(C=(X_5,\dots,X_9)\). Witnesses in allocation order: points \(Q=(X_{10},\dots,X_{14})\), \(Q_2=(X_{15},\dots,X_{19})\), \(Q_+=(X_{20},\dots,X_{24})\); \(\mathtt{member}\) blocks \([25,32)\) and \([32,39)\); a \(\mathtt{natural}\) block \([39,140643)\); a \(\mathtt{raw\_add}\) block \([140643,140649)\); the rational constants \(c_1=X_{140649}\), \(c_2=X_{140650}\), \(c_3=X_{140651}\) of the generator point \(G=(0,c_1,-145,c_2,c_3)\); and \(\mathtt{raw\_add}\) blocks \([140652,140658)\) and \([140658,140664)\). The formula is $\(\varphi=\bigwedge\Bigl(\langle\mathtt{member}[N]\rangle,\ \langle\mathtt{member}[C]\rangle,\ \langle\mathtt{natural}[Q]\rangle,\ \langle\mathtt{raw\_add}[Q,Q,Q_2]\rangle,\ \bigvee\bigl(\bigwedge(\mathrm{eq}(N,Q),\mathrm{eq}(C,Q_2)),\ \beta\bigr)\Bigr),\)$ $\(\beta=\bigwedge\bigl(\langle\mathtt{raw\_add}[Q,G,Q_+]\rangle,\ \mathrm{eq}(N,\mathrm{neg}(Q_+)),\ \langle\mathtt{raw\_add}[Q_2,G,C]\rangle\bigr),\)$ the two calls in \(\beta\) using the blocks \([140652,140658)\) and \([140658,140664)\), and the polynomial is $\((8c_1-1641)^2+(4c_2+15465)^2+(32c_3-87483)^2+\kappa(\varphi)^2 .\)$ The generator equations stay outside the internal disjunction.

With \(Q=\iota(q)\), \(q\ge0\), the branches are \(C=\iota(2q)\), \(N=\iota(q)\) and \(C=\iota(2q+1)\), \(N=\iota(-(q+1))\): the template says \(N=\iota(\mathrm{dec}(c))\) for \(C=\iota(c)\), \(c\ge0\), where \(\mathrm{dec}(c)=c/2\) for even \(c\) and \(-(c+1)/2\) for odd \(c\).
