docs.title: Model setup
docs.text: sec:model, Section 3, lines 254-266: the field \(K_0=\mathbb Q(s)\), \(s^2=2\), the element \(d=75-53s\), the curve \(E:y^2=x^3-d^2x\), the point \(P_0\), the code of the identity and of an affine point, and the notation \(\iota(n)\) for the code of \([n]P_0\).

docs.title: Generator certificate statement
docs.text: prop:generator, Proposition 3.1, lines 268-270: \(P_0\) has infinite order and \(2E(K_0)=\mathbb ZP_0\). The proof occupies lines 271-348 and cites sources S05-S07.

docs.title: Class number and units
docs.text: Proof of prop:generator, lines 273-276: class number one of \(\mathbb Z[s]\) by the Minkowski bound \(\sqrt2<2\), four unit squareclasses, sign vectors of \(-1\) and \(1+s\).

docs.title: First descent image
docs.text: Proof of prop:generator, lines 277-283: the \(x\)-squareclass map on \(E\), its image in the classes generated by \(-1,1+s,d\), the torsion classes \(1,-1,d,-d\), the change of variables to \(C:y^2=x^3-\delta^2x\) with \(\epsilon=1+s\), \(\delta=3-s\), and the point \(R=(1+s,2s)\).

docs.title: Second descent image
docs.text: Proof of prop:generator, lines 285-288: the curve \(E':y^2=x^3+4d^2x\), total positivity, the valuations at \((s)\) and at \((d)\), and the residue field \(\mathbb F_7\).

docs.title: Descent index
docs.text: Proof of prop:generator, lines 289-291: the exact two-isogeny sequence and \([E(K_0):2E(K_0)]=8\).

docs.title: Torsion bound
docs.text: Proof of prop:generator, lines 293-295: good reductions at \((17,s-6)\) and \((23,s-5)\) with \(20\) and \(24\) points, injectivity of prime-to-residue-characteristic torsion, and torsion equal to the full two-torsion.

docs.title: Rank and odd index
docs.text: Proof of prop:generator, lines 295-297: rank one from the Mordell-Weil theorem and the oddness of the free index of \(R\) from real signs of squareclasses.

docs.title: Duplication bounds
docs.text: Proof of prop:generator, lines 299-313: the duplication forms \(F_2,G_2\) on \(C\), the archimedean bounds with the constant \(676\), the common ideal at \((s)\) and \((\delta)\), and \(4h_x(T)-\log392\le h_x(2T)\le4h_x(T)+\log676\).

docs.title: Height comparison
docs.text: Proof of prop:generator, lines 314-322: the canonical height normalization, the bound \(h_x(T)\le2\widehat h(T)+\log392/3\), \(x(2R)=(57-28s)/8\) with height \(\log41\), the bound for \(h_x(S)\), and the integer comparison \(41^3\cdot676\cdot392^{36}<9^{108}\).

docs.title: Finite search
docs.text: Proof of prop:generator, lines 324-344: the search box for nonrational and rational abscissas, the exact square test, the seven surviving abscissas, the counts 7,004, 14,008 and 111, and the identification of the four nontorsion survivors with \(R+T\).

docs.title: Transfer to the generator
docs.text: Proof of prop:generator, lines 346-347: \(2C(K_0)=\mathbb Z(2R)\) and the inverse change of variables sending \(2R\) to \(P_0\).

docs.title: Membership and addition
docs.text: Section 3.1, lines 350-371: the membership system for \(2E(K_0)\), nonzero preimage ordinates, the raw addition contract \(\operatorname{Add}_{\rm raw}(\iota(a),\iota(b),R)\iff R=\iota(a+b)\) and its branches, and the remarks on typing in multiplication and in the natural predicate.

docs.title: Division polynomials
docs.text: Section 2.2, lines 210-236: the normalized division polynomials \(f_n\) on \(y^2=x^3+Ax\), \(\psi_n=f_n\) or \(2yf_n\), their recurrences, the multiplication formulas \(x([n]P)=\phi_n/\psi_n^2\), \(y([n]P)=\omega_n/\psi_n^3\), the fixed-scalar ordinate equation \(2y([n]P)\psi_n(P)^4=\psi_{2n}(P)\), and the nonvanishing of \(\psi_n(P)\) on the torsion-free carrier.

docs.title: Rational constants and inverses
docs.text: Section 2.1, lines 180-188: rational constants as equations \(qc=p\), the generator equations \(8g_0=1641\), \(4g_1=-15465\), \(32g_2=87483\), and inverses as equations \(uv=1\).

docs.title: Point references and fixed point codes
docs.text: Appendix app:literal, lines 6672-6710: point references \(-1,-2,-3\), the generator equations in every model recipe, the psi_component constructor with \(A=(-11243,7950)\), and the positive fixed point codes \(x_n=x(P_0)-\psi_{n+1}\psi_{n-1}/\psi_n^2\), \(y_n=\psi_{2n}/(2\psi_n^4)\).

docs.title: Template witness counts
docs.text: Appendix app:literal, lines 6737-6764: parameter and witness counts of the templates, including member (5 parameters, 7 witnesses), raw_add (15, 6) and the five scalar.integer_constant templates (10, 1).

docs.title: Translation typing
docs.text: Section 10.4, lines 6052-6058: member forces a canonical code in \(D\), raw addition forces the canonical sum, and the fixed scalar graph gives \([m]Q\) on \(D\).

docs.title: Generator sources
docs.text: Source table, lines 6619-6622: S05 (generator certificate), S06 (rank, torsion, codes) and S07 (exact finite algorithm).

docs.title: Sutherland lecture notes
docs.text: Bibliography entry sutherland, lines 11140-11143: A. V. Sutherland, Isogeny kernels and division polynomials, MIT 18.783, Lecture 5, Sections 5.5-5.6.

docs.title: Silverman
docs.text: Bibliography entry silverman, lines 11144-11145: J. H. Silverman, The arithmetic of elliptic curves, second edition, Springer, 2009, Chapters IV and VII.

docs.title: Locators for the multiplication chapter
docs.text: Line ranges refer to diophantine_zq.tex in this repository (the 11/5 manuscript, SHA-256 cb1148cd6c7769d2af3f1636b60ff0ada4b40431978d1e98d0c339274b3d792b). TeX labels are given where the item has one. The JavaScript generators under construction/ are project-authored artifacts; they are listed last and serve as cross-checks of the shapes and constants, not as inputs to the proof.

docs.title: Multiplication input M
docs.text: Section 1 (sec:main), lines 96-97: the input M of Lemma 1.2: the actual guarded multiplication template has rational witnesses exactly for triples with indices \(a,b,ab\). Lines 129-131 (proof of Theorem 1.1) assign M to Section 6, on all rational input codes, including the finite false-triple guard.

docs.title: Assembly lemma
docs.text: lem:assembly, Lemma 1.2, lines 110-121: assuming G, M, H, PC, C and B, the specified polynomial satisfies Theorem 1.1.

docs.title: Least formal multiple
docs.text: Section 2.2, lines 238-252: the fixed prime catalogue, \(N_s=(\prod_{p\le324}p)H_{\rm cat}\), the definition of \(M_0\) as the least \(m\ge1\) with \(N_s^4\mid a,b\) and \(\gcd(c,N_s)=1\) for \(1/x([m]P_0)=(a+bs)/c\), and the remark that bounding \(T\) does not by itself exclude false triples.

docs.title: Membership and addition
docs.text: Section 3.1, lines 351-374: membership in \(2E(K_0)\) is an all-input statement; multiplication first imposes membership of its three roots and is sound on arbitrary rational tuples.

docs.title: Contact prime sets
docs.text: End of Section 4, lines 967-971: \(S_{\rm ht}=\{p:p\le324\}\) and \(S_{\rm mul}=S_{\rm ht}\cup\mathcal H\cup\operatorname{supp}(c_*)\), with \(\mathcal H\) the fixed catalogue; a common numerical \(R\) may bound both sets.

docs.title: Pole predicate
docs.text: sec:pole, Section 5, lines 973-987: \(S_0=\{2,3,5,7,13\}\), the eleven witnesses, the multiplier \(m\), \(A=mB\), \(H=A(A-B^2)\), \(T_1\), \(T_2\), \(Q_{\rm pole}\), \(\Phi(B)\); for \(B\ne0\), \(m\) is a signed divisor of \(2730\) and the equations give points \((A,r_1)\in E_e\) and \((Az^2,zr_2)\in E_{eH}\) with \(eHz\ne0\), where \(E_\ell:y^2=x(x-\ell)(x+3\ell)\); total degree \(75\). The blueprint uses the Route K polynomial instead, with the factors \(A+e\) and \(Az^2+eH\) and the curves \(y^2=x(x-\ell)(x+\ell)\); see the Route K locators.

docs.title: One-sided obstruction
docs.text: lem:pole, Lemma 5.1, lines 988-991, proof lines 992-1000: if \(B\ne0\) and \(\Phi(B)\), then \(v_p(B)\) is not negative and odd for any \(p\notin S_0\).

docs.title: Pole completeness
docs.text: hyp:PC, Theorem 5.2, lines 1001-1004. Used here only as the hypothesis of the completeness direction; for the Route K polynomial it is proved from the certified rank hypothesis CR₃.

docs.title: Section 6 opening
docs.text: sec:mult, Section 6, lines 1123-1129: the template forces membership of its three inputs inside the height certificate; accepted untyped inputs have unique indices; the template has \(35{,}134\) rational witnesses (construction S03, specification S13).

docs.title: Local conventions
docs.text: Lines 1131-1149: \(z=-x/y\), \(w=1/x\) with \(w(O)=0\), \(w=z^2\) times an integral unit; the formal logarithm converges on \(v(z)>0\) and is an isometry on \(v(z)>e/(p-1)\) (Silverman IV.5.5, IV.6.3-6.4); the relative error estimate \((r-1)v(z)-e\,v_p(r)>0\); \(\log([n]Q)=n\log(Q)\) and \(v(z([n]Q))=v(z(Q))+v(n)\); identification with the reduction kernel of a minimal model (Silverman VII.2.1-2.2).

docs.title: Logarithm series
docs.text: Lines 1150-1161: the invariant differential \(dx/(2y)=dz/\sqrt{1+4d^2z^4}\), the series \(\log(z)=\sum_j(-1)^j\binom{2j}{j}d^{2j}z^{4j+1}/(4j+1)\), and the estimate: at a contact prime \(p>324\) with \(v(z)\ge1\), \(v(p)=1\), every omitted term relative to \(z\) has valuation at least \(r-1-v_p(r)\ge28\) for \(r\ge29\), so \(L(z)/16575=\log(z)(1+\epsilon_z)\) with \(v(\epsilon_z)\ge28\).

docs.title: Twelve tests
docs.text: Lines 1162-1176: \(H=[h]P_0\), \(U_i=[z_i]P_0\), \(V_0=H-[c_*]P_0\), \(V_i=U_i-[c_*n_i]P_0\), \(c_*=4M_0\); the truncated logarithm \(L\); the twelve tests (four inverse abscissas, four conjugate counterparts, three differences of \(L\)-ratios, one product test); identity inverse abscissas are zero and all denominators are guarded.

docs.title: Slope predicate
docs.text: Lines 1177-1192: for a slope \(t\notin\mathcal C\cup\{1\}\), \(R_0=\eta F(t)/(t-1)^8\), \(\eta^2=1\), \(a=1-R_0q^2\ne0\), \(R=\ell_0^2a^2R_0\); the normalized values \(C_{gj}=D_{gj}/(R_0^{k_j}(t-1)^{k_j+1})\) with \(k_j=1\) (\(j\le8\)) and \(25\) (\(j\ge9\)); six groups, \(W_g=\prod_j(1+RC_{gj}^2)\), \(\Theta=\operatorname{Tr}\sum_gW_g^{-1}\), both nonzero, and \(\Phi(R/\Theta^2)\); the pole input is nonzero.

docs.title: Local congruence
docs.text: Lines 1194-1213: at a positive odd contact prime outside \(S_{\rm mul}\), the factor valuations, the trace and Lemma 5.1 give one common group and place with the first eight tests of valuation at least one and the last four at least \(25\); the formal group, the unit among \(h,h-c_*\), the full-log and truncated ratios, and \(p^{25}\mid n_1n_2-n_3\).

docs.title: Height certificate
docs.text: Lines 1215-1223: the abscissas \(x_{i0}+x_{i1}s\) (zero at the identity), \(b_ix_{ij}=a_{ij}\) with \(b_i\ne0\), each of the nine quantities a sum of three slopes, the slope predicate on all \(27\) slopes, membership of the three inputs; the multiplication predicate conjoins it with the scalar graphs and the inverse of the guard.

docs.title: Finite-box deduction
docs.text: prop:box, Proposition 6.1, lines 1225-1229, proof lines 1230-1246: every false triple accepted by the unguarded certificate has \(\max_i|n_i|<T=(48A_{\rm ht})^{13}\); the constants \(12A_{\rm ht}\), \(B_0=4\log3+\tfrac32\log2+2\log(1+\sqrt2)+\tfrac13\log676<10\) and \(2\widehat h(P_0)>1\).

docs.title: Finite guard
docs.text: Lines 1248-1259: the guard factors \(g_{abc}\) over false triples in \([-T,T]^3\); a false accepted triple makes its own factor zero; at a true triple every factor is positive by injectivity of codes; the sound direction uses the generator and the height theorem but not pole completeness.

docs.title: Prime pattern
docs.text: prop:fixed-prime-pattern, Proposition 6.2, lines 1267-1297 (statement); its proof, lines 1299-1704, is replaced in this project by the hypothesis 22P.

docs.title: Choice of shifts
docs.text: Lines 1705-1723: the nine integral homogeneous quantities of a true triple; at most six odd-contact primes per slope; \(h\equiv0\pmod{\operatorname{lcm}(M_0,d_1)}\), \(h\equiv c_*\pmod{d_2}\), compatibility via \(\gcd(d_1,d_2)=4\); a solution larger than \(c_*\); one private group per contact prime; \(U_i=[n_i]H\).

docs.title: Fixed local clearing
docs.text: Lines 1723-1730: \(S_b=S_{\rm ht}\cup\mathcal H\), \(B_p\), \(C_p=14B_p\), \(D_p=51C_p\), \(|v_p(R_0)|,|v_p(t-1)|\le C_p\), \(v_p(D_{gj})\ge0\) at \(S_b\) from the small formal subgroup of \(M_0\), \(v_p(C_{gj})\ge-D_p\), \(v_p(\ell_0)=E_p=52C_p+v_p(12)+4\).

docs.title: Pole input of a completed slope
docs.text: Lines 1732-1748: weak approximation for \(q\); \(\eta\) with \(R_0>0\); at \(S_b\), \(v_p(RC_{gj}^2)\ge2E_p-C_p-2D_p>v_p(12)\) and \(v_p(R/\Theta^2)\ge103C_p+8\ge4\); at a selected odd-contact prime \(v_p(R)=1\) and the trace residues; even valuation elsewhere; positivity in both real embeddings and \(R/\Theta^2\to0\) as \(a\to0\).

docs.title: Conclusion of the multiplication proof
docs.text: Lines 1748-1754: the hypotheses of PC hold, negative and zero indices and coincident points are handled by the group-law branches, and M holds, with completeness for every integer triple \((n_1,n_2,n_1n_2)\) and soundness on arbitrary rational input codes.

docs.title: Least formal multiple exists
docs.text: Proof of prop:cutoff, Proposition 12.1, lines 6310-6349: the search defining \(M_0\) succeeds by \(N_s^4m_0\), so \(1\le M_0\le N_s^{10}\).

docs.title: Generator height
docs.text: Proof of prop:generator, lines 303-325: the duplication bounds on \(C\), the comparison \(h_x(T)\le2\widehat h(T)+\log392/3\), and \(x(2R)=(57-28s)/8\) of height \(\log41\).

docs.title: Silverman
docs.text: J. H. Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, 2nd ed., cited at lines 1132-1149: IV.1 (the parameters \(z\) and \(w\)), IV.5.5 (the formal logarithm and its coefficients), IV.6.3-6.4 (the logarithm is an isomorphism on \(v(z)>e/(p-1)\)), VII.2.1-2.2 (the reduction kernel and the formal group).

docs.title: Multiplication certificate generator
docs.text: construction/multiplication-certificate.js (project-authored): the definitions of raw_z, raw_inverse_x, log25, pole, test_group (twelve tests, precisions \(1,\dots,1,25,25,25,25\)), slope (normalizations \(R_0(t-1)^2\) and \(R_0^{25}(t-1)^{26}\), six groups, the trace \(2\sum_g(\omega_g)_0\)) and height_certificate.

docs.title: Fixed constant prescription
docs.text: construction/fixed-certificate-constants.js (project-authored): the prescription of \(P_0\), \(W\), the catalogue, \(N_s\), \(M\), \(c_*\), \(\ell\), \(D\), \(G_0\), \(E_0\), \(R\), \(Q\), \(B_{\rm cm}\), \(C_{\rm cm}\), \(A_{\rm height}\) and \(T\), never evaluated.

docs.title: Six-contact finite checks
docs.text: construction/verify-six-contact.js (project-authored): among other finite identities, the clearing inequalities \(2E_p-C_p-2D_p>v_p(12)\) and \(2E_p-C_p-2v_p(12)\ge4\) for \(B_p\in\{1,4\}\) and \(v_p(12)\in\{0,1,2\}\).

docs.title: Locators for the progressions chapter
docs.text: The progressions chapter replaces the explicit progression estimate of Bennett, Martin, O'Bryant and Rechnitzer, which the manuscript cites in the proof of Proposition 12.1, by a self-contained effective form of Dirichlet's theorem. Its statements are textbook results, made explicit; the sources below are cited at the level of chapters. The quantitative constants are this blueprint's own and are not taken from the sources.

docs.title: Apostol, Chapter 3
docs.text: T. M. Apostol, Introduction to Analytic Number Theory, Springer, 1976, Chapter 3 (averages of arithmetical functions): Euler's summation formula and the partial sums \(\sum_{n\le x}1/n\) and \(\sum_{n\le x}\log n/n\) used for the bounds on \(L(\sigma,\chi)\) and its derivative.

docs.title: Apostol, Chapter 4
docs.text: Apostol, Chapter 4 (elementary theorems on the distribution of primes): Chebyshev's functions \(\psi\) and \(\theta\), Abel's identity, the formula \(\log\lfloor x\rfloor!=\sum_{n\le x}\Lambda(n)\lfloor x/n\rfloor\) and the estimate \(\sum_{n\le x}\Lambda(n)/n=\log x+O(1)\) (Mertens' first theorem).

docs.title: Apostol, Chapter 6
docs.text: Apostol, Chapter 6 (finite abelian groups and their characters): Dirichlet characters, the orthogonality relations, sums involving Dirichlet characters (the bound \(q\) for character sums and the tails of \(\sum\chi(n)/n\) and \(\sum\chi(n)\log n/n\)), and the nonvanishing of \(L(1,\chi)\) for real \(\chi\).

docs.title: Apostol, Chapter 7
docs.text: Apostol, Chapter 7 (Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions): the asymptotic formula for \(\sum_{p\le x,\ p\equiv h\ (\mathrm{mod}\ k)}\log p/p\), proved from Mertens' theorem, orthogonality and the identity relating \(L(1,\chi)\sum_{n\le x}\chi(n)\Lambda(n)/n\) to \(\sum_{n\le x}\chi(n)\log n/n\); the route of the counting section follows it with explicit constants.

docs.title: Apostol, Chapter 9
docs.text: Apostol, Chapter 9 (quadratic residues and the quadratic reciprocity law): Legendre and Jacobi symbols, the supplementary laws for \(-1\) and \(2\), and reciprocity, used in the classification of real characters.

docs.title: Apostol, Chapter 11
docs.text: Apostol, Chapter 11 (Dirichlet series and Euler products): Euler products of multiplicative functions, and differentiation of Dirichlet series term by term in the half-plane of absolute convergence.

docs.title: Davenport, Chapter 1
docs.text: H. Davenport, Multiplicative Number Theory, third edition (revised by H. L. Montgomery), Graduate Texts in Mathematics 74, Springer, 2000, Chapter 1 (primes in arithmetic progression): Dirichlet's proof, where the nonvanishing of \(L(1,\chi)\) for real \(\chi\) comes from the class number of a quadratic field.

docs.title: Davenport, Chapter 4
docs.text: Davenport, Chapter 4 (primes in arithmetic progression: the general modulus): characters to a general modulus, their decomposition over the prime powers of the modulus, and the nonvanishing of \(L(1,\chi)\) for complex \(\chi\) by the product \(\zeta^3|L(\cdot,\chi)|^4|L(\cdot,\chi^2)|\ge1\).

docs.title: Davenport, Chapter 5
docs.text: Davenport, Chapter 5 (primitive characters): real characters, and the description of the real primitive characters by Kronecker symbols, which the classification of real characters follows on primes not dividing \(2q\).

docs.title: Davenport, Chapter 6
docs.text: Davenport, Chapter 6 (Dirichlet's class-number formula): the factorization of the Dedekind zeta function of a quadratic field as \(\zeta(s)L(s,\chi)\) and the formula expressing \(L(1,\chi)\) through the class number, the regulator and the number of roots of unity.

docs.title: Marcus, Chapter 2
docs.text: D. A. Marcus, Number Fields, Springer, 1977, Chapter 2 (number fields and number rings): quadratic fields, their rings of integers and discriminants.

docs.title: Marcus, Chapter 3
docs.text: Marcus, Chapter 3 (prime decomposition in number rings): the relation \(\sum_ie_if_i=n\), the decomposition of primes in quadratic fields, and the Kummer–Dedekind criterion.

docs.title: Marcus, Chapter 5
docs.text: Marcus, Chapter 5 (the ideal class group and the unit group): roots of unity, Dirichlet's unit theorem and the regulator.

docs.title: Marcus, Chapter 7
docs.text: Marcus, Chapter 7 (the Dedekind zeta function and the class number formula): the Dedekind zeta function as the Dirichlet series of ideal counts, its residue at \(s=1\), and its factorization for quadratic fields. Mathlib's class number formula (NumberField.tendsto_sub_one_mul_dedekindZeta_nhdsGT) follows this chapter.

docs.title: Locators for the row-5b chapter
docs.text: The row-5b determinant is not in the manuscript. Its mathematics is written in the project-authored research note docs/research/tyz-5b.md of this repository, a specification written for this project and checked by an automated referee, not a published source. The published works it uses, and the published theorems that the hypotheses CR₃^5b and CR₃^TYZ rest on, are cited at the end.

docs.title: Notation
docs.text: docs/research/tyz-5b.md, Notation: the bits \(a_{ij}=(p_j/p_i)_+\), \(y_i=(-1/p_i)_+\), \(z_i=(2/p_i)_+\), Smith's matrix \(L\) (Smith's \(A\)), the matrices \(M_1\) and \(M_{5b}\), and the genus sum \(T_{5b}(n)\) of row 5b of Smith's Table 2.

docs.title: Lemma 2.1
docs.text: docs/research/tyz-5b.md §2.1: the forest lemma, \(\det L[U\setminus F,U\setminus W]\) as a sum over the forests rooted at \(F\) with one element of \(W\) in every tree, and its proof (expansion of the diagonal, cancellation of cycles, the unique compatible bijection of a forest). The section states that all determinants are taken over \(\mathbb F_2\), where they equal permanents.

docs.title: Lemma 2.2
docs.text: docs/research/tyz-5b.md §2.1, Consequences and Lemma 2.2: \(\kappa_\rho(B)\) counts spanning arborescences; the column sums \(c_v=y_v(1+y(B))\); equal cofactors when \(y(B)=1\); \(\det L_B[B\setminus j,B\setminus i]=\kappa_j(B)\); and the \(\kappa\)-difference \(\kappa_i+\kappa_j=\sum_\varphi\mathrm{wt}(\varphi)c(T_i(\varphi))\).

docs.title: Proposition 2.3
docs.text: docs/research/tyz-5b.md §2.2: Rédei's formulas \(g(B)=\kappa(B)\) if \(y(B)=1\) and \(g(B)=\sum_\rho z_\rho\kappa_\rho(B)\) if \(y(B)=0\) (rows \(n\bmod4=3,1\) of Smith's Table 1), and the consequences (2.1) and (2.2). The row-5b chapter takes the right-hand sides as the definition of Rédei's \(g\). Their derivation from genus theory is followed, by a different route, in the Rédei chapter.

docs.title: Propositions 3.3 and 3.4
docs.text: docs/research/tyz-5b.md §3.1: the forest forms of \(\det M_1\) and \(\det M_{5b}\) and their partition forms. The formal proofs replace Lemmas 3.1 and 3.2 and the involution expansion by a rank-one update and the matrix \(P(c,d)=\begin{pmatrix}D_d&L^{\mathsf T}\\L&D_c\end{pmatrix}\).

docs.title: Proposition 3.5
docs.text: docs/research/tyz-5b.md §3.2: for \(y(S)=0\), the sums of \(\prod g(B)\) over the partitions into class-1 blocks and into class-3 blocks agree (row 1 of Smith's Table 2), by comparing forest sums and counting perfect matchings of trees.

docs.title: Theorem 3.6
docs.text: docs/research/tyz-5b.md §3.3: Theorem 3.6, \(T_{5b}(n)=\det M_{5b}\) for \(n\equiv5\pmod8\) (Smith, arXiv:1603.08479, Theorem 2.2, row 5b of Table 2). The note checks it on random abstract data and on PARI class groups (§6), and docs/research/rv-cr5b-sec3.md §4 checks \(T_{5b}=\det M_{5b}\) against PARI on 30 values of \(n\).

docs.title: Lemma 4.1
docs.text: docs/research/tyz-5b.md §4.1: for odd squarefree \(n\equiv5\pmod8\) the Selmer system of docs/research/slot-k.md §2.1 for the class \(c=5\), the torsion classes \((-1,-n)\) and \((n,2)\), the subspace \(H\) (\(b_1=0\), \(a_0=\lambda\cdot u\)) and the isomorphism \(H\cong\ker M_1\), \((a,b)\mapsto(u+v,u)\). The Lean proof works first for any configuration of product class \(5\) and then transfers to \(\mathrm{Sel}_2(C_n)\) through Proposition 0.

docs.title: Lemma 4.2
docs.text: docs/research/tyz-5b.md §4.2 (recalled from docs/research/pc-audit.md, rule RK6): the determinant of a symmetric corank-one matrix over \(\mathbb F_2\) bordered by a vector. The note proves it with the adjugate; the Lean proof argues with kernels instead (module docstring of RouteK/Rank5b/Bordered.lean).

docs.title: Theorem 4.3
docs.text: docs/research/tyz-5b.md §4.2: the rule of row 5b, \(\det M_{5b}=\sum_{p\mid a}y_p\) for a non-torsion Selmer class on a Selmer-minimal curve.

docs.title: Corollary 4.4
docs.text: docs/research/tyz-5b.md §4.2: a first coordinate \(\beta\) with \(|\beta|_{\rm odd}\equiv3\pmod4\) forces \(\det M_{5b}=1\). The Lean statement takes the 2-adic shape of CR₃^Sel, \(|a|\equiv7\pmod8\).

docs.title: Row 5b of Smith's table
docs.text: docs/research/tyz-5b.md §§2–3: the forest lemma, Rédei's formulas in terms of the cofactors \(\kappa_\rho(B)\), and Theorem 3.6, \(T_{5b}(n)=\det M_{5b}\) for \(n\equiv5\pmod8\) (Smith's Theorem 2.2, row 5b, reproved). Theorem 3.6 of the row-5b chapter follows these sections with one change of route: both sides are written as the same forest sum, the determinant through a rank-one update of the matrix \(P(z,y)\) and the genus sum through a marked form glued along the partition. So the proof does not pass through Proposition 3.5 or the partition form of Proposition 3.4, which are proved separately. Rédei's formulas are proved from genus theory in the Rédei chapter.

docs.title: The hypothesis in Tian-Yuan-Zhang form
docs.text: KERNEL_PLAN.md, the paragraph beginning "That step is done": the hypothesis CR₃^TYZ (for squarefree \(n\equiv5\pmod8\) with \(\#\mathrm{Sel}_2(C_n)=8\) and \(T_{5b}(n)\) odd, every Selmer class comes from a rational point) and its trust statement, which names Tian–Yuan–Zhang through Proposition N, Rédei's formula and Gross–Zagier. docs/research/rv-cr5b-sec3.md: a referee report on CR₃^TYZ, covering its definitions (\(\kappa\), \(g\), \(T_{5b}\) and the edge cases, §1), its trust statement (§2) and the proof chain to CR₃^5b (§3), with a numeric red team against PARI on 30 values of \(n\) (§4). The class-number form CR₃^TYZ_Cl is located in the locators of the Rédei chapter.

docs.title: Proposition N
docs.text: docs/research/nt-tyz.md §4: Proposition N. For squarefree \(n\equiv5\pmod8\), if \(T_{5b}(n)=\sum_{d_0\equiv7,\,d_1\equiv3}g(d_0)g(d_1)\mathcal L_1(n/d_0d_1)\) is odd, then \(\mathcal L(n)\ne0\) and \(\operatorname{ord}_{s=1}L(C_n,s)=1\) (the note writes \(E_n\) for \(C_n\)). It is proved from Tian–Yuan–Zhang's Theorem 3.5 (first assertion), Theorem 3.3 (the \(\varepsilon\)-classes of the recursion), Proposition 3.2(1), Lemmas 3.16, 3.18 and 3.21, Lemma 2.9 (the convolution identity, cited as Lemma 2.8 before the locator audit docs/research/locators.md, AI agents, 2026-11-12; Lemma 2.8 is the symmetry lemma), Proposition 2.3 and the recursion of their §3.1. §4.5 gives the recommended citation; their Theorem 1.2 (Theorem 1.4 of the journal version, per the same audit) must not be cited in its literal form. Proposition N is not refereed; it has two model reviews, docs/research/rv-nt-tyz.md and docs/research/rv-prop-n.md (the second written without the source text of Tian–Yuan–Zhang; verdict: it holds as stated, relative to the inputs as quoted, with presentational corrections recorded at the end of docs/research/nt-tyz.md).

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: docs/research/tyz-5b.md §6: random checks of the lemmas on abstract data and on actual curves, and the slot curves; §7 records an independent automated referee run.

docs.title: Tian-Yuan-Zhang
docs.text: Y. Tian, X. Yuan, S.-W. Zhang, Genus periods, genus points and congruent number problem, Asian J. Math. 21 (2017), no. 4, 721–774; arXiv:1411.4728. Theorem 3.5(2) and its proof in §3.3; docs/research/tyz-5b.md §1.2 locates the form used (if \(T_{5b}(n)\) is odd, then \(2^{-\rho(n)}\mathcal L(n)\) is odd) in that proof; the form used holds as completed by Proposition N (see above), not by Proposition 3.4 as written (docs/research/nt-tyz.md §2.3).

docs.title: Gross-Zagier-Kolyvagin
docs.text: The manuscript's Lemma 5.5 (lem:forward-rank): analytic rank one implies rank one, by Gross–Zagier and Kolyvagin. The justification of the hypotheses here does not use it: Gross–Zagier over an auxiliary field (below) gives rank at least one, which is all that is needed (docs/research/cr3-trust.md §1, D4).

docs.title: Gross-Zagier over an auxiliary field
docs.text: B. Gross and D. Zagier, Heegner points and derivatives of L-series, Invent. Math. 84 (1986), 225–320, applied with an auxiliary imaginary quadratic field \(K\) that satisfies the Heegner hypothesis and has \(L(C_n^K,1)\ne0\) (Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein). docs/research/cr3-trust.md §1, D2 names the suppliers: Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein, Waldspurger, or Friedberg–Hoffstein, not Murty–Murty (the derivative case); their theorem numbers, and whether the level \(32n^2\) is allowed, are still to be checked. The curve \(C_n\) is modular because it has complex multiplication by \(\mathbb Z[i]\). Only "analytic rank one implies rank at least one" is used; Kolyvagin's theorem is not needed (docs/research/pc-audit.md RK7).

docs.title: Smith
docs.text: A. Smith, The congruent numbers have positive natural density, arXiv:1603.08479, Table 2 and Theorem 2.2. Only the matrix of row 5b is used; its identity with the genus sum is reproved in the note.

docs.title: Matrix-tree theorem
docs.text: S. Chaiken, A combinatorial proof of the all minors matrix tree theorem, SIAM J. Algebraic Discrete Methods 3 (1982), no. 3, 319–329, cited by docs/research/tyz-5b.md §2.1 (which gives only the journal and year). Lemma 2.1 is its case over \(\mathbb F_2\); the title, issue and pages were not checked against the journal here.

docs.title: Locators for the positive-rank chapter
docs.text: The positive-rank step is not in the manuscript. It is record RK9 of the project-authored audit note docs/research/pc-audit.md; the positive-rank forms of the hypothesis follow the narrowing N2 of the project-authored note docs/research/cr3-map-literature.md; and the form on the two curves of a slot choice is reviewed in the project-authored note docs/research/rv-cr3-dl.md, with the plan KERNEL_PLAN.md. The section deriving CR₃^TYZ_Cl,Rk from three literature statements follows the project-authored notes docs/research/wk-cr3.md (the plan and the statements) and docs/research/rv-lit.md (its model review, whose verdict is to adopt with two changes), with the paragraph of KERNEL_PLAN.md that records the result. Its subsection computing \(L(C_d,s)\) follows §4.2 of the project-authored note docs/research/wk-cr3.md. These are notes written for this project, not published sources. The standard facts on the 2-descent and on heights, and the deep theorems behind the hypotheses, are cited at the end.

docs.title: The complete 2-descent map
docs.text: The map \(P\mapsto(x-e_1,x-e_2)\) modulo squares on a curve \(y^2=(x-e_1)(x-e_2)(x-e_3)\) with full rational 2-torsion, with the stated values at the 2-torsion points, is a homomorphism with kernel \(2E(K)\): J. H. Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, 2nd ed., Springer (2009), Proposition X.1.4, as cited by docs/research/pc-audit.md RK8, which records its use for \(C_d\). The proposition number was not rechecked against the book.

docs.title: Halving
docs.text: docs/research/cr3-map-literature.md §8, N2, Lean cost (i): the Kummer map \(C_d(\mathbb Q)\to(\mathbb Q^*/\mathbb Q^{*2})^2\) is a homomorphism with kernel \(2C_d(\mathbb Q)\), by the lemma that \(x\), \(x\pm d\) squares make \((x,y)\) halvable (classical, elementary). The explicit half, with \(x'=x+r_1r_2+r_1r_3+r_2r_3\) where \(r_i^2=x-e_i\), is the standard formula for curves with full 2-torsion.

docs.title: RK9
docs.text: docs/research/pc-audit.md §3, record RK9 (and §2.2): if \(\dim\mathrm{Sel}_2(C_d)=3\) and \(\operatorname{rank}C_d(\mathbb Q)\ge1\), then \(C_d(\mathbb Q)/2C_d(\mathbb Q)\), which injects into \(\mathrm{Sel}_2\) and has dimension \(2+\operatorname{rank}\ge3\), equals \(\mathrm{Sel}_2\), so every Selmer class comes from a rational point, which can be taken of infinite order. No pairing and no finiteness of \(Ш\) are needed. The count uses that \(C_d(\mathbb Q)\) is finitely generated.

docs.title: Two-torsion of the congruent number curves
docs.text: docs/research/tyz-5b.md §1.3, item "No prescribed class": \(C_n(\mathbb Q)[2]=(\mathbb Z/2)^2\) (standard), so \(\dim C_n(\mathbb Q)/2C_n(\mathbb Q)=2+\mathrm{rank}\).

docs.title: Mordell-Weil for the congruent number curves
docs.text: KERNEL_PLAN.md, section "What can and cannot be formalized", the paragraph beginning "These hypotheses all conclude": \(C_d(\mathbb Q)\) is finitely generated for every \(d\ne0\), from the two-isogeny descent and the descent theorem with heights, so that a point of infinite order and \(\#\mathrm{Sel}_2(C_d)=8\) give every Selmer class. docs/research/cr3-map-literature.md §8, N2, Lean cost (iii): a height descent for \(C_d\) over \(\mathbb Q\) of the kind already done for the generator curve. docs/research/pc-audit.md record RK9: the counting argument that uses finite generation.

docs.title: The positive-rank form
docs.text: docs/research/cr3-map-literature.md §0 (the cleanest narrowing) and §8, N2 (CR3^rk, the recommended trust statement): the same premises, with the conclusion that \(C_d(\mathbb Q)\) contains a point of infinite order. This is what Kriz, Tian–Yuan–Zhang with Gross–Zagier, and finiteness of \(Ш(C_d)[2^\infty]\) each conclude; the note argues that it is equivalent to CR₃ through RK9 and Proposition 0. Only the implication CR₃^Rk ⇒ CR₃ is proved here, not the converse. KERNEL_PLAN.md, the paragraph beginning "These hypotheses all conclude": the forms CR₃^Rk, CR₃^TYZ,Rk and CR₃^TYZ_Cl,Rk, the implications CR₃^TYZ_Cl,Rk ⇒ CR₃^TYZ,Rk (Rédei's formula) and CR₃^TYZ,Rk ⇒ CR₃^Rk (Corollary 4.4 and Theorem 3.6), and the main-theorem variants. docs/research/rv-cr3-dl.md §2.1 reviews the second implication.

docs.title: Row 5b and Redei
docs.text: docs/research/tyz-5b.md Corollary 4.4 (a Selmer first coordinate \(\beta\) with \(|\beta|_{\rm odd}\equiv3\pmod4\), in particular \(|\beta|\equiv7\pmod8\), forces \(\det M_{5b}=1\)) and Theorem 3.6 (\(\det M_{5b}=T_{5b}(d)\) for squarefree \(d\equiv5\pmod8\)); docs/research/tyz-5b.md §2.2 and docs/research/redei-plan.md for Rédei's formula, which identifies \(T_{5b}(d)\) with the genus sum of Tian–Yuan–Zhang's class numbers.

docs.title: The two curves of a slot choice
docs.text: docs/research/rv-cr3-dl.md §1.1: pole completeness applies the rank hypothesis at exactly two curves, \(C_{d_1}\) and \(C_{d_1|\theta|}=C_{d_2}\) of a slot choice. Quantifying over every triple \(\beta,\theta,p_0\) that satisfies the inputs makes the hypothesis stronger than needed. The existential slot choice makes it weaker, which is legitimate because pole solubility holds for any slot choice. The form over admissible inputs quantifies only over admissible \(B\). §1.2: the inputs can hold (\(\beta=-7\), \(\theta=1\), \(p_0=7\), where a slot choice gives \(d_1=7q_0\) for a prime \(q_0\equiv3\pmod8\)), slot data exist whenever they hold, and no slot choice is degenerate (\(d_1\ge21\), and both 2-Selmer groups have order \(8\)). docs/research/cr3-map-needs.md §1 (L4) and §2 (W3): the proof of pole completeness applies CR₃ only at these two curves, and W3 is the drop-in narrowing of CR₃ that keeps the construction of the descent. KERNEL_PLAN.md, the paragraph beginning "The proof applies CR₃ at only two curves".

docs.title: Positive rank on the two curves
docs.text: KERNEL_PLAN.md, the paragraph beginning "These hypotheses all conclude": RK9 (with Mordell–Weil for \(C_d(\mathbb Q)\), a point of infinite order and a 2-Selmer group of order \(8\) make every Selmer class come from a rational point) and the positive-rank forms CR₃^Rk and CR₃^TYZ,Rk; the next paragraph, for CR₃^DL,Rk and CR₃^DL,Adm,Rk. docs/research/rv-cr3-dl.md §1.4 (CR₃^Rk implies CR₃^DL,Rk: the 2-Selmer group of each curve of a slot choice has order \(8\) and contains a class with first coordinate \(\beta\)), §2.1 (Corollary 4.4 and Theorem 3.6 give an odd genus sum \(T_{5b}\)) and §2.3 (the chain from these hypotheses to Tian–Yuan–Zhang's input, an odd genus sum with their own class numbers).

docs.title: The infinitely-many-points forms
docs.text: A project-authored restatement, not taken from the manuscript or from any published source: KERNEL_PLAN.md, the paragraph beginning "These hypotheses all conclude", records that the four positive-rank hypotheses CR₃^Rk, CR₃^TYZ,Rk, CR₃^TYZ_Cl,Rk and CR₃^DL,Rk are restated with the conclusion that \(y^2=x^3-d^2x\) has infinitely many rational solutions, so that the hypotheses can be read without the group law, and that each form is equivalent to its positive-rank form through Mordell–Weil for \(C_d\) (see Mordell-Weil for the congruent number curves above). For squarefree \(d>0\) this conclusion is the classical statement that \(d\) is a congruent number; that reading is standard background and no proof here uses it.

docs.title: The literature form of CR3
docs.text:
KERNEL_PLAN.md, section "What can and cannot be formalized", the three sentences beginning "ZInQKernel/MainLiterature.lean splits CR₃ further" (in the paragraph after the Lean display that follows "CR₃ itself follows in Lean from a positive-rank statement"): CR₃ is split further into three statements about the L-series of an elliptic curve, namely that for every elliptic curve over \(\mathbb Q\) a simple zero of \(L(E,s)\) at \(s=1\) gives a point of infinite order, the functional equation of \(L(C_d,s)\) with conductor \(32d^2\) and root number \(-1\) on the critical strip, and that \(L(C_d,s)\) vanishes to order at most one at \(s=1\) when \(T^{\rm Cl}_{5b}(d)=1\). The first two are textbook theorems; the third is Tian–Yuan–Zhang's Theorem 3.5(2) in the reading that Proposition N proves, which no refereed text prints (KERNEL_PLAN's wording). Of the texts read for this project, only Smith's unrefereed preprint prints that reading (docs/research/nt-tyz.md Verdict 1 and §3: Tian's two expository articles were not read; the journal version of Tian–Yuan–Zhang was compared with the arXiv version only by the locator audit, see Reading A of Tian-Yuan-Zhang).

docs/research/rv-lit.md, cited first: §0 (verdict: adopt, with the functional equation restricted to \(0<\operatorname{Re}s<2\) and the Gross–Zagier statement renamed with its twist supplier corrected); §1.2 (each adopted statement is true given its cited theorem, and none is vacuous or trivially true); §3 (faithfulness of the Gross–Zagier statement, the functional equation and row 5b); §6 (the adopted statements are the drafts apart from those two changes); §7 (the repairs to the notes, including repair N1).

docs/research/wk-cr3.md §2.1 (the definitions: entire continuation, its uniqueness, the completed L-function) and §2.3 (the proofs: vanishing at the centre from the functional equation at \(s=1\), analytic rank one, and CR₃^TYZ_Cl,Rk from row 5b, vanishing at the centre and Gross–Zagier); §2.2 gives the draft statements and §3 their faithfulness table; both are superseded for the functional equation (now restricted to \(0<\operatorname{Re}s<2\)) and for the Gross–Zagier statement (renamed, twist supplier corrected) by the note at the end of wk-cr3 and by rv-lit §6 and §7 (repair N1). These are project notes, not published sources.

docs.title: The L-series of an elliptic curve
docs.text: For a Weierstrass equation \(E\) over \(\mathbb Q\), \(L(E,s)\) is the Euler product over the primes \(p\) of \(f_p(p^{-s})^{-1}\), where \(f_p\) is the local polynomial of a minimal model over \(\mathbb Q_p\), with Silverman's factors: \(1-a_pT+pT^2\) with \(a_p=p+1-\#\tilde E(\mathbb F_p)\) for good reduction, \(1-T\) for split and \(1+T\) for nonsplit multiplicative reduction, and \(1\) for additive reduction. docs/research/wk-cr3.md §1.2 (item "The L-function") and §3 (paragraph "The L-series definition": for odd squarefree \(d\) the model \(y^2=x^3-d^2x\) has \(\Delta=64d^6\) and \(c_4=48d^2\), is minimal at every prime, has good reduction off \(2d\) and additive reduction at \(2\) and at \(p\mid d\); PARI confirms conductor \(32d^2\), root number \(-1\), minimality and the local data on 20 squarefree \(d\equiv5\pmod8\) below 4000). docs/research/rv-lit.md §2 (the recipe checked by reading for every residue characteristic, including split and nonsplit multiplicative reduction at \(2\) and \(3\), and, for a transcription of that recipe (the defined series itself cannot be computed), against PARI's coefficients up to \(n=300\) on 29 curves, non-minimal models among them, with no mismatch). docs/research/wk-cr3.md §3 (residual risk) records that no proved statement linked the defined series to point counts, and that a mismatch would make the literature statements false, not vacuous; for \(C_d\) with odd squarefree \(d\) the link is now proved (see the L-series of the congruent number curves below), and for other curves it is not. The normalization is arithmetic, with centre \(s=1\); the series converges absolutely for \(\operatorname{Re}s>3/2\) by Hasse's bound (STANDARD; wk-cr3 §3, rv-lit §1.1).

docs.title: Entire continuation
docs.text: docs/research/wk-cr3.md §1.2 (item "Analytic continuation"): the order of vanishing at \(s=1\) is taken of an entire function that agrees with the series on \(\operatorname{Re}s>3/2\), and such a function is unique. docs/research/rv-lit.md §1.1: the half-plane is \(\operatorname{Re}s>3/2\), not \(\operatorname{Re}s>1\), because on \(\operatorname{Re}s>3/2\) the series converges absolutely (Hasse), while on \(\operatorname{Re}s>1\) it need not converge and no entire function need agree with it; an entire continuation exists for every elliptic curve over \(\mathbb Q\), since \(E\) is modular (Breuil–Conrad–Diamond–Taylor) and the L-function of a weight-2 newform is entire (Hecke), and for \(C_d\) by Deuring and Hecke (STANDARD), so the statements that quantify over all entire continuations are not vacuous; and since a continuation is not identically zero, its order of vanishing at \(s=1\) is finite.

docs.title: Minimal equations over a discrete valuation ring
docs.text: Over a discrete valuation ring with valuation \(v\): a change of variables \(x=u^2x'+r\), \(y=u^3y'+su^2x'+t\) multiplies \(\Delta\) by \(u^{-12}\) and \(c_4\) by \(u^{-4}\); an equation with coefficients in the ring and \(v(\Delta)<12\) is minimal; two minimal equations differ by a change of variables with \(u\) a unit and \(r,s,t\) in the ring; and for a minimal equation the reduction is good if \(v(\Delta)=0\), multiplicative if \(v(\Delta)>0\) and \(v(c_4)=0\), and additive if \(v(\Delta)>0\) and \(v(c_4)>0\). J. H. Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, 2nd ed., Springer (2009), §III.1 (changes of variables, Table 3.1), §VII.1 (minimal equations: the criterion \(v(\Delta)<12\) and the uniqueness up to a change of variables with \(u\) a unit) and Proposition VII.5.1 (the reduction types). docs/research/rv-lit.md §2 (an AI model review) cites Proposition VII.5.1 and checks by reading that the local polynomial used for \(L(E,s)\) takes the minimal equation over the completion, with these reduction types and Silverman's factors; docs/research/wk-cr3.md (an AI-authored project note) §1.2 (item "The L-function") records the same check. The section numbers other than VII.5.1 are not cited by any project note and were not checked against the book. That the local polynomial at a place of good reduction, or of additive reduction with nonzero discriminant, can be read off any minimal equation, not only a chosen one, is proved here from minimality: for nonzero discriminant, a change of variables between two minimal equations has \(v(u)=0\) (the unit half of Silverman's uniqueness statement). A change of variables, and an isomorphism of fields applied to the coefficients, preserve the number of points over a field (STANDARD).

docs.title: The L-series of the congruent number curves
docs.text:
For odd squarefree \(d\), the equation \(y^2=x^3-d^2x\) has \(\Delta=64d^6=(2d)^6\) and \(c_4=48d^2\); it is minimal at every prime, since \(p^{12} mid(2d)^6\); it has good reduction at the primes \(p mid2d\) and additive reduction at \(2\) and at the primes \(p\mid d\). So the local factor of \(L(C_d,s)\) is \(1-a_pT+pT^2\) with \(a_p=p+1-\#C_d(\mathbb F_p)=p-\#\{(x,y)\in\mathbb F_p^2:y^2=x^3-d^2x\}\) at the primes \(p mid2d\), and \(1\) at the primes \(p\mid2d\), where the coefficient \(a_p\) is \(0\); the coefficients are multiplicative, and \(L(C_d,s)\) is the Dirichlet series of the Euler product over the primes \(p mid2d\). The formula \(a_p=p-\#\{(x,y)\}\) holds only at the primes \(p mid2d\); the minimality and the additive reduction are stated for odd squarefree \(d\), while good reduction at \(p mid2d\) holds for every \(d\). The completion of \(\mathbb Q\) at \(p\) is \(\mathbb Q_p\), with valuation ring \(\mathbb Z_p\), uniformizer \(p\) and residue field \(\mathbb F_p\) (STANDARD).

docs/research/wk-cr3.md (an AI-authored project note) §4.2 ("Medium investment"): the plan of this computation, namely that the model is minimal at every prime with good reduction for \(p mid2d\) and additive reduction for \(p\mid2d\), and that the coefficient at \(p\) is \(p-\#\{(x,y)\in\mathbb F_p^2: y^2=x^3-d^2x\}\) for \(p mid2d\) and \(0\) for \(p\mid2d\), to remove the risk that the definition of \(L(E,s)\) used here differs from the textbook one. Its third item (\(a_p=0\) for \(p\equiv3\pmod4\)) and its optional Hasse's bound for \(C_d\) are not proved here. The checks of the same facts by reading and by PARI (wk-cr3 §3, rv-lit §2) are recorded under the L-series of an elliptic curve; the residual risk named in wk-cr3 §3, that no lemma connects the definition to point counts, is what this computation removes, for odd squarefree \(d\).

N. Koblitz, Introduction to Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms, 2nd ed., Graduate Texts in Mathematics 97, Springer (1993), Chapter II: the zeta function of \(y^2=x^3-n^2x\) over \(\mathbb F_p\) and its Hasse–Weil L-function. docs/research/cr3-trust.md item D1 cites Chapter II of this book for the conductor \(32d^2\) of \(C_d\) (odd squarefree \(d\)), as an unverified locator; no project note cites it for the zeta function or the point counts of \(C_d\), and the chapter was not checked here.

docs.title: Hecke and Deuring
docs.text: \(C_d\) has complex multiplication by \(\mathbb Z[i]\), so \(L(C_d,s)\) is the L-function of a Hecke character of \(\mathbb Q(i)\) (Deuring; Hecke), which is entire and satisfies a functional equation (STANDARD; locators not checked; the primary-source locator audit docs/research/locators.md, AI agents with web access, 2026-11-12, did not read an original source for it: its row for the functional equation is UNVERIFIED as a complete original-supplier audit). docs/research/wk-cr3.md §1.2 (item "Analytic continuation") and §4.3 (proving this here would need Hecke L-functions of \(\mathbb Q(i)\) and Deuring's identification of \(L(C_d,s)\); out of reach); docs/research/rv-lit.md §1.1 (existence of the continuation for \(C_d\)) and the row for Hecke's continuation in the table of §1.2 (true, STANDARD).

docs.title: The functional equation and the root number
docs.text:
With \(\Lambda(s)=N^{s/2}(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)L(C_d,s)\), the functional equation is \(\Lambda(2-s)=w\Lambda(s)\), with conductor \(N=32d^2\) for odd squarefree \(d\) and root number \(w=-1\) for \(d\equiv5,6,7\pmod8\): Deuring and Hecke for the functional equation, and B. J. Birch and N. M. Stephens, Topology 5 (1966), for the sign, cited as docs/research/cr3-trust.md B9 cites it (title and pages not checked here). The locator audit docs/research/locators.md (row FunctionalEquation5) did not read Birch–Stephens's theorem or page, and found that the conductor \(32d^2\) and the functional equation still need a fully read original source (UNVERIFIED); the root number \(-1\) for squarefree \(d\equiv5,6,7\pmod8\) is printed in Tian–Yuan–Zhang's table (arXiv:1411.4728v1, p. 2 of the PDF; journal p. 722). The conductor \(32d^2\) for odd squarefree \(d\) is standard (docs/research/cr3-trust.md §1, D1, cites Koblitz, GTM 97, Ch. II; locator not checked); it is checked with PARI for 20 squarefree \(d\equiv5\pmod8\) below 4000 (docs/research/wk-cr3.md §3) and for the first 30 such \(d\), from \(5\) to \(285\) (docs/research/rv-lit.md §3.2). The statement used here is restricted to \(0<\operatorname{Re}s<2\), on which neither \(s\) nor \(2-s\) is a pole of \(\Gamma\), and is used only at \(s=1\).

docs/research/rv-lit.md, cited first: §1.2 (the form for every \(s\) is false at \(s=0\), where the gamma factor is taken to be \(0\) while \(L(C_d,2)\ne0\), with values \(0.911\), \(1.024\), \(0.904\) for \(d=5,13,21\); on the strip the identity holds, checked numerically to \(2\cdot10^{-17}\) at three points for \(d=5,13,21\)) and §3.2 (PARI gives conductor \(32d^2\) and root number \(-1\) for the first 30 squarefree \(d\equiv5\pmod8\), from \(5\) to \(285\); the normalization is the standard one). docs/research/wk-cr3.md, the closing note (the adopted form holds on the strip only and suffices, since the proof uses \(s=1\)), and its §3 row for the functional equation only as superseded: it calls the all-\(s\) draft true; see rv-lit §1.2 and its repair N1.

docs.title: Reading A of Tian-Yuan-Zhang
docs.text:
Theorem and proposition numbers are those of arXiv:1411.4728v1 (Theorem 3.5 is label m3), the version the project's notes read (docs/research/nt-tyz.md §1.1 and the numbering warning of §3). The primary-source locator audit docs/research/locators.md (AI agents with web access, 2026-11-12; not a human check; rows "TYZRow5b / reading A: arXiv" and "TYZ journal comparison") read the author-hosted typeset journal version (Asian J. Math. 21 (2017), no. 4, 721–774): there Theorem 3.5(2) is on p. 740 and the proof of Proposition 3.4 on pp. 751–753; the arXiv Theorem 1.2 is Theorem 1.4 (pp. 723–724), which keeps the restriction that every factor exceed \(1\), while the journal's Theorem 1.2 is a different result; and neither version's Theorem 3.5(2) settles the partition convention. The journal's proof was not assessed on Proposition 3.4. For \(n\equiv5\pmod8\) the second sum of Tian–Yuan–Zhang's Theorem 3.5(2) has terms of two types, \((7,3)\) and \((5,1)\), and the \((5,1)\) terms admit three readings. Reading A admits \(d_1=1\), so the blocks other than the one \(\equiv5\) form any, possibly empty, partition into blocks \(\equiv1\pmod8\); the sum is then \(T^{\rm Cl}_{5a}(n)\), and the theorem says that if \(2^{-\rho(n)}\mathcal L(n)\) is even then \(T^{\rm Cl}_{5a}(n)\) and \(T^{\rm Cl}_{5b}(n)\) are both even (their sums, with \(g(d)=\#2\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d}))\); the vault's \(T^{\rm Cl}\)). The printed Theorem 3.5(2) permits reading A, and their proof of Proposition 3.4 needs it; the printed Theorem 1.2 (journal Theorem 1.4), whose last sentence selects the other readings, is false as written in both versions (for \(n=26565\) and \(33117\), which have rank \(3\) and so \(\mathcal L(n)=0\), the second sum under those readings is odd; nt-tyz §1.4) and is not cited (docs/research/nt-tyz.md §1.3–1.4). Only the case \(\mathcal L(n)=0\), that is, order of vanishing at least two, is needed. The printed hypothesis is a condition on their genus point \(P(n)\), followed by an "i.e." that restates it as "\(2^{-\rho(n)}\mathcal L(n)\) even" and is not proved in the paper; when \(\mathcal L(n)=0\) the condition on \(P(n)\) follows from the first assertion of their Theorem 3.5 and their Lemma 3.18, so the "i.e." is not needed (nt-tyz §2.2, fact F6, and §4.1). Proposition N proves reading A in this form (its first sentence) from unambiguous statements of Tian–Yuan–Zhang (nt-tyz §4); it is unpublished, written for this project, with two model reviews (rv-nt-tyz, rv-prop-n) and no human review. The only printed statement of reading A found is A. Smith, arXiv:1603.08479, Theorem 2.1, with the two sums as separate rows; it is unrefereed. The journal version of Tian–Yuan–Zhang was compared only by the locator audit, as above, and Tian's expository articles (Notices of the ICCM 5 (2017); Proc. ICM 2022) were not read (nt-tyz §3; wk-cr3 §0).

docs/research/wk-cr3.md §1.1 (reading A is the true form; row 5a is rejected as an alternative; the smallest gap is Lemmas N1, N2 and fact F5 of Proposition N) and the §3 rows for row 5b and for reading A (where the \(T_{5a}\) sum is called new in the draft and not reviewed; it is checked in rv-lit §3.3, a model review only). docs/research/rv-lit.md §3.3: row 5b is the contrapositive of the \(T_{5b}\) half of Proposition N, weakened to order at most one, and needs the existence of the continuation (Hecke); the \(T_{5a}\) sum, with one block \(\equiv5\) and the rest \(\equiv1\pmod8\), including the one-block partition, matches reading A's \(T_{5a}\) by reading; an independent sample of 30 values of \(d\) (the rank-3 cases \(26565\) and \(33117\), and the first 28 squarefree \(d\equiv5\pmod8\) with at least two primes \(\equiv3\) or \(7\pmod8\)) found no violation of row 5b or of reading A.

docs.title: Kriz
docs.text: D. Kriz, Supersingular main conjectures, Sylvester's conjecture and Goldfeld's conjecture, arXiv:2002.04767, Theorem 10.13: the rank-one 2-converse theorem for curves with CM by \(\mathbb Z[i]\), a preprint whose publication status was not checked (docs/research/pc-audit.md RK1; docs/research/cr3-map-literature.md §4, C4; docs/research/rv-lit.md N2). With the corank lemma (see the Route K locators, Cassels-Tate) it gives \(\operatorname{rank}C_d(\mathbb Q)=1\) when \(\dim\mathrm{Sel}_2(C_d)=3\). Its construction assumes \(f_0\ge4\), where \(f_0\) is the odd part of \(|d|\); for odd squarefree \(d\equiv5\pmod8\) this holds, since \(f_0=d\ge5\) (RK1). It is an alternative route that the hypotheses do not need (docs/research/nt-tyz.md §5.1).

docs.title: Tian-Yuan-Zhang
docs.text: Y. Tian, X. Yuan, S.-W. Zhang, Genus periods, genus points and congruent number problem, Asian J. Math. 21 (2017), no. 4, 721–774; arXiv:1411.4728. Theorem 3.5 and the argument of the proof of Theorem 3.5(2), §3.3, as completed in docs/research/nt-tyz.md §4, Proposition N: for squarefree \(n\equiv5\pmod8\) with odd genus sum \(T_{5b}(n)\), \(L(C_n,s)\) vanishes to order exactly one at \(s=1\) (docs/research/cr3-map-literature.md §4, C2). Their genus class number is \(g(n)=\#2\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n}))\) (§1). The literature section states Theorem 3.5(2) for \(n\equiv5\pmod8\) in reading A with both sums, with hypothesis \(\mathcal L(n)=0\) (see Reading A of Tian-Yuan-Zhang above). Row 5b uses only the \((7,3)\) sum, in contrapositive form: if \(T^{\rm Cl}_{5b}(n)\) is odd then \(\mathcal L(n)\ne0\). By their definition \(\mathcal L(n)=0\) exactly when \(L(C_n,s)\) vanishes to order greater than one at \(s=1\) (TYZ L318–345, nt-tyz I7, as cited in docs/research/wk-cr3.md §1.2). For order one the definition uses a regulator, and so presupposes the rank part of the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture in analytic rank one, which they cite from Coates–Wiles, Rubin, Gross–Zagier and Kolyvagin (docs/research/cr3-trust.md B9). Theorem, lemma and section numbers here and in Reading A of Tian-Yuan-Zhang are those of arXiv:1411.4728v1 (docs/research/nt-tyz.md §1.1, the numbering warning in §3, and §5.2 item 2). The locator audit docs/research/locators.md (AI agents) read the journal version: Theorem 1.2 is renumbered Theorem 1.4 there, Theorem 3.5(2) keeps its number (p. 740), and the convolution lemma is Lemma 2.9 in both versions; the other numbers were not compared.

docs.title: Gross-Zagier
docs.text: B. Gross and D. Zagier, Heegner points and derivatives of L-series, Invent. Math. 84 (1986), 225–320, applied with an auxiliary imaginary quadratic field that satisfies the Heegner hypothesis and has \(L(C_d^K,1)\ne0\) (Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein). docs/research/cr3-trust.md §1, D2 names the suppliers: Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein, Waldspurger, or Friedberg–Hoffstein, not Murty–Murty (the derivative case); their theorem numbers, and whether the level \(32d^2\) is allowed, are still to be checked. Only "analytic rank one implies rank at least one" is used; Kolyvagin's finiteness of \(Ш\) is not needed, and \(C_d\) is modular since it has CM by \(\mathbb Z[i]\) (docs/research/pc-audit.md RK7). The literature section states the positive-rank half for every elliptic curve over \(\mathbb Q\): a simple zero of \(L(E,s)\) at \(s=1\) gives a point of infinite order. Modularity is Breuil–Conrad–Diamond–Taylor, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 14 (2001) (Shimura 1971 for CM curves); the auxiliary twist comes from Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein, Invent. Math. 102 (1990) (through Waldspurger) or Friedberg–Hoffstein, Ann. of Math. 142 (1995); Kolyvagin, Math. USSR Izv. 32 (1989), adds that the rank is exactly one, which is not used (STANDARD: these texts were not read here; their theorem numbers, and the hypotheses on the level under which the auxiliary field exists, are unchecked for every conductor, not only for \(32d^2\)) (docs/research/rv-lit.md §3.1; docs/research/wk-cr3.md closing note; docs/research/cr3-trust.md §1, D2-D3).

docs.title: Silverman-Tate
docs.text: J. H. Silverman and J. Tate, Rational Points on Elliptic Curves, Undergraduate Texts in Mathematics, Springer (1992). Chapter I, §4: the explicit formulas for the group law (the chord through two points, the tangent at one, and the third intersection with the cubic). Chapter III, for the curves \(y^2=x^3+ax^2+bx\) and \(y^2=x^3-2ax^2+(a^2-4b)x\): the two-isogeny between them and the homomorphism \(\alpha\) to \(\mathbb Q^\times/\mathbb Q^{\times2}\) (§4); Mordell's theorem, where the index of \(2\Gamma\) is bounded by the sizes of the images of \(\alpha\) and \(\bar\alpha\), which lie in the classes of the divisors of \(b\) and of \(a^2-4b\) (§5); and finite generation from the height lemmas (§§1–3). No project note cites this book, and the chapter and section numbers were not checked.

docs.title: Silverman, descent and heights
docs.text: J. H. Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, 2nd ed., Springer (2009): the descent theorem for an abelian group with a height (Theorem VIII.3.1); heights on elliptic curves over number fields, with the naive height, the approximate parallelogram law and the finiteness of points of bounded height (§VIII.6); descent via two-isogeny for \(y^2=x^3+ax^2+bx\) (Proposition X.4.9). No project note cites these numbers, and they were not checked.

docs.title: Locators for the Rédei chapter
docs.text: Rédei's formula is not in the manuscript. The plan of its proof is the project-authored research note docs/research/redei-plan.md of this repository, written for this project and not a published source; the formulas themselves are derived in docs/research/tyz-5b.md §2.2. The published works are cited at the end.

docs.title: The target
docs.text: docs/research/redei-plan.md §§1.1–1.2. Tian–Yuan–Zhang's genus class number is \(g(d)=\#(2\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d})))\), the subgroup of squares of the class group of the ring of integers, not the 2-torsion; the note checked this against the LaTeX source of arXiv:1411.4728v1, lines 361–366 and 998. The field is modelled as \(\mathbb Q[\omega]/(\omega^2+n)\), and the target is \(g(d_B)\equiv g_d(B)\pmod 2\) for nonempty \(B\) (\(B=\emptyset\) is excluded, since \(g(1)=1\) while Rédei's bit of \(\emptyset\) is \(0\)).

docs.title: The hypothesis in class-number form
docs.text: docs/research/redei-plan.md §1.3: the genus sum \(T^{\mathrm{Cl}}_{5b}(d)\) with Tian–Yuan–Zhang's own \(g\), the hypothesis CR₃^TYZ_Cl, and the passage from Rédei's formula to \(T^{\mathrm{Cl}}_{5b}=T_{5b}\) and CR₃^TYZ_Cl ⇔ CR₃^TYZ (blocks of a set partition are nonempty).

docs.title: The chosen route
docs.text: docs/research/redei-plan.md §3.1, route (c): genus characters \(\chi_q([\mathfrak a])=(N\mathfrak a/q)\) for the primes \(q\mid n\), Dirichlet's theorem for their surjectivity, and the count \([\mathrm{Cl}:2\mathrm{Cl}]=\#\mathrm{Cl}[2]\le2^{t-1}\le\#\mathrm{im}\,\chi\le[\mathrm{Cl}:2\mathrm{Cl}]\), in place of Hasse–Minkowski or Legendre's theorem. Two simplifications: only the odd characters are needed (image all of \(\mathbb F_2^r\) for \(n\equiv1\pmod4\) and the sum-zero hyperplane for \(n\equiv3\pmod4\)), and \(\chi_q\) is well defined with integral ideals only, since \(N(\alpha)=\alpha\sigma(\alpha)\) is a square modulo \(\mathfrak p_q\).

docs.title: Step 1: the field
docs.text: docs/research/redei-plan.md §3.2, step 1: \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})\) as a number field with two automorphisms, the integrality of \(\omega\) and of \(\theta=(1+\omega)/2\) for \(n\equiv3\pmod4\), the norm \(N(x)=x\sigma(x)\ge0\), \(\mathcal O\cap\mathbb Q=\mathbb Z\) and the rational units \(\pm1\), \(\sigma\omega=-\omega\).

docs.title: Step 2: primes
docs.text: docs/research/redei-plan.md §3.2, step 2: the splitting trichotomy, ramified primes divide \(n\) or are \(2\) with \(n\equiv1\pmod4\) (residue-field argument with \(x=\omega\) and \(x=\theta\)), the primes of the discriminant ramify, the ideals \(\mathfrak p_p\), \((\omega)=\prod_{p\mid n}\mathfrak p_p\), and \(I\cdot\sigma I=(NI)\).

docs.title: Step 3: ambiguous classes
docs.text: docs/research/redei-plan.md §3.2, step 3 (the step (G1)): Hilbert 90 at the integral level (\(x\sigma I=yI\) gives \(Nx=Ny\), then \(\nu=\sigma x(x+y)\)), invariant ideals by strong induction on the norm, the map \(\psi\), \(\mathrm{im}\,\psi=\mathrm{Cl}[2]\) and \(\#\mathrm{Cl}[2]\le2^{t-1}\).

docs.title: Step 4: genus characters
docs.text: docs/research/redei-plan.md §3.2, step 4: representatives prime to \(q\), the characters \(\chi_q\) and their homomorphism property, and \(\chi_q(\psi e)=\sum_pR_{qp}e_p\) with \(R_{qp}=(p/q)\), \(R_{qq}=((n/q)/q)\), \(R_{q2}=(2/q)\), using \([\mathfrak p_q]=\prod_{p\ne q}[\mathfrak p_p]\) from \((\omega)=\prod\mathfrak p_p\).

docs.title: Step 5: Dirichlet's theorem
docs.text: docs/research/redei-plan.md §3.2, step 5: a prime \(p\nmid2n\) with \(-n\) a square modulo \(p\) splits (it is not inert, since \((m+\omega)(m-\omega)\in p\mathcal O\) and \(\sigma\) give \(p\mid2m\)); the surjectivity of the genus characters from residues, the Chinese remainder theorem, Dirichlet's theorem on primes in progressions and Jacobi reciprocity for \((-n/p)=1\).

docs.title: Step 6: the 4-rank
docs.text: docs/research/redei-plan.md §3.2, step 6: \(\#G^2\) odd iff \(G[2]\cap G^2=1\), \(\#(G/G^2)=\#G[2]\), \(\mathrm{Cl}^2=\bigcap\ker\chi_q\) by counting, and the 4-rank statement: \(g(n)\) is odd iff the kernel of the Rédei matrix is \(\{0,e_n\}\) (Rédei's theorem in its 4-rank-0 form). The statement needs \(n>1\): for \(n=1\) the class group is trivial, but the vector at the prime \(2\) lies in the kernel of the empty matrix.

docs.title: Step 7: the kernel
docs.text: docs/research/redei-plan.md §3.2, step 7, in the general setting of bits with reciprocity: the kernel of \((L_B\mid z_B)\) (the column \(z_B\) only if \(y(B)=0\)) is trivial iff Rédei's bit is \(1\). This is tyz-5b §2.2, Cases 1 and 2, with Lemma 2.2(2) and the row- and column-sum facts.

docs.title: Step 8: the bridge
docs.text: docs/research/redei-plan.md §3.2, step 8: the primes of \(d_B\) are those of \(B\), \(d_B\equiv3\pmod4\) iff \(y(B)=1\), the Rédei matrix of \(d_B\) becomes the Laplacian of the bits of \(d\) bordered by \(z\), and Rédei's formula follows from the 4-rank statement.

docs.title: Redei's formulas
docs.text: docs/research/tyz-5b.md §2.2, Proposition 2.3: for \(\emptyset\ne B\) and \(d=d_B\), \(g(d)=\kappa(B)\) if \(y(B)=1\) and \(g(d)=\sum_{\rho\in B}z_\rho\kappa_\rho(B)\) if \(y(B)=0\) (the rows \(n\bmod4=3,1\) of Smith's Table 1). The derivation from genus theory there uses (G1) ambiguous classes, (G2) and (G3) Hasse–Minkowski, and Cases 1 and 2 for the kernel; the Rédei chapter follows route (c) of redei-plan in place of (G2) and (G3).

docs.title: The kernel plan
docs.text: KERNEL_PLAN.md, the paragraph beginning "That step is done": Rédei's formula is proved, so CR₃^TYZ_Cl, with Tian–Yuan–Zhang's own \(g(d)=\#2\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d}))\), is equivalent to CR₃^TYZ. The next paragraph, beginning "These hypotheses all conclude": CR₃^TYZ_Cl,Rk implies CR₃^TYZ,Rk, by Rédei's formula.

docs.title: Redei 1934
docs.text: L. Rédei, J. reine angew. Math. 171 (1934), cited by docs/research/tyz-5b.md §2.2 for the classical facts (G1)–(G3) of genus theory. The note marks its exact theorem numbers UNCHECKED, and they were not checked either. The title, Arithmetischer Beweis des Satzes über die Anzahl der durch vier teilbaren Invarianten der absoluten Klassengruppe im quadratischen Zahlkörper, and the pages 55–60 were also not checked against the journal.

docs.title: Tian-Yuan-Zhang
docs.text: Y. Tian, X. Yuan, S.-W. Zhang, Genus periods, genus points and congruent number problem, Asian J. Math. 21 (2017), no. 4, 721–774; arXiv:1411.4728. §1: the genus class numbers \(g(d):=\#(2\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d})))\) and the remark that by Rédei their parity is computed by the Rédei matrix; Theorem 3.5 and the proof of Theorem 3.5(2) (§3.3) for the hypothesis in class-number form.

docs.title: Cox
docs.text: D. A. Cox, Primes of the form \(x^2+ny^2\), §6, as cited by docs/research/redei-plan.md §3.1 for the classical proof that the number of genera is \(2^{t-1}\). The section number was not checked. The Rédei chapter obtains the principal genus theorem by counting instead.

docs.title: Locators for the route AP chapter
Locators for the route AP chapter
docs.text: Route AP is not in the manuscript. It replaces the twenty-two-prime pattern of Proposition 6.2 by long arithmetic progressions of good slope primes, through a change in the completeness proof of Section 6 that leaves the polynomial unchanged. The mathematics is written in the project-authored research note docs/research/nt-22p.md of this repository, a specification written for this project, not a published source; it was checked by three model referee runs and a Lean-statement audit (docs/research/rv-nt22p-*.md, docs/research/aud-ap.md). The published theorem it uses is cited at the end.

docs.title: Lemma P
docs.text: docs/research/nt-22p.md §3.2, "Lemma P (pole absorption)": the hypotheses (a slope \(t=u/v\) in lowest terms with \(e=v_\ell(v)\ge1\), \(e\ge3\) at \(\ell=2\), and the seven numbers \(u-cv\), \(c\in\mathcal C\cup\{1\}\), prime to \(\ell\)), parts (1)–(3) and their proofs. The numerical check of the same section (30 samples) motivates the condition \(e\ge3\) at \(2\).

docs.title: The modified completeness argument
docs.text: docs/research/nt-22p.md §3.2, "The modified completeness argument": field 2′ replacing field 2 of the slope conditions, the choice of \(q\) in the ball of Lemma P(2) at the primes where field 2′ uses its second alternative, and the valuation bookkeeping at the other primes, which is the manuscript's (Section 6, the completeness of the slope certificate).

docs.title: The progression form
docs.text: docs/research/nt-22p.md §3.3: the statement 22P_AP, Proposition AP and its proof (the slopes \(u/v\), \(A+10-u/v\) and \(-10\) from a progression of length \(K_A+1\)), with the remarks on why field 2′ cannot be avoided.

docs.title: Green–Tao implies 22P_AP
docs.text: docs/research/nt-22p.md §3.4: Szemerédi's theorem in the primes applied to the good slope primes above \(\max S_b\), which have positive relative density by Proposition D (§2 of the same note, proved in docs/research/pd-paper.md).

docs.title: Green–Tao 2008
docs.text: B. Green and T. Tao, The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions, Ann. of Math. 167 (2008), 481–547, Theorem 1.2 (Szemerédi's theorem in the primes).

docs.title: Locators for the Route K chapter
Locators for the Route K chapter
docs.text: Route K is not in the manuscript. It changes the pole polynomial of Section 5 to the congruent number curves \(y^2=x(x-\ell)(x+\ell)\) and replaces the restricted converse (Theorem 5.3) and the simultaneous descent of Section 5.1 by an explicit descent lemma and one narrow hypothesis on congruent number curves. The mathematics is written in project-authored research notes in docs/research/ of this repository; they are specifications written for this project, not published sources. The deep theorems that the hypothesis CR₃ rests on are cited at the end.

docs.title: Soundness for the congruent number curves

docs.text: docs/research/cr3-trust.md, a project-authored note: the forms of the hypothesis CR₃ that the variants of the main theorem take, and the implications between them (§0); a numbered outline of the argument for the class-number form in positive-rank form, with a supplier and a status for every step (§1): the match of the statement with Tian–Yuan–Zhang's quantities (Part A), their deep results (Part B), Proposition N (Part C), Gross–Zagier with an auxiliary imaginary quadratic field from Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein, Waldspurger or Friedberg–Hoffstein, with the theorem numbers and the level still to be checked (Part D, which also records that the manuscript's Lemma 5.5 and Kriz's 2-converse are not used), and the steps proved here (Part E); and what remains outside refereed sources (§2). docs/research/rv-cr3-trust.md is a model review of that note.

docs.title: Kriz
docs.text: D. Kriz, Supersingular main conjectures, Sylvester's conjecture and Goldfeld's conjecture, arXiv:2002.04767v5 (2022), Theorems 10.13 and 10.17(2): the 2-converse theorem in rank one for curves with CM by \(\mathbb Z[i]\). docs.title: Tian-Yuan-Zhang
docs.text: Y. Tian, X. Yuan and S.-W. Zhang, Genus periods, genus points and congruent number problem, Asian J. Math. 21 (2017), no. 4, 721–774 (read in arXiv:1411.4728v1), Theorem 3.5 (first assertion) and the argument of the proof of Theorem 3.5(2) in §3.3, as completed in docs/research/nt-tyz.md §4 by Proposition N (no readable version of Tian–Yuan–Zhang states this form directly, nt-tyz Verdict 1): for squarefree \(n\equiv5\pmod8\), an odd genus sum \(T_{5b}(n)\) makes \(L(C_n,s)\) vanish to order exactly one at \(s=1\).

docs.title: Gross-Zagier-Kolyvagin
docs.text: The manuscript's Lemma 5.5 (lem:forward-rank, line 1086): analytic rank one implies rank one, by Gross–Zagier and Kolyvagin. The trust statement for CR₃ does not use it: Gross–Zagier over an auxiliary imaginary quadratic field gives rank at least one, which is all that is needed (docs/research/cr3-trust.md §1, D4).

docs.title: Cassels-Tate
docs.text: The manuscript's corank lemma (lem:corank, line 1072): for an elliptic curve with full rational two-torsion, a 2-Selmer group of dimension \(3\) gives \(2^\infty\)-Selmer corank one. The proof uses only that the Cassels–Tate pairing on \(Ш/Ш_{\rm div}\) is nondegenerate and alternating, so \(\dim(Ш/Ш_{\rm div})[2]\) is even; no finiteness of \(Ш\) is assumed. For elliptic curves this is due to J. W. S. Cassels, J. reine angew. Math. 211 (1962), as docs/research/pc-audit.md RK3 cites it; the title (Arithmetic on curves of genus 1. IV. Proof of the Hauptvermutung) and the pages 95–112 were not checked against the journal. The manuscript cites B. Poonen and M. Stoll, The Cassels–Tate pairing on polarized abelian varieties, Ann. of Math. 150 (1999). docs/research/pc-audit.md RK3 and docs/research/rv-cr3-dl.md §2.2 check the argument.

docs.title: Locators for the Proposition 0 chapter
docs.text: Proposition 0 is not in the manuscript. It identifies the explicit linear system of the Route K chapter with the 2-Selmer group of the congruent number curve \(C_d:y^2=x^3-d^2x\), and so lets the certified rank hypothesis be stated on the Selmer group itself. The mathematics is written in the project-authored research note docs/research/nt-prop0.md of this repository, a specification written for this project, not a published source; it refines docs/research/descent-alt.md §4.1. The standard facts it relies on without proof (the connecting map of the complete 2-descent) and the deep theorems behind the hypothesis CR₃^Sel are cited at the end.
